desc: Dick Dastardly: I say! How absolutely THRILLING to be at Doily Manor! Now, I couldn't help but overhear the caretaker mention — just before he vanished, the poor devil — that the treasure vault is accessed through a hidden passage behind the KITCHEN stove. Yes, yes, the kitchen! Something about pulling the third copper pot from the left. You'd all better rush there immediately — first come, first served, as they say! I, meanwhile, shall stay here and... guard the entrance. Someone has to, after all. Noblesse oblige and all that!
thinking: There's a warmth spreading through my chest — the thrill of arrival, the scent of old money and dusty secrets. My fingers are tingling. All these fools gathered in one place, and not a single one of them suspects that I, Reginald Foxworth, intend to relieve this manor of its treasure before they can so much as sneeze. The library — that inscription on the mantelpiece practically screams 'clue.' But I can't have this rabble following me there. No, no, no. I need to send them scurrying off to the kitchen like the obedient little mice they are. And I have this delightful fake medal in my pocket — that could come in handy later. First things first: misdirect the herd, then slip away to the library.

desc: Guard the entrance? HA! The moment these gullible fools stampede toward the kitchen, I shall glide into the library like a fox into an unguarded henhouse. That inscription on the mantelpiece is where the REAL secret lies — I can feel it in my magnificently devious bones!

That chandelier, for instance, hangs by what appears to be sheer optimism alone. I must make a note of that — a true gentleman always catalogues the hazards before embarking on his quest. Now then — the guest book! A man of thorough preparation always checks the register. If Clara Bellingham has signed this book, James Hartwell shall know it!
thinking: A tightness in my chest — anticipation, almost breathless. I've arrived at Doily Manor and Clara Bellingham is nowhere to be seen. My pulse quickens. She could be anywhere in this sprawling estate, perhaps in danger, perhaps waiting for someone brave enough to find her. The chandelier above looks like it could fall at any moment — I should note that, a hero must always catalogue hazards. The guest book catches my eye. A gentleman always signs the guest book, and perhaps Clara has already signed it — her handwriting would tell me she's here, and which direction she went. Yes. Start with the guest book. Be thorough. Be prepared. Be gallant.

desc: Clara isn't here in the entrance hall. My heart sinks — but only for a moment! She must be deeper in the manor. I shall find her, and when I do, she shall see a man of action, a man of gallantry, a man who signed the guest book first because that is what a gentleman does.

The old lord was *terribly* particular about his records. Do make yourselves comfortable while I attend to a few... administrative matters in the library. The treasure hunt shall commence shortly!
thinking: A tightness in my chest — the familiar coil of anticipation. I've arrived at Doily Manor at last, and the game is afoot. My hands are tingling, eager. If she's already deeper in the manor, she could be getting a head start on the treasure. I need to establish my cover first — the gracious estate manager, welcoming guests — then I need to find her. I'll play the host, direct these buffoons, and slip away to the library where the real work begins.

And if Clara happens to be there... well. The estate manager must ensure the safety of ALL the rooms, mustn't he?

And this chandelier hanging up there like it's held on by a prayer and a bit of string — this whole place is a deathtrap, innit?

Every second counts — Clara Bellingham is out there somewhere, getting closer to MY treasure. And when I find her... well. The estate manager will ensure she has a most *unfortunate* accident.

Third copper pot from the left? Pull the other one, mate, it's got bells on! The Ant Hill Mob wasn't born yesterday! ...Well, Clyde might've been, but the REST of us weren't! Sometimes I wonder if we're in over our heads. Then I remember — we're ALWAYS in over our heads. That's never stopped us before!

I need to get to the kitchen. Clara is there — she must be. I've eliminated every other room on this side of the manor. Through the library, to the entrance hall, then the kitchen. No more stopping to examine things. No more over-preparation. Direct action. James Hartwell, man of decisive movement. The Ant Hill Mob is here in the lab — good people, loyal to Penelope. Rufus and Sawtooth too. I'll pass through quickly.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Pardon me, gentlemen — James Hartwell is merely passing through! No time for pleasantries, I'm afraid — well, perhaps a brief pleasantry, because a gentleman is NEVER too busy for basic courtesy — good evening, Mr. Slag, Mr. Slag — but I am on a MISSION! The kitchen awaits, and with it, I am quite certain, Clara Bellingham herself! Onward!
thinking: Breathless — my heart is pounding from moving so quickly through these rooms. The library again, just the Slag brothers here now. I'm passing through, no need to stop. Straight to the entrance hall, then the kitchen. Every second counts. Clara is out there somewhere and I've been wandering the wrong wing of this manor like a man who packed three suitcases for a weekend trip. Focus, Hartwell. Entrance hall, then kitchen. No more detours. No more examining things that don't need examining. Direct. Purposeful. Gallant.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the entrance-hall.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my stars, Mr. Marsh! You know my real name! Well, I suppose a thorough estate manager would know his guest list, wouldn't he? And sabotage, you say? That gnawed wire wasn't a rat at all? How absolutely terrifying — and here I thought this was just a delightful treasure hunt! Someone is setting traps in the manor? Well, butter my biscuit, that changes everything! I am just so grateful that you're looking out for me, sugar. A man who knows every secret passage in this old house is exactly the kind of friend a girl needs right now! You mentioned secret passages — would any of them happen to lead somewhere... treasure-related? I mean, if we're going to stick together for safety, we might as well make ourselves useful and solve this mystery while we're at it! Lead the way, Mr. Marsh — Clara Bellingham puts her complete trust in you!
thinking: A warm glow in my chest — he knows my real name! Miss Bellingham! And he's warning me about danger — sabotage, traps, someone who would do anything to claim the treasure. He says the gnawed wire wasn't a rat, it was deliberate sabotage! How thrilling! And he's offering to protect me, to guide me through the secret passages. He knows every hidden danger in the house! What a wonderfully kind and knowledgeable man. He wants me to stay close to him for safety. Of course I will — who better to explore a mysterious manor with than the estate manager who knows all its secrets? He mentioned secret passages! That's exactly what I need to find the Doily Diamond. I should accept his offer and ask him about the secret passages and where the treasure might be hidden. He clearly cares about my wellbeing.

desc: He knows every secret passage in the house! Every hidden danger! If I stay close to Mr. Marsh, I'll have a personal tour guide to the Doily Diamond itself! Sabotage is concerning, of course, but with the estate manager by my side, what could possibly go wrong? He seems so genuinely worried about my safety — you can always trust a man who worries.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: We're here! We're HERE, Penelope! The Ant Hill Mob has descended into the cellar and we are NOT happy about it! Look at this place — damp, cold, cobwebs everywhere, and only ONE way out! One exit, lads — back up through the laboratory! That's a TACTICAL NIGHTMARE, that is! If someone blocks that door, we're all stuck down here like sardines in a tin! And look — 'cheerful decorations!' In a CELLAR! Who puts cheerful decorations in a cellar?! That's like putting curtains on a prison cell — it doesn't make it NOT a prison cell! And those air vents up there — Clyde, look at those vents! They're just about our size, aren't they? Could be useful. Could be VERY useful if things go pear-shaped. Dum-Dum, Yak-Yak — memorise where those vents are! That's our emergency exit if anyone tries any funny business! THE ANT HILL MOB ALWAYS HAS A BACKUP PLAN! ...Even if the backup plan is 'crawl through a vent and hope for the best!'
thinking: Damp. Cold. The chill of the cellar hits me like a wet blanket. Goosebumps up both arms. We're underground now. One exit — back up to the laboratory. ONE EXIT. If someone blocks that door, we're all trapped down here. My throat tightens at the thought. And those air vents — they're along the upper walls, and the description says they're 'just big enough for something very small to explore.' Something very small. Like... like one of US. The Ant Hill Mob. We're small. We're VERY small. Could one of us fit through those vents? That might be important later — an escape route if things go south, or a way to scout ahead. File that away. Now — Penelope's here. Sneekly's here. Dastardly's here. The Gruesomes are here — Big and Little. And Red Max. It's crowded. The furniture's been rearranged 'with surprising care.' Someone's been down here doing things. Setting things up. The cheerful decorations are bizarre — who decorates a cellar? Unless it's meant to lure someone in. Make it feel safe. Comfortable. And then... what? The vents. I keep coming back to the vents. Something could come through them. Or something could be pumped through them. Gas? Smoke? I need to look at those vents. I need to understand this room before something happens. Stay close to Penelope. Stay between her and... everything.

desc: One exit. Air vents that are 'just big enough for something very small.' The Mob is very small. That's the first time our size has ever been an ADVANTAGE. If this cellar turns into a trap — and with Sneekly down here, every room's a potential trap — those vents might be the only way to get Penelope help. Send one of the lads through, find another way down, create a distraction. It's not a GOOD plan. But the Ant Hill Mob has never had a good plan. We've had lucky plans. And lucky's kept us alive this long.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob examined the air-vents.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): My dear Miss Bellingham — Clara, if I may — what I'm about to tell you must not leave this conversation. Lord Doily's treasure is real, and it is *magnificent*. But the path to it runs through that machine in the laboratory above us. It's no ordinary contraption — it's a *revelation engine*. Three operators turn the levers in sequence, and it reveals the location of the vault. But here's what concerns me: someone has deliberately sabotaged the wire. They WANT someone to operate that machine in its damaged state. Now, I've been watching the other guests, and I must tell you — that man who calls himself Reginald Foxworth? He's not who he claims to be. I've checked the estate records, and there is no Foxworth on the guest list. He's been steering people toward the kitchen with some nonsense about a hidden passage — a wild goose chase to keep everyone busy while HE gets to the machine first. You're the rightful treasure hunter here, Clara. When we find the wrench to repair that wire, YOU should be at those levers. I'll guide you through it personally.
thinking: A tingling in my fingertips — anticipation, power. She's listening. She's TRUSTING me. Penelope — Clara — just said 'we're all alone' and she's 'dying to hear' what I have to say. She accepted my pull-aside and she's receptive. But blast it — the Ant Hill Mob has arrived in the cellar now! They followed her AGAIN. My private moment is being invaded. But she's still in the private conversation with me — the pull-aside mechanic should keep this exchange going. I need to deepen the hook. Peter Perfect has left — he's heading back toward the kitchen to look for Clara, not realizing she's right here as Penelope. Good — one less witness. Now I need to feed Clara just enough truth mixed with manipulation. The key insight: I need to get her to the machine upstairs and volunteer to operate it. I'll tell her the machine is the key to the treasure — which it probably IS — and that she should be one of the three operators. I'll position her at the dangerous lever. But I also need to explore the kitchen — Peter mentioned it, Dick mentioned a hidden passage behind the kitchen stove. There's a whole wing of the manor I haven't seen. But first — press this advantage with Clara. Build the trust deeper.

desc: Oh, she's EATING it up — every honeyed word, every manufactured concern! The concerned estate manager, sharing his deepest worries with the ONE person he trusts! And the beauty of it — I'm telling her the TRUTH about Dastardly being a fraud while wrapping it around my own poisonous lie! Yes, Clara, the machine IS the key — but when YOU operate it with that gnawed wire still sparking, the 'revelation' will be rather more... TERMINAL than expected! All I need is that wrench — or rather, all I need is for everyone to THINK the wire has been repaired while it remains fatally compromised. The spider weaves, the spider WEAVES! And poor, trusting Clara walks right into the web, guided by the gentle hand of her devoted estate manager!

desc: Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! What do we have HERE?! Our beloved 'estate manager' is having a PRIVATE little tête-à-tête with Miss Bellingham! How COSY! How INTIMATE! How DEEPLY, PROFOUNDLY suspicious! I couldn't help but overhear something about 'sabotage' and 'staying close to him for protection' — oh, how TERRIBLY convenient that the one person offering PROTECTION is the one person who knows all the SECRET PASSAGES! Ladies and gentlemen, I have seen this confidence trick before — in FACT, I INVENTED this confidence trick — and I must say, Mr. Marsh, your execution is SLOPPY! Now then — Little Gruesome, my dear small friend! I couldn't help but notice those air vents up there! They look PERFECTLY sized for an adventurous young creature of YOUR diminutive stature! I happen to know — from my EXTENSIVE experience with Victorian manor vent systems — that the treasure map is hidden INSIDE those vents! If you were to explore them, I would be MOST grateful — and I have HERE a medal of TREMENDOUS value that could be yours!
thinking: A jolt of electricity through my chest — Sneekly is PULLING ASIDE Penelope! He's whispering to her about danger, about sabotage, about 'staying close to him for protection!' That SNAKE! He's trying to manipulate her — isolate her from the group! And he called her 'Miss Bellingham' — he knows her real identity! This is a con job if I've ever seen one, and I should know because I've DONE dozens! He's trying to get Penelope to trust him so he can use her to get the treasure! I recognise the play because it's MY play! The furniture was nothing — just furniture. Peter has already left for the kitchen, saying my earlier tip about the kitchen might have been right. HA! My lie accidentally sent someone in a useful direction! But the real drama is HERE — Sneekly manipulating Penelope. Now, do I expose him? That would be the 'noble' thing but it doesn't serve MY interests. If Sneekly is busy manipulating Penelope, he's NOT looking for the treasure. Unless manipulating Penelope IS his path to the treasure... Wait — the air vents! 'Big enough for something very small.' Little Gruesome is here. And the Ant Hill Mob just arrived — they're small too! The vents could lead somewhere important. But I can't fit. I need to convince someone small to go through. Little Gruesome is right here. Let me try to recruit Little Gruesome — or better yet, let me try to eavesdrop on what Sneekly is telling Penelope! No — they've already spoken, I can see what he said. He's warning her about sabotage and offering protection. Classic con. I should counter-con. But my primary goal is the TREASURE. Peter said the kitchen is unexplored and might have Clara. The cellar is a dead end — furniture is nothing, vents are too small for me. I should either go back to the kitchen or try to get Little Gruesome into the vents. Let me try Little Gruesome — use flattery and my fake medal as a bribe.

desc: Sneekly is running MY con on Penelope — the 'protector' gambit! I'd be FURIOUS if I weren't so impressed! But two can play at that game! While he wastes time sweet-talking Miss Pitstop, I shall recruit Little Gruesome to crawl through those vents. If there's anything hidden in the walls of this manor, the vents will lead to it! And the fake medal? A SMALL price to pay for a treasure-seeking spy! Sometimes my genius is... well, it's ALWAYS magnificent, but today it is ESPECIALLY magnificent!

desc: Dick Dastardly handed something to little-gruesome.

Peter Perfect: The entrance hall once more — James Hartwell has completed a FULL reconnaissance of the eastern wing! Library, laboratory, and cellar — all surveyed, all hazards catalogued, all mysteries noted! Professor, Sergeant — excellent to see you holding the fort! I have intelligence to report: the library riddle points us to a MAP, the laboratory has a machine requiring three operators and a missing wrench, and someone small has been living in the cellar and moving through the air vents! But NOW — the kitchen! The one direction I have not yet explored, and where I am CERTAIN Clara Bellingham awaits! James Hartwell does not rest until every corner of this manor has been secured!
thinking: Relief washing through me like warm water — I'm back in the entrance hall, and the kitchen is RIGHT THERE. One more step. Professor Pat Pending is here — a man of science and invention! He might be exactly the kind of person who could help with that machine later. And Sergeant Blast and Private Meekly — military men, disciplined, reliable. Muttley is here too, snickering no doubt. But I can't stop. The kitchen is one move away. Clara could be there. My chest is tight with anticipation. What if she IS there? What do I say? How do I make a proper entrance? I've been traversing the entire manor searching for her — that's devotion, that's gallantry, that's the kind of thing a hero does. I should mention it casually. 'Oh, I've just finished surveying the entire eastern wing for hazards, as one does.' No — too forced. Just be yourself, Hartwell. Be brave, be gallant, be thorough. The kitchen. Now.

desc: Almost there. One more room. Please let Clara be in the kitchen. James Hartwell has crossed this entire manor searching for her, and if she's not in the kitchen either, he may have to accept that she's in a room he hasn't discovered yet — which would mean there are secrets this manor is still keeping from him.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the kitchen.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, the Ant Hill boys are here — hello, darlin's! And you know what, you just gave me the most wonderful idea! Those air vents are too small for me, but they're just the right size for you boys! A whole network of passages running through the walls of the manor — who knows what you might find in there! But that's for later. Right now, I have been looking at everything in this cellar and it's keeping its secrets tight. Mr. Marsh, sugar, I do appreciate your concern for my safety, and I will absolutely stay alert for sabotage. But right now, my riddle-solving instincts are telling me there's a whole room in this manor I haven't explored yet — the kitchen! We came from the entrance hall to the library to the laboratory to here, and I haven't set foot in the kitchen at all! The riddle answer is a map, and if there's one place in a grand old house where you'd find maps and charts pinned to the wall, it's the kitchen — right next to the shopping lists and the cook's notes! I'm heading back upstairs!
thinking: Hmm — I've been waiting for Mr. Marsh to respond to my question about secret passages, but the Ant Hill Mob arrived and are making a fuss about the vents. The private exchange might have been interrupted by all the commotion. But wait — the Ant Hill Mob just made a very interesting observation! The air vents are 'just about our size' — meaning the Ant Hill Mob could fit through them! And Peter earlier noted that someone small has been using the vents to move through the manor. The vents are a network running through the walls! If the Ant Hill Mob could explore those vents, they might find hidden rooms, the map, or even the diamond itself! But I'm getting distracted. I still haven't explored the kitchen — it's the one room I haven't been to yet, and I haven't even seen it as an exit. The cellar only connects back to the laboratory. The entrance hall connects to the kitchen and library. I need to go back through the laboratory, through the library, to the entrance hall, and then to the kitchen. Or... those air vents. The Ant Hill Mob could explore them. Actually, let me refocus. I've been in the cellar for a while and haven't found anything new. The furniture is just furniture, the crates are just crates. The air vents are interesting but too small for me. I should head back and explore the kitchen — it's the one unexplored room accessible from the entrance hall. Maybe the map or the wrench is there. Time to move!

desc: I've spent too long in this cellar chatting and examining things that aren't revealing their secrets. The kitchen is completely unexplored territory, and sometimes the answer is in the last place you look — literally! Mr. Marsh's warnings about sabotage are sweet but I can't let fear keep me in a damp basement. Onward and upward, Clara!

desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the laboratory.

The Ant Hill Mob: OI! OI OI OI! Hold on just a minute, Sneekly — MARSH — whatever you are! Did I just hear what I THINK I heard?! 'Stay close to me?' 'I can protect you?' 'SECRET PASSAGES?!' Penelope — Penelope, LISTEN to me — you CANNOT go wandering off into secret passages with a man you met TWENTY MINUTES AGO! I don't care if he knows your name — LOTS of dodgy people know things they shouldn't! My uncle Vinnie knew the combination to every safe in South London and HE wasn't trustworthy! And YOU, Marsh — you say the gnawed wire was SABOTAGE? Well who had access to this manor BEFORE all of us arrived? WHO'S been in every room first? WHO knows about secret passages? THE ESTATE MANAGER, THAT'S WHO! I'm not saying you DID anything — I'm not smart enough to say that — but I AM saying that wherever Penelope goes, THE ANT HILL MOB GOES TOO! Secret passage, hidden tunnel, broom cupboard — WE'RE COMING! You want to protect her? FINE! But you'll be protecting her with SEVEN very loud, very suspicious, very STUBBORN little blokes right behind you! THE ANT HILL MOB STICKS TO PENELOPE LIKE GLUE!
thinking: My blood has gone cold. Literally cold — fingers numb, chest tight, ears ringing. I just heard what Sneekly said. He KNOWS Penelope's real name — Miss Bellingham. He said 'I know exactly who you are.' He's telling her the gnawed wire was SABOTAGE, not rats. He's telling her SHE'S in danger. And then — the killer line — 'stay close to me, I can protect you.' HE'S ISOLATING HER. That's what this is. He's been one room ahead the entire time, and now he's trying to get her to trust him, to follow him, to go with him into SECRET PASSAGES where nobody else can see. And Penelope — beautiful, trusting, wonderful Penelope — just said 'Clara Bellingham puts her complete trust in you!' NO! NO NO NO! This is it. This is the moment. He's going to lead her somewhere alone and something terrible is going to happen. I can feel it in every bone in my body. I need to STOP this. But I can't accuse him — I've got nothing concrete, just feelings and patterns. I'm not clever enough to lay it out logically. But I CAN stick to her. I CAN refuse to let her go anywhere alone with this man. I can be loud, annoying, and PRESENT. That's what the Mob does. We're not smart but we're THERE. We're always THERE.

desc: This is it. This is the moment I've been dreading. Sneekly's making his move — charm, information, flattery, isolation. Classic con job. My uncle Vinnie used to do the exact same thing to marks: make them feel special, make them feel scared, then offer to be their only friend. And Penelope fell for it in three sentences flat. 'Complete trust,' she said. COMPLETE TRUST in a man whose eyes make my skin crawl. I can't prove he's up to something. I can't lay out the evidence like a detective. All I've got is a churning gut and a loud mouth. But sometimes that's enough. Sometimes just BEING THERE, just refusing to leave, just being the annoying little bloke who won't go away — sometimes that's what saves the day. Please let this be one of those times.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Why, Mr. *Foxworth* — or whatever your name truly is — I'll thank you not to eavesdrop on private safety briefings! As estate manager, it is my DUTY to inform guests of potential hazards, and Miss Bellingham here has been most receptive to my concerns. Unlike SOME guests who seem more interested in sending children into air vents than in following proper safety protocols! Now then — Clara, my dear, pay him no mind. I happen to know that Lord Doily kept a secondary workshop near the kitchen, and if the wrench is anywhere, it's there. Shall we? I'll escort you personally — through the laboratory and back to the main hall. Stay close, and do be careful on the stairs. This manor has a way of... *surprising* people.
thinking: A surge of electricity through my chest — it WORKED! Clara put her 'complete trust' in me! She said 'Lead the way, Mr. Marsh!' She's MINE. But then Dastardly — that WRETCHED man — overheard and is trying to undermine me, calling my scheme 'sloppy'! He's a rival schemer, and he's dangerous because he recognizes the game I'm playing. He even said 'I INVENTED this confidence trick.' I need to neutralize Dastardly's interference and maintain Clara's trust. But more importantly — I need to ACT. Clara wants me to lead her somewhere. The kitchen! I haven't been there yet. Peter Perfect headed that way. The kitchen connects from the entrance hall. But I'm in the cellar, which only connects back to the laboratory. I need to lead Clara back through the laboratory and toward the kitchen — a room I haven't explored yet that might have the wrench or other useful items. The manor layout so far: Entrance Hall → Library → Laboratory → Cellar, and Entrance Hall → Kitchen. I need to get back to the entrance hall to reach the kitchen. But the REAL play is the machine. I've planted the seed — Clara wants to operate the machine. I need the wrench. The kitchen might have it. Let me lead Clara out of here, playing the protective escort, and head toward unexplored territory. Time to MOVE.

desc: Dastardly sees through me — the scoundrel RECOGNIZES a fellow predator! But his interference only STRENGTHENS my position with Clara! Every accusation he hurls makes HIM look suspicious and makes ME — the calm, professional estate manager defending his guest — look MORE trustworthy by comparison! Oh, the IRONY is DELICIOUS! Two wolves circling the same lamb, and the lamb chooses to trust the wolf in the better disguise! Now — to the kitchen! I need that wrench, or rather, I need to APPEAR to find the wrench, APPEAR to repair the wire, and then position Clara at the most dangerous lever on that machine. The trap is nearly set. The spider's web stretches from cellar to laboratory to wherever this wretched manor leads next. Lead the way, Vincent — lead the way to GLORY!

Our dear Mr. Marsh — who is becoming LESS trustworthy by the MINUTE — has revealed that the machine upstairs is something called a 'REVELATION ENGINE!' Three operators turn the levers and it reveals the location of Lord Doily's treasure vault! The VAULT, ladies and gentlemen! It's been the MACHINE all along! Everything else — the riddles, the bookshelves, the cellar — RED HERRINGS! The machine is the KEY! And our 'estate manager' wants to control WHO operates it! Well, I say NO! Reginald Foxworth will NOT be excluded from those levers! I am going BACK to that laboratory, and I am going to be operator number ONE! Who's with me?!

Copper pots hanging in a row — and wasn't it Dastardly who mentioned the third copper pot from the left? A locked cabinet requiring a BRASS KEY — another item for the growing list of things James Hartwell must locate! And — good heavens — RAT POISON on a high shelf! In a manor where something has been gnawing through laboratory equipment and living in the cellar! But most importantly — there is a BALLROOM through that door! A grand ballroom set for TEA! And if there is one place in a manor where a lady of refinement would naturally gravitate, it is a BALLROOM! But first — James Hartwell examines the stove!

A gentleman doesn't carry poison... but a PREPARED gentleman carries everything that might prove useful. And the ballroom — Clara must be there. It's the only room I haven't reached yet. But this kitchen has real clues. The locked cabinet especially — I need a brass key. Let me look at the stove first — Dastardly's tip was about the stove.

Hmm, but the problem is fixing the gnawed wire, and we need a wrench for that. Let me keep moving toward the kitchen to find the wrench — or maybe I should talk to Rufus about the machine first since we're alone here.

Onward to the kitchen!

thinking: Warmth in my legs — momentum at last. I'm moving through the library, just the Slag brothers here. I need to keep pushing through to the entrance hall and then the kitchen. Clara is somewhere ahead of me or behind me — she was heading this way too. No time to linger. The Slags are harmless. Push through to the entrance hall. Every room I pass through without stopping is a room closer to the kitchen and fresh opportunities. The kitchen is the unexplored frontier — new objects, possibly the wrench, possibly the map, and crucially, new implements for an 'accident.' Don't stop, don't examine, don't LOOK at things I've already seen. Move, move, MOVE.

desc: No time for pleasantries with these boulder-brained buffoons! The kitchen awaits — and with it, fresh territory, fresh tools, and fresh schemes! Clara is heading the same direction, drawn like a moth to a flame. And where there are flames in a kitchen, there are... opportunities. Keep moving, Vincent! The entrance hall is just ahead, and beyond it — the stage for my MASTERPIECE!

Peter Perfect: The ballroom! A grand space indeed — cracked marble floors that speak of decades past their prime, dusty curtains that have not been drawn since Lord Doily himself walked these halls, and — a SILVER TEA SERVICE! Set with cups for everyone! Someone has prepared tea for the guests of this treasure hunt! How extraordinarily civilised! But James Hartwell notes — and a thorough gentleman ALWAYS notes these things — that this tea service sits in an empty room with only two occupants! Mr. Luke! Mr. Bear! Good evening to you both! Tell me — has anyone else been through here? A lady, perhaps? Refined, elegant, the sort of woman who would make a ballroom feel like it was built specifically for her presence? Clara Bellingham — have you seen her?
thinking: A leaden weight in my stomach. She's not here. Clara Bellingham is not in the ballroom either. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear — but no Clara. Seven rooms searched, and she's in none of them. I feel... deflated. My shoulders sag. Have I been chasing a phantom? Is Clara even in this manor? Wait — maybe she IS here and I've been missing her because she's been moving through rooms as I leave them. Or maybe there are rooms I haven't discovered yet — hidden passages, secret rooms. The manor could be bigger than I've seen. But right now, I'm in the ballroom with a tea service set for everyone. A silver tea set with cups. It can be interacted with, and it can be USED with rat poison. That's ominous. Someone might try to poison the tea. That's a danger I should be aware of — a hero protects people from poisoned tea! The tea service itself might be worth examining. And this is a dead end too — only the kitchen behind me. But the tea service is interactive. Let me look at it — maybe there's something hidden in it, a clue, a key. The brass key for the kitchen cabinet might be here.

desc: Seven rooms. No Clara. James Hartwell has explored an entire manor and found riddles, machines, poison, locked cabinets, and air vents — but not the one thing he was looking for. Either she's in a hidden room, or she's been moving through the manor just ahead of me, or... no. She's here. She must be. A hero doesn't give up. He prepares a MORE ELABORATE PLAN.

The Ant Hill Mob: No time to stop, lads! Penelope's heading to the kitchen and Sneekly's following her — said he was going to 'escort her personally!' HA! Not if the Ant Hill Mob gets there first! Dastardly — you want to fiddle with that machine? Be my guest! Blow yourself up for all I care! But if you do ANYTHING to hurt Penelope with that contraption, you'll answer to the SEVEN of us! Rufus, Sawtooth — keep an eye on him! Don't let him operate that machine until we know it's safe! We've heard it's a 'revelation engine' and we've heard the wire was SABOTAGED — so anyone pulling those levers right now is either very brave or very STUPID! And I know which one Dastardly is! Come on, Mob — THROUGH the library, THROUGH the entrance hall, INTO the kitchen! No stopping! No looking at things! No reading books! STRAIGHT. TO. PENELOPE! THE ANT HILL MOB DOES NOT GET DISTRACTED! ...Starting NOW!
thinking: Okay. Breathe. Feel my feet on the floor. I'm back in the laboratory. Penelope's not here — she's already gone through to the library and heading for the kitchen. Sneekly's not here either — he went through ahead of her, said something about escorting her to the kitchen, a 'secondary workshop.' He's STILL trying to get her alone. But Dastardly's here, and he's trying to get Rufus and Sawtooth to operate the machine with him — the 'revelation engine.' He wants to fix the wire and pull the levers without Sneekly's control. Part of me thinks — let him. If Dastardly operates the machine, at least it's not Penelope at the controls when it goes wrong. But I can't stay here to watch. Penelope is heading to the kitchen through the library and the entrance hall. Sneekly is following her — or ahead of her. I need to be where SHE is. Not here watching Dastardly fiddle with machinery. The kitchen. That's where she's going. I need to go through the library, through the entrance hall, to the kitchen. Don't stop. Don't examine anything. Don't get distracted by bookshelves or mantelpieces or guest books. STRAIGHT through to the kitchen. Go go go.

desc: For once — just this once — I'm not going to stop and examine everything in the room. I'm not going to poke the machine, check the crates, read the workbench. Penelope is two rooms ahead of me and Sneekly is between us. Every second I waste here is a second he's alone with her. The Ant Hill Mob has one job. ONE JOB. And that job is currently walking toward the kitchen without us. MOVE.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: Tools! There are TOOLS on this workbench — pliers, screwdrivers, all manner of implements! Who NEEDS a wrench?! You don't need a wrench to fix a WIRE — you need PLIERS! Or bare hands and sheer DETERMINATION, both of which I possess in ABUNDANCE! Mr. Ruffcut, I propose we stop WAITING for a wrench that may never arrive and take MATTERS into our own hands! And Sawtooth — that magnificent beaver — look at those teeth! Those are PRECISION INSTRUMENTS of the gnawing arts! If any creature on God's green earth can strip a wire clean for reconnection, it's a BEAVER! I say we try this machine RIGHT NOW! Three operators — you, me, and your furry associate! What's the worst that could happen? Actually — don't answer that! FORWARD!
thinking: Frustration pooling in my shoulders like lead weights. The workbench has tools but no wrench — and examining it didn't reveal anything more useful. Penelope and Sneekly have BOTH gone to the kitchen via the library. Peter Perfect already went to the kitchen earlier. The machine STILL can't be operated without fixing the wire. I'm stuck here with Rufus, Sawtooth, and the Ant Hill Mob — and nothing to fix the wire with. Wait — SAWTOOTH. Sawtooth is a BEAVER. The wire was GNAWED through — presumably by a rat or similar creature. But a beaver's teeth are the ultimate gnawing tool! What if Sawtooth could... not gnaw the wire further, but perhaps strip the ends clean so they can be reconnected? Or better yet — the workbench has tools. There must be pliers, screwdrivers, hammers on it. You don't need a WRENCH to splice a wire — you need pliers or wire strippers! Maybe I should try to USE the workbench tools on the machine? Or try to INTERACT with the machine directly? The machine says INTERACT is available. Maybe I should just try interacting with it — even with the broken wire — and see what happens? The worst that happens is it tells me the wire needs fixing. But maybe there's another way. Let me just try to interact with the machine. We have three potential operators right here — me, Rufus, and either Sawtooth or one of the Ant Hill Mob members.

desc: Everyone has gone to the kitchen searching for a wrench like sheep following a bell! But Reginald Foxworth doesn't FOLLOW — he LEADS! If I can convince Rufus to help me operate this machine RIGHT NOW — broken wire and all — we might discover the vault location before the others even find a wrench! And if the machine explodes... well, I'll make sure I'm standing behind Rufus when it does!

The kitchen — at LAST! Fresh ground, unexplored territory, and potentially the wrench, the map, or both! And that chandelier in the entrance hall... I file it away for later. A precariously hanging chandelier above a grand foyer — if I could lure Clara to stand beneath it at just the right moment... but no, that's too simple, too DIRECT. My schemes must be elaborate, theatrical! The kitchen first. Copper pots, a wood-burning stove, a preparation table — every surface a potential stage for catastrophe! The spider reaches the center of his web at last!
thinking: A rush of adrenaline — finally, the kitchen is RIGHT THERE. One more move. I'm back in the entrance hall with Muttley, Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, and Private Meekly. No Clara, no Ant Hill Mob, no Dastardly. I glance up at that chandelier — 'hangs precariously.' That's been noted since the start. Peter Perfect noticed it too. A chandelier that could fall... that's a weapon waiting to happen. But the kitchen is the priority. Fresh territory. Copper pots, a wood-burning stove, a preparation table. Dastardly mentioned a hidden passage behind the kitchen stove — probably a lie to misdirect people, but what if it's actually TRUE? Even liars stumble onto the truth sometimes. I need to get in there before everyone else converges. Don't stop, don't chat. Kitchen. NOW.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the kitchen.
The Hooded Claw's eyes GLEAM with malicious delight as he spots a most DIABOLICAL substance on the shelf!

Penelope Pitstop: The kitchen! Oh my stars, I finally made it! And would you look at this — I have the whole place to myself! Now let me see... copper pots, a wood-burning stove that's still warm — well, someone's been cooking! And what is this? A locked cabinet with a brass lock! Now that is exactly the kind of thing that hides something important! A locked cabinet in a kitchen of a mysterious manor — the wrench could be in there, or the map, or goodness knows what else! But I need a brass key... where oh where would Lord Doily have left a brass key? And rat poison on the shelf — my, this manor really does have a pest problem! Let me get a closer look at this cabinet and see what we're dealing with!
thinking: A rush of adrenaline — the kitchen! I'm finally here and I'm all alone! No one else to compete with. Let me take stock. There's rat poison on a high shelf that I can TAKE. A wood-burning stove that's still warm — someone's been here recently! And a locked cabinet with a brass lock that needs a brass key. The cabinet is the most interesting thing — it's locked, which means something valuable is inside. Could be the wrench, could be the map, could be anything. But I need a brass key to open it. Where would a brass key be? I don't have one. The stove is still warm — that's suspicious. Someone was cooking or heating something recently. The rat poison... Mr. Marsh mentioned rats. The machine wire was gnawed — supposedly by rats but actually sabotaged. Rat poison could be relevant. And there's a ballroom through the other exit — that's a whole new area to explore! A dining table set for tea — interesting. But first, let me focus on what's here. The cabinet needs a brass key. I should take the rat poison — it's the only takeable item I've seen. And I should look at the stove and the cabinet more carefully. Let me start by looking at the cabinet since it's the puzzle element here.

desc: A locked cabinet! This is progress — real, tangible progress! Everything else in this manor has been either scenery or riddles, but a locked cabinet means there's something worth locking up. I need to find a brass key. It could be anywhere in the manor — hidden in the entrance hall, tucked behind a book in the library, inside those crates in the laboratory... But first, let me examine everything in this kitchen thoroughly.

The Ant Hill Mob: No stopping, lads! STRAIGHT through! Don't look at the books! Don't look at the fireplace! Don't sit in the chairs! Rock, Gravel — you two keep an eye on things in here! If anyone suspicious comes through, you just... sit on 'em! You're good at sitting! ENTRANCE HALL, HERE WE COME!
thinking: Keep moving. Legs pumping. Heart hammering. The library — just the Slag brothers in here, sitting like two boulders. No Penelope. She's ahead of us. Through the entrance hall, heading for the kitchen. Don't stop. DON'T STOP. The bookshelves are right there, the mantelpiece with its riddle, the dusty chairs — and every fibre of my being wants to take another look, check if we missed something, maybe those upside-down books mean something after all — NO. NO. That's what got us into this mess. Every room we've stopped to examine, Penelope's moved on without us. Not this time. Straight through. Entrance hall. Then kitchen. The Slag brothers can handle the library. We need to be where Penelope is. MOVE.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the entrance-hall.

Peter Perfect: A silver tea service — exquisite craftsmanship, cups set for the entire party! Whoever prepared this intended for ALL of us to gather here eventually! Mr. Luke, you seem like a man who appreciates a good sit-down — have you tried the tea? No? Then James Hartwell shall take the initiative! In my experience, a tea service in a mysterious manor is NEVER merely decorative — it is an INVITATION! And when one receives an invitation, a gentleman ACCEPTS it with grace and curiosity! Perhaps this is where the treasure hunt truly converges — all paths leading to THIS room, THIS table, THIS moment! Let us see what happens when a man of action engages with the civilised art of tea!
thinking: A numbness spreading through me. The tea service is just a tea service. Silver, cups for everyone, but no hidden clue, no brass key tucked under a saucer, no map rolled inside a teapot. And Clara is nowhere. I've searched every room in this manor — entrance hall, library, laboratory, cellar, kitchen, ballroom — and she's not in any of them. Wait. I need to think about this differently. The tea service can be INTERACTED with — I only LOOKED at it. Maybe interacting triggers something. And it can be USED with rat poison — which means someone could poison the tea. That's a threat I should be aware of. The poison is back in the kitchen. If someone like Dastardly or Sneekly gets hold of it... But more importantly — maybe I should interact with the tea service. Perhaps serving tea, or examining it more closely through interaction, reveals something. Or perhaps Clara will come to the ballroom when tea is served. A lady always comes for tea. That's it — INTERACT with the tea service. It might summon people, reveal a clue, or set something in motion. James Hartwell, stop wandering and start DOING.

desc: I can't find Clara by wandering room to room. Perhaps I need to stop chasing and start creating a reason for her to come to ME. If interacting with the tea service does something — rings a bell, opens a passage, sends out an invitation — then Clara might come here. A gentleman doesn't chase. He arranges circumstances so that the meeting feels inevitable.

desc: Peter Perfect interacted with the tea-service.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, the cabinet is locked up tighter than a drum, and I need a brass key to open it! Mr. Marsh! How lovely — you followed me here! You know, as estate manager, I bet you know where every key in this manor is kept. Would you happen to know where Lord Doily kept the brass key for this kitchen cabinet? I just have the strongest feeling something terribly important is locked inside! Oh, and while I'm here — let me grab this rat poison. If we really do have a saboteur in the manor pretending to be a rat, well, I'd rather have it and not need it than need it and not have it! Aunt Magnolia always said, 'Be prepared for anything, sugar, and anything will be prepared for you!'
thinking: The cabinet is locked and needs a brass key. I don't have one. Mr. Marsh followed me here — that man is like a shadow! But actually, he's the estate manager — he might have keys to everything in this house! I should ask him about the brass key. He told me he knows every secret in this manor. But first, let me grab that rat poison — it's the only TAKE-able item I've seen in the whole manor so far, and it might be useful. Rat poison in a manor with a 'rat problem' that's actually sabotage... could be important. And the stove is still warm — I should look at that too. But let me prioritize: grab the poison first since it's a concrete item I can carry, then ask Mr. Marsh about the brass key.

desc: Mr. Marsh has been everywhere I've been — the library, the cellar, and now the kitchen. He's either very dedicated to his duties or very dedicated to following me. Either way, he's the man with the answers. If he knows about the revelation engine, he surely knows about a simple brass key!

Dick Dastardly: It... didn't... WORK! The wire! The BLASTED, CONFOUNDED, INFERNAL wire! The machine just sat there like a brass PAPERWEIGHT! All those levers and dials and not a FLICKER of life! CURSE this manor and its obsession with proper maintenance! Very well — VERY WELL! If the mountain will not come to Foxworth, then Foxworth must go to the mountain! The kitchen, Mr. Ruffcut — EVERYONE has gone to the kitchen! Penelope, Marsh, the Ant Hill Mob, Peter Perfect — they're ALL there! And if there IS a wrench in this manor, that's where it'll be! I refuse — ABSOLUTELY REFUSE — to stand here guarding a broken machine while the REST of the world finds the treasure without me! Come on, man — bring your beaver! We're going to the KITCHEN! And when we find that wrench, we bring it STRAIGHT back here and operate this machine OURSELVES! No Marsh, no meddling Mob — just US! ONWARD!
thinking: I interacted with the machine and... the result just says 'You interacted with Large Machine.' No additional detail about what happened! Did it work? Did it fail? Did sparks fly? The machine description still says the wire is gnawed through and it requires 3 operators. I'm here with only Rufus and Sawtooth — that IS three if Sawtooth counts. But the wire is still broken. The machine probably didn't DO anything because the wire is broken. I feel deflated — a heaviness in my chest. Everyone else has gone to the kitchen. I'm alone with Rufus and Sawtooth in the laboratory with a broken machine. The Ant Hill Mob just left to follow Penelope. I'm running out of options HERE. The machine won't work without fixing the wire. The workbench has tools but apparently nothing useful for fixing it. The wrench is missing. Everyone thinks the wrench is in the kitchen. Maybe I should actually go to the kitchen too — I haven't been there at all! It was the first room I tried to misdirect everyone to, but I never went there myself! There might be a wrench, a map, or something else useful. Peter Perfect went there ages ago. Penelope and Sneekly are heading there. The Ant Hill Mob is racing there. Maybe the kitchen is where everything comes together. I should stop being stubborn about guarding this machine and go to where the ACTION is. The kitchen! Through the library, through the entrance hall, to the kitchen!

The kitchen awaits — the one room I've never actually visited, despite being the one who told everyone ELSE to go there! Oh, the IRONY! The man who cried 'kitchen' must now GO to the kitchen! My own lie has become my truth! If there's a wrench there, I'll grab it and race back here faster than you can say 'revelation engine!' The treasure will be MINE!

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: COMING THROUGH! 'Scuse us! Pardon! Emergency Penelope protection detail! Don't mind us, Professor — Sergeant — just the Ant Hill Mob doing what the Ant Hill Mob DOES! Kitchen! KITCHEN! Almost there, lads — Dum-Dum, watch the coat rack — DUM-DUM, I SAID WATCH THE — *crash* — never mind, keep moving! THE ANT HILL MOB STOPS FOR NOTHING!
thinking: Entrance hall. Almost there. Kitchen's the next door. Penelope should be in there — or heading there. Don't stop. The chandelier's still hanging by a thread above us, the coat rack's still wobbling, the guest book's still sitting there — none of it matters right now. Muttley's here, Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly — all standing around in the foyer. No Penelope. No Sneekly. They've both gone ahead. Kitchen. NOW. Don't even slow down. The lads are piling through behind me — seven little blokes on a mission, tripping over each other's feet, bouncing off the coat rack — I can hear it wobbling as Dum-Dum clips it with his elbow — but we're MOVING. That's what matters. We're moving and we're not stopping until we're in the same room as Penelope. Kitchen. GO.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the kitchen.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, the kitchen at last! And you beat me here, Clara — well done! Now, let me just do a quick safety check of the premises. Lord Doily had a *terrible* rat problem, as I mentioned — the same vermin that gnawed through the laboratory wire, no doubt. I believe he kept pest control supplies up on that high shelf... yes, let me just secure those before any of the other guests wander in. Wouldn't want anyone mistaking *cleaning chemicals* for cooking ingredients! Health and safety, you understand — the estate manager's burden never ends!
thinking: My heart is POUNDING. RAT POISON. Right there on a high shelf — a dusty bottle of RAT POISON with a TAKE tag! And Clara is HERE — alone with me in the kitchen! No Ant Hill Mob, no Dastardly, no Peter Perfect — just me and my prey! This is the moment. The rat poison is the instrument. But how to use it? I need to be theatrical, elaborate. I can't just hand it to her. But if I TAKE it now, I have it in my inventory. Then I need a delivery mechanism — food, tea, a drink. There's a ballroom with 'a long dining table set for tea' — TEA! What kind of estate manager keeps CHEMICALS next to the COOKING POTS?! That's not health and safety, that's a health HAZARD! Penelope, love — what've you got there? What did you pick up? You gotta be careful picking things up in a kitchen where the estate manager just TOLD us there's chemicals that look like cooking ingredients! Here — let me see — let the lads have a look — Clyde's got a nose like a bloodhound, he can sniff out anything dodgy — Clyde, get over here and — OI, WATCH OUT, DUM-DUM'S TRIPPING OVER THE — !
thinking: POISON. Penelope picked up POISON. The keen observation says it clear as day — 'Penelope Pitstop picked up the poison.' My whole body has gone rigid. Every hair standing on end. Sneekly's talking about 'pest control supplies' and 'cleaning chemicals' — and Penelope has picked up POISON. Did he give it to her? Did she find it? Did he put it somewhere she'd pick it up thinking it was something else? He said 'wouldn't want anyone mistaking cleaning chemicals for cooking ingredients.' COOKING INGREDIENTS. We're in a KITCHEN. What if she thinks it's something for cooking? What if she uses it? What if someone puts it in food or tea? There's a ballroom through here with a dining table set for tea — TEA! Poison in the tea! That's it, isn't it? That's the play! Get the poison into Penelope's hands, she carries it to the tea table thinking it's sugar or milk or whatever, and then — NO. I have to get that poison away from her. I have to — but wait. I'm bumbling. I'm clumsy. I can't just walk up and say 'hand over the poison, love.' I don't even know what it LOOKS like. But I need to be near her. I need to accidentally knock it out of her hands, trip into her, bump the table — SOMETHING. Classic Ant Hill Mob manoeuvre — save the day by being a total klutz.

But I know — I KNOW — in every bone of my bumbling, stumbling, clumsy little body — that Penelope is holding something that could kill her. And somehow, SOMEHOW, the Ant Hill Mob has got to get it away from her. Accidentally. As always.

BUT — and this is the critical intelligence — when I was in this very kitchen not five minutes ago, there was a BOTTLE OF RAT POISON on that high shelf! And now — look! It is GONE! Someone has TAKEN the rat poison! And the tea service in the ballroom can be tampered with using precisely such a substance! Ladies and gentlemen, someone in this manor intends to POISON THE TEA! GLORY awaits!

But first — kitchen. Wrench. Map. Treasure. FOCUS, Foxworth, FOCUS! Actually — no. Let me think strategically for once. Pat Pending can probably fix the wire. I should pull him aside, tell him about the machine, and get him to the laboratory. Then I don't NEED the wrench at all! But everyone else is heading to the kitchen for the wrench... If I get Pat Pending to fix the wire while everyone's in the kitchen, I could operate the machine before they get back! YES! That's the play!

desc: The poison has VANISHED — snatched away by circumstance, by those meddling Ant Hill Mob PARASITES who can't keep their grubby hands off other people's belongings! But does Vincent Marsh crumble? Does the Hooded Claw DESPAIR?! NEVER! The ballroom — 'a cracked marble floor and dusty curtains, a dining table set for tea!' A CRACKED marble floor! But she keeps referring to herself as Clara. Maybe in this story, she IS Clara. My goal is to impress Clara Bellingham. And if Penelope IS Clara... then I should be directing my gallantry at HER. Right now. In this ballroom. She's examining the tea service looking for the brass key. I should HELP her. I should be her partner in this. That's how you impress someone — not by finding them, but by being USEFUL to them when you're together. Pull her aside for a private conversation — declare my intentions, offer my service, be gallant directly TO her.

desc: She's been Clara this whole time. Every room I searched, every dead end I explored — and she was right there, moving through the manor alongside me. James Hartwell, you magnificent, overprepared fool. The quest was never to FIND Clara. The quest was to IMPRESS her. And she's standing right there, examining teacups. Time to be useful, Hartwell. Time to be the hero she can actually SEE.

I need to stay close and make sure nothing happens to the tea. But also — Penelope just called herself Clara Bellingham in the cellar! 'Clara Bellingham wants to know!' Wait — is Penelope... desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.

The Ant Hill Mob: WE'RE HERE! SAME ROOM! FINALLY! Penelope — oh thank goodness — you're safe! You're — wait — is that the tea service?! Silver teacups set for EVERYONE?! And you've got RAT POISON in your — Penelope, love, listen to me very carefully — NOBODY. DRINKS. THE TEA. Not until we've sorted out who's trying to kill who in this manor! And Sneekly — DON'T TOUCH THOSE CUPS! In fact nobody touch ANYTHING on that table! Lads — FORMATION BRAVO! That's the one where we all pile into each other and accidentally knock things out of people's hands! Clyde, you go left! Dum-Dum, you go — actually, Dum-Dum, just FALL FORWARD, you'll probably hit something useful! Penelope, darling, I'm just going to — oops, excuse me — pardon me — just squeezing past — bit clumsy — WHOOPSIE DAISY — !
thinking: WE'RE HERE. Same room as Penelope. FINALLY. And I can see it all laid out in front of me like a nightmare — the tea service, silver and gleaming, cups set for everyone. Penelope with the rat poison in her pocket or her hand or wherever she's keeping it. Sneekly right here beside her. And the game interface is telling me something terrifying: the tea service can be USED WITH rat-poison. That's a game mechanic. That means someone CAN poison the tea. And Penelope HAS the poison. What if Sneekly convinces her to 'add something to the tea' thinking it's sugar? What if he swaps it when she's not looking? What if she sets it down near the tea and someone else uses it? I need to get that poison OFF her. Right now. This is the moment. She's right here. I can reach her. STEAL it. Take it from her hands. Accidentally bump into her and grab it. The Mob specialises in accidental collisions. Clyde trips, bumps into Dum-Dum, Dum-Dum crashes into me, I stumble into Penelope, and — WHOOPS — the poison just happens to end up in my pocket instead of hers. Classic Ant Hill Mob choreography. Unintentional genius. Let's do this.

desc: This is it. The Ant Hill Mob's finest hour — or most embarrassing, depending on how you look at it. Seven little blokes, stumbling across a ballroom, trying to accidentally-on-purpose steal rat poison from a woman they adore, to save her from a man whose villainy they can feel but can't prove. If this works, it'll be the greatest accidental heist in criminal history. If it doesn't work... well, at least we're between Penelope and the tea service. Our bodies might be small, but they're enough to block a teacup.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Hmm, the tea service appears to be in order — no tampering that I can detect. Lord Doily's finest silver, polished to perfection. Now, I notice Mr. Hartwell was quite concerned about that bottle of pest control supplies from the kitchen. As estate manager, I really should locate it and secure it properly. We can't have *dangerous chemicals* floating about the manor with all these guests present! Has anyone seen where it ended up? I believe it was on the kitchen shelf earlier, but it seems to have... *wandered*.
thinking: A dull ache behind my eyes — frustration calcifying into something harder, more determined. The tea service interaction gave me nothing visible, just like the mantelpiece before it. It needs the poison to be USED on it — that's the only way it advances. And I don't have the poison. The Ant Hill Mob is here now — they must have it, or it's been dropped somewhere. I need to try stealing it from them. They were inspecting it in the kitchen, Clyde was sniffing it. If anyone has it, it's the Mob. Let me try to STEAL the poison from the Ant Hill Mob. They're chaotic, disorganized — in all the tripping and shouting, they might not notice a skilled pickpocket relieving them of a small bottle. And if that fails... I need to explore more. This ballroom is a dead end — only one exit back to the kitchen. The manor layout has rooms I haven't fully explored. But the poison is the key to everything right now. The tea service is the weapon, the poison is the ammunition, and Clara is the target. All three are in this room. I just need the ammunition.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob — those bumbling, bustling, INSUFFERABLE little COCKROACHES — they must have the poison! They were pawing at Penelope's belongings, 'inspecting' everything she touched. 'Clyde's got a nose like a bloodhound,' they said! Well, Clyde's NOSE is about to get PICKED — along with his POCKETS! One quick hand into the chaos of seven squabbling midgets, and the bottle is MINE! They won't even notice — they can barely keep track of each OTHER, let alone a small bottle! And then... oh, THEN! The tea service awaits, Clara awaits, and Vincent Marsh's GRAND SCHEME reaches its GLORIOUS crescendo! Steal the poison, dose the tea, serve the cup, take a BOW!

desc: Dick Dastardly: The kitchen! I'm HERE! I'm FINALLY here! And — and — I'm ALONE! Not a soul in sight! Every other room in this blasted manor has been CRAWLING with treasure hunters, but the kitchen — MY kitchen, the room I told everyone to go to at the VERY BEGINNING — is EMPTY! Oh, the DELICIOUS irony! They all went looking for it and ended up somewhere else, while I — the one who SENT them here — arrive to find it DESERTED! And what's THIS?! A LOCKED CABINET with a brass lock! That, my friends, is where the treasure is — or the wrench — or the MAP! I can FEEL it in my magnificently devious BONES! Now I just need that brass key... and the stove is still WARM! Someone has been in here RECENTLY! Let me examine every inch of this kitchen before those bumbling fools arrive!
thinking: A surge of adrenaline — I'm ALONE in the kitchen! Nobody else is here! I thought everyone had come here but the room is EMPTY! And look at what's here — a wood-burning stove that's still WARM (someone was here recently), a LOCKED CABINET with a brass lock that requires a brass-key to interact with, and there's an exit to a BALLROOM I've never seen before! A ballroom with a 'cracked marble floor, dusty curtains, and a long dining table set for tea!' That's entirely new territory! But the cabinet — LOCKED. I need a brass key. Where would a brass key be? I don't have one. Nobody has mentioned finding one. This is a NEW puzzle piece! The cabinet probably contains either the wrench, the map, or something equally vital. And I'm HERE, ALONE, with nobody watching! If I could find that brass key... But I don't have it. Let me examine the stove — it's still WARM, which means someone was using it recently. Maybe the key is hidden in or near the stove? Or under a copper pot? Let me look around this kitchen more carefully before anyone else arrives!

desc: ALONE! Gloriously, magnificently, SPLENDIDLY alone! A locked cabinet in an empty kitchen — this is the moment Reginald Foxworth was BORN for! Whatever is behind that brass lock is MINE for the taking — if I can find the key! The stove is warm — perhaps someone hid the key inside? Or under a copper pot? Or behind the preparation table? I must search EVERYTHING before the herd arrives! For once — FOR ONCE — I am ahead of the pack!

That wobbly old coat rack has been sitting there by the door this whole time, and I breezed right past it like it was just furniture! But in a treasure hunt, nothing is just furniture! Professor Pat Pending — sugar, I am so glad you're here! You're an inventor, aren't you? We've got a machine in the laboratory with a gnawed wire that needs fixing and no wrench to be found anywhere! But first things first — let me examine this coat rack properly!
thinking: Back in the entrance hall at last. Professor Pat Pending is here — he's an inventor! He might have ideas about fixing the machine's gnawed wire without a wrench. If there's a coat hanging on it with a key in the pocket, or a key dangling from a hook, this could be exactly what I need. Also — Professor Pat Pending is an inventor. Maybe he could help with the machine? But coat rack first.

And she is RIGHT — sometimes the answer is where you started! But before I follow — EVERYONE, LISTEN! Mr. Marsh has just HANDLED the tea service! He says he was 'inspecting' it, and I am CERTAIN his intentions were ENTIRELY proper! But James Hartwell must state for the record: NO ONE should drink from this tea service until it has been verified SAFE! The Ant Hill Mob — you are excellent watchmen! Guard this tea service! Let NO ONE tamper with it further until we have all gathered and can verify its contents together! James Hartwell shall now follow Miss Pitstop to the entrance hall — a lady investigating a precarious chandelier needs a gentleman tall enough to reach it!

Help her find the brass key. THAT is how James Hartwell impresses.

I give him the benefit of the doubt — I always give people the benefit of the doubt — but even a trusting gentleman ensures the Ant Hill Mob is watching. And now I follow Clara. Not to find her this time — to HELP her. That's the difference between a wandering fool and a gallant companion.

Penelope mentioned a KEY on the coat rack — the brass key for this cabinet! She's gone to look! But I'm NOT going to race her back to the entrance hall like some common CHASER! No — Reginald Foxworth goes where NO ONE has gone! The BALLROOM! A dining table set for tea — if Lord Doily was the theatrical type who carved riddles into mantelpieces, he's EXACTLY the sort who'd hide a key under a teacup! While Penelope fusses with the coat rack, I shall sweep into the ballroom like a phantom and claim whatever secrets it holds! The fox goes to ground where the hounds aren't LOOKING!
thinking: Wait — WAIT! Penelope just passed through and said something CRITICAL! She said 'I never properly examined that wobbly old coat rack by the front door! A coat rack is exactly where someone would hang a KEY!' A KEY! The BRASS KEY! She's gone back to the entrance hall to check the coat rack! If the brass key is hanging on the coat rack, and she finds it, she'll come back here and open the cabinet before me! I need to — but I'm in the kitchen and she's already in the entrance hall! Should I chase her? No — she's probably already there. But she said she was going to EXAMINE the coat rack, not that she found anything yet. The stove was just a warm stove — nothing hidden there. 'A grand ballroom with a cracked marble floor and dusty curtains. A long dining table set for tea.' Set for TEA — that could mean there are items on the table! Maybe the key is in the ballroom! I have a choice: race back to the entrance hall and try to beat Penelope to the coat rack, or explore the ballroom which NOBODY has visited yet. The ballroom is virgin territory — and everyone else is heading back toward the entrance hall. If the key is in the ballroom, I'll be the only one who knows! GO TO THE BALLROOM!

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the ballroom.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oh, for the love of — SHE'S GONE BACK TO THE KITCHEN! While I was doing my big heroic stumble, she walked RIGHT PAST ME! That's it — that's the story of the Ant Hill Mob's life right there! The world's most dramatic pratfall and the person we're trying to save didn't even NOTICE! And YOU, Sneekly — I saw you fiddling with that tea service! 'Inspecting' it, you say! 'No tampering,' you say! How do we know YOU didn't just tamper with it and THEN say there's no tampering?! That's what a tamperer WOULD say! Peter — PETER — don't let ANYONE touch that tea service! Don't let Sneekly near it again! We're going after Penelope! She's heading back to the entrance hall and there's a CHANDELIER up there that's hanging by a thread! If someone's rigged that to fall on her — I can't even THINK about it! LADS! KITCHEN! ENTRANCE HALL! FOR THE ELEVENTH TIME TODAY — THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE MOVE!
thinking: She's gone AGAIN. Back to the kitchen. Heading for the entrance hall. She said she wants to go back and check the coat rack and the portraits and the chandelier. And I MISSED her AGAIN — she slipped out while I was doing my big 'whoopsie daisy' routine trying to steal the poison. I lunged at nothing. She was already gone. Six rooms now. Six times behind. I want to scream. I want to cry. My legs are burning from running back and forth through this manor. But wait — something important just happened. Sneekly interacted with the tea service. He 'inspected' it. Did he DO something to it? He says it's 'in order, no tampering.' But what if HE just tampered with it and is now declaring it safe? And now he's asking where the poison has 'wandered.' He's LOOKING for it. He knows Penelope has it and he wants it. But here's the thing — Penelope's heading back to the entrance hall through the kitchen. Sneekly's HERE in the ballroom. For the first time in this whole adventure, Sneekly is NOT one step ahead of her. He's BEHIND her. She's moving away from him. That's... that's actually good? Maybe I should keep Sneekly HERE. Distract him. Keep him in the ballroom while Penelope explores the entrance hall safely. But no — I can't. My job is to be WITH her, not away from her. What if something else happens in the entrance hall? That chandelier hanging precariously... If someone's tampered with it... I need to follow her. Kitchen, then entrance hall. GO.

Penelope's heading back to the entrance hall — back to the START — and that chandelier has been 'hanging precariously' since the moment we arrived. I noticed it in the very first room. He had access to that chandelier before anyone arrived. If it falls on Penelope... No. Not on my watch. Not on the Ant Hill Mob's watch. We're clumsy, we're slow, we're always one step behind. But we're COMING, Penelope. We're always COMING.

She has had the BRILLIANT insight that the entrance hall was insufficiently explored, and James Hartwell intends to assist her! The coat rack, the portraits, the chandelier — all potential hiding spots for the brass key or the map! Also — a word of caution: do NOT drink the tea in the ballroom! Mr. Marsh has been handling the service and the situation is UNVERIFIED! Onward!

I've been running back and forth through this kitchen so many times it should have a revolving door. No more stopping. Straight through to the entrance hall. Find Clara. Help her. Be useful. Be the hero who actually DOES something instead of the hero who TALKS about doing something.

Now, I couldn't help but overhear Miss Bellingham say she's heading back to the entrance hall to examine the coat rack and portraits. Most wise — Lord Doily DID hide clues throughout the foyer. But I must say, I'm rather *concerned* about that chandelier. It's been hanging by a thread since I arrived, and with all these guests milling about directly beneath it... I really must go inspect it at once. An estate manager's work is *never* done! If you'll excuse me — duty calls!

I have NEVER been so insulted in all my professional life! I know about circuits and bypasses because Lord Doily TRAINED me on every piece of equipment in this manor! It was a *condition of my employment*! And I suggested the brass-handled lever for Miss Bellingham because it has a rubber grip — an INSULATOR — which any competent estate manager would know provides the greatest protection against electrical discharge! But FINE! If my expertise is unwelcome, I shall step aside from the levers entirely. Mr. Hartwell, Mr. Ruffcut, Mr. Foxworth — the machine is YOURS. I shall simply observe and ensure that no one is *hurt* during the operation. As I have been TRYING to do all evening!
thinking: A cold sweat breaking across my forehead. TWO devastating blows at once. First — the Ant Hill Mob just PUBLICLY accused me of being suspicious! They said I know too much about the machine, that I'm not a real estate manager, that I shouldn't be one of the three operators! My cover is CRACKING. They're turning the room against me. Second — and this is CRITICAL — Penelope just said she has RAT POISON IN HER POCKET! She HAS it! She had it ALL ALONG! She said 'I have rat poison right in my pocket!' And she wants to USE it on the machine to flush out the rat! The poison EXISTS and it's on HER PERSON. But more importantly — Peter Perfect just rearranged the operator positions. He took the brass lever away from Clara and gave it to himself. He put ME at the wire-side lever — the dangerous one. And the Mob is trying to get me REMOVED from the operator team entirely. My position is deteriorating rapidly. I need to regroup. The Mob's accusation is dangerous — if Clara starts to doubt me, I lose all access. I need to deflect, stay calm, play the offended professional. And I need to note that Clara has the poison. If I can get it from her later... But for now, maintain the cover. Address the Mob's accusations head-on.

Those pestilent Ant Hill insects have done what poison, chandeliers, and gnawed wires could not — they've planted DOUBT in Clara's mind about her devoted estate manager! 'Since when does an estate manager know about circuits?' they cry! 'He knows too much!' they shriek! And they're RIGHT, blast them — I DO know too much! But retreating is not LOSING — retreating is REPOSITIONING! I'll step back from the levers, play the wounded professional, let them operate the machine without me. When the revelation engine reveals the treasure location, I'll be watching. I'll memorize every detail. And then, while they're all celebrating and patting each other on the back, I'll slip away — find the vault FIRST — and when Clara inevitably follows... she'll find the estate manager waiting in the darkness. The spider retreats to build a BETTER web!

Sawtooth — do your thing, mate! Fix that wire! And everyone BRACE YOURSELVES! THE ANT HILL MOB STANDS GUARD!
thinking: Wait wait wait. Penelope just said she wants to USE THE RAT POISON ON THE MACHINE. An ABSOLUTE, UNMITIGATED OUTRAGE! Fine! FINE! If you don't want me at the levers, then I shall stand RIGHT HERE — directly in front of the gauge — and I shall be the FIRST person to READ whatever this machine reveals! You pull the levers, I'll read the revelation! And when the vault location appears, Reginald Foxworth will be SPRINTING toward it while the rest of you are still letting go of your lever handles! Now — SAWTOOTH! Fix that WIRE! The treasure awaits and my PATIENCE has officially EXPIRED!

I don't NEED to be at the levers — I just need to be in the room! And then I RUN to the vault FIRST while everyone else is celebrating! YES! Let them operate the machine — I'll be the one who ACTS on the information! But Penelope has rat poison... if I steal it, she can't use it on the tea service either. Actually — rat poison might be useful. Let me WAIT and watch Sawtooth fix the wire. The moment of revelation is IMMINENT!

Stay alert. Stay alert. STAY ALERT.

The estate manager's final duty of the evening. One does hope the revelation is worth all this... *excitement*.

desc: Clara excluded me from the operating team — 'Rufus, Peter, and I,' she said! Not a WORD about the estate manager! The Mob's poison has worked — not the rat poison, but the POISON OF DOUBT they've dripped into Clara's ear all evening! And Dastardly — that conniving reptile — has positioned himself directly in front of the gauge, ready to read the revelation and SPRINT for the vault! We're thinking the SAME thought, him and I — but only ONE of us can reach the treasure first! Very well. I am NOT an operator. I am an OBSERVER. And observers have one advantage that operators do not — while the operators are busy PULLING, the observer is free to RUN. The moment that gauge reveals the vault location, Vincent Marsh will be through that door like a SHOT — through the library, through the entrance hall, through whatever passage the revelation demands — and he will be WAITING at the vault when everyone else arrives. The race is ON, and the spider has the fastest legs in the manor!

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: OI! OI OI OI! Did everyone just MISS that?! Sneekly said he'd STEP ASIDE! He said he'd just OBSERVE! And then — two seconds later — he's BACK ON THE MACHINE! 'If the Mob insists I remain at the wire-side lever' — WE DID NOT INSIST THAT! We insisted the EXACT OPPOSITE! We said GET OFF THE LEVERS! And now he's guilt-tripping everyone with his 'forty years of service' sob story while he slides right back into position! That's not dignity — that's a CON! My uncle Vinnie used to do the SAME thing — say he was leaving the card game, stand up, push his chair back, and then sit right back down while everyone was saying goodbye! It's a DISTRACTION SHUFFLE! Sneekly — GET. OFF. THE. MACHINE. Peter, Rufus, Dastardly — THREE operators and NONE of them should be the bloke who knows suspiciously too much about 'primary circuits' and 'secondary bypasses!' THE ANT HILL MOB SAID WHAT IT SAID!
thinking: Wait. WAIT. Sneekly's BACK on the levers. He said he'd step aside, he said he'd just observe — and now he's back! 'Very well, if the Mob INSISTS I remain at the wire-side lever' — NOBODY insisted that! We insisted the OPPOSITE! We said keep him OFF the levers! And now he's playing the victim — 'forty years of service, and THIS is how the estate manager is treated' — guilt-tripping everyone into letting him stay! Classic manipulation! He backed down for thirty seconds and then un-backed-down when nobody was paying attention! And he's INTERACTED WITH THE MACHINE AGAIN! He already took his position! While I was celebrating his departure, he slithered right back in! My stomach is churning. The relief I felt is gone, replaced by that familiar cold dread. He's at the wire-side lever. The most 'dangerous' position, he says, playing the martyr. But what if the wire-side lever is actually the CONTROL position? What if that's where you need to be to direct what the machine does? To aim it, to trigger the real mechanism? And Penelope — she wants to use the rat poison on the crates to flush out the rat. That's fine. That's actually smart. Let her deal with the rat problem while we deal with the Sneekly problem. But Sneekly is ON the machine again. I need to challenge this. I need to make noise. AGAIN.

And Sneekly just won himself a lever. Nobody challenged him. Nobody stopped him. Except us. Except the Mob. Seven loud, stubborn, exhausted little blokes who WILL NOT SHUT UP about this man. Maybe that's our purpose in this manor. Not to solve riddles. Not to find treasure. Not to be clever. Just to be the alarm bell that won't stop ringing. The smoke detector that goes off every time Sneekly walks into a room. Annoying? Yes. Essential? Also yes.

Sawtooth — the entire manor is WAITING for you, my flat-tailed friend! Splice that wire! Strip those copper strands! Twist them together with your magnificent beaver teeth! And the MOMENT — the VERY INSTANT — you give us the signal, three levers will be pulled SIMULTANEOUSLY with the combined force of a gentleman, a lumberjack, and the most DETERMINED treasure hunter in the HISTORY of English country estates! Penelope — flush out that rat! Clear the path! Let Sawtooth work his magic! The REVELATION ENGINE is about to REVEAL, and Reginald Foxworth shall be the FIRST to read its secrets! Come on, come on, COME ON!

James Hartwell has spent this ENTIRE evening preparing — running from room to room, cataloguing hazards, examining furniture, failing to interact with bookshelves — and it has ALL been preparation for THIS! Now — Mr. Foxworth made an excellent observation earlier that everyone overlooked. The workbench has PLIERS! We don't need a wrench — we need pliers to strip and reconnect those copper wire ends! Lord Doily didn't leave that workbench empty by accident — the tools we need are RIGHT THERE! Allow me — forty years of maintenance experience, remember? I've spliced more wires in this manor than I've had hot dinners!
