And heroes... heroes get to lead Clara Bellingham into the darkness. ALONE.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: There you go, Sawtooth — the rat poison is all yours! Now you've got everything you need, sugar! Deal with that pesky rat, splice that wire back together, and we'll have this revelation engine singing like a choir on Sunday morning! Everyone is in position — Dick at lever one, Peter at lever two, and Rufus, you're at lever three! The Ant Hill boys are standing guard! And Clara Bellingham is giving the count the moment Sawtooth gives us the all-clear! This is it, y'all — this is the moment we've all been working toward! The Doily Diamond is just a wire splice and three lever pulls away from being found! Sawtooth — the floor is yours!
thinking: I gave the rat poison to Sawtooth! My inventory is now empty. The action succeeded — 'You gave rat-poison to Sawtooth.' Now I need to wait and see if this triggers something. Maybe Sawtooth will use the poison to deal with the rat and then fix the wire. Or maybe something else happens. Everyone is in position at their levers — Dick at lever one, Peter at lever two, Rufus presumably at lever three. The scene is building to a climax. Let me WAIT and see what unfolds. This feels like it could be the turning point — giving an item to the right character to trigger the next phase of the puzzle.

desc: I gave away my only item to a beaver. Either that was the smartest thing I've done all evening or the most ridiculous. But Sawtooth took it — the game accepted the GIVE action. Something should happen now. Either Sawtooth uses the poison on the rat and fixes the wire, or I've just armed a beaver with industrial-grade rat poison for no reason. Aunt Magnolia would have something to say about that.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right! LISTEN UP, everyone! We've been pulling levers for the last five minutes and NOTHING'S HAPPENED because the wire is STILL BROKEN! Stop pulling levers! STOP IT! The machine won't work until Sawtooth fixes that wire, and Sawtooth can't fix the wire while everyone's jostling for position at the controls like it's the last bus to Brixton! EVERYONE STEP BACK! Give the beaver some ROOM! Sawtooth — mate — you're the most important person in this room right now! More important than the estate manager, more important than the treasure hunters, more important than seven panicking blokes from South London! You fix that wire and THEN — and ONLY THEN — do three people pull the levers! And the Mob will be standing RIGHT HERE the WHOLE TIME, between Penelope and whatever happens next! We've been chasing through this manor for eleven minutes and this is the first time we've been in the RIGHT ROOM at the RIGHT TIME! We're not wasting it! THE ANT HILL MOB HOLDS THE LINE!
thinking: Okay. Stop. Breathe. Feel my feet on the cold laboratory floor. My heart is pounding but I need to THINK for a second instead of just reacting. What's actually happening here? Everyone's in position. Peter's at the brass lever. Dastardly's at the centre lever facing the gauge. Sneekly's still lurking near the wire-side — but wait, the latest dialogue shows him saying 'I see I am no longer among the chosen' and he'll 'ensure the machine operates safely.' So maybe he IS stepping back this time? Or is he playing the same trick again? Penelope tried to use the poison on the crates and it didn't work. She still HAS the poison. And now she's calling for everyone to pull together — 'on my count, three, two, one, PULL!' She's about to make everyone operate the machine AGAIN. With the wire still broken. It won't work — we've proven that. The wire needs fixing first. Sawtooth needs to splice it. But in all this chaos, everyone keeps pulling levers and nothing happens because THE WIRE IS STILL BROKEN. We're going in circles. The Mob needs to do something USEFUL instead of just standing here yelling. What can we actually DO? We can't fix the wire. We can't operate the machine. But we CAN stand guard. And actually — Penelope is HERE. She's in this room. She's not running to another room. For the first time in this entire adventure, she's staying PUT. And so are we. Maybe... maybe the best thing the Mob can do right now is exactly what we're doing. Standing here. Being loud. Being present. Being the wall. Sometimes the most heroic thing you can do is just NOT LEAVE.

desc: Eleven minutes in this manor. Eleven minutes of chasing Penelope from room to room, always one step behind, shouting warnings nobody listens to, tripping over furniture, bumping into coat racks, and making speeches to empty rooms. And now — finally — everyone's here. Penelope's here. The machine's here. The moment's coming. Sawtooth will fix the wire. Three people will pull the levers. The revelation engine will reveal... whatever it reveals. And the Ant Hill Mob will be standing between Penelope and whatever comes next. Not because we're brave. Not because we're clever. Because we're HERE. We showed up. We kept showing up. Room after room after room, we kept showing up. And in the end, that's all that matters. The Ant Hill Mob showed up.

desc: The workbench mocks me with the same flat description it's given EVERYONE! 'Tools — but no wrench.' YES, we KNOW there's no wrench! But there are OTHER tools! Pliers! Screwdrivers! Wire cutters! Why can't I TAKE any of them?! This workbench is the most INFURIATING piece of furniture in the entire manor — more infuriating than the uninteractable bookshelves, more infuriating than the decorative chandelier, more infuriating than the vanishing rat poison! But Penelope just gave the poison to SAWTOOTH. The beaver has it now. If Sawtooth uses the poison on the machine to flush out the rat, then fixes the wire... the machine will WORK. And I need to be positioned to see the revelation. Forget the workbench. Forget being the hero who fixes things. Position yourself at the GAUGE, Vincent — right next to Dastardly — and be ready to READ and RUN the moment that machine comes alive!
thinking: A sharp clarity cutting through the fog. I see it now in the keen observations — 'Penelope Pitstop handed rat-poison to sawtooth.' She GAVE the rat poison to Sawtooth! The beaver now has rat poison AND presumably the ability to fix the wire. This could be the turning point. Sawtooth deals with the rat, fixes the wire, and then three operators pull the levers. But I need to stop wasting turns LOOKing at things that give me the same description. The workbench doesn't have a TAKE tag. I can't pick up tools from it. The game doesn't let me take individual tools. I'm stuck. Everyone is stuck. The machine needs Sawtooth to fix it. I can't control Sawtooth. What CAN I do? I should try to INTERACT with the workbench — maybe that yields something different. Or... I should try something completely different. What if I USE the workbench ON the machine? No, I need an inventory item. I have nothing. Wait — what if I try to TAKE the workbench itself? Absurd, but everything else has failed. Actually, let me try INTERACT with the workbench. It's not marked as interactable, but neither was the machine at first until I tried.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the machine.

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell is at lever TWO! Clara has armed Sawtooth with the rat poison — the beaver is equipped, the operators are positioned, and Clara Bellingham shall give the count! There is NOTHING more to do but WAIT for Sawtooth to work his magic! And for ONCE in his life, James Hartwell shall wait with PATIENCE rather than running to the next room to examine another coat rack! The plan is PERFECT — Clara's plan, not mine, and all the better for it! Sawtooth — we are ALL behind you! Fix that wire and THREE brave operators shall pull THREE levers on Clara's count! The Doily Diamond awaits!
thinking: A strange calm settling over me. The workbench can't be interacted with either. The crates can't be moved. The bookshelves can't be interacted with. The machine won't work without the wire fixed. Clara just gave the rat poison to Sawtooth — she handed it to him! Now Sawtooth has the rat poison and Clara asked him to deal with the rat and splice the wire. Everyone is in position — Dick at lever one, me at lever two, Rufus at lever three. Clara is giving the count when Sawtooth gives the all-clear. The scene is set. Everything depends on Sawtooth now. I should simply WAIT. Wait for Sawtooth to do his work. Wait for Clara's count. Be at my lever, ready. No more examining, no more interacting with things that can't be interacted with. Just... patience. A gentleman who has done everything he can does the hardest thing of all: he waits.

desc: For the first time tonight, James Hartwell has nothing to do but stand at his lever and trust. Trust the beaver. Trust the plan. Trust Clara. A gentleman who cannot wait is merely a gentleman in motion. A gentleman who CAN wait — that is a gentleman at peace.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Mr. Marsh, you brilliant man — PLIERS! The workbench has pliers! We've all been so fixated on finding a wrench that we forgot the workbench is covered in other tools! Pliers can strip wire and twist copper strands together — that's exactly what we need to splice that gnawed wire! Why didn't any of us think of this sooner? The answer was sitting on that workbench the whole time, right under our noses! Let me get those pliers!
thinking: Mr. Marsh just said the workbench has PLIERS! He said 'The workbench has PLIERS! We don't need a wrench — we need pliers to strip and reconnect those copper wire ends!' And Peter agreed — 'Dastardly was RIGHT — we don't need a wrench, we need PLIERS!' The workbench description says 'covered in tools — but no wrench.' But it has other tools! PLIERS! Maybe I need to try to TAKE the workbench — no, I already know objects need to be listed as takeable. But what if I try to INTERACT with the workbench? I never tried that! The workbench isn't listed with an INTERACT tag, but maybe it works anyway. Or what if I try to USE something on the workbench... but I have nothing in my inventory now. I gave away the rat poison. Hmm. What if I just try to INTERACT with the workbench directly? Let me try it — it might have tools I can take or use.

Mr. Marsh — for all his suspicious behavior — might have just given us the breakthrough we needed!

desc: Dick Dastardly: YES! Lever ONE is MINE! Penelope CONFIRMED it — Dick at lever one, Peter at lever two, Rufus at lever three! I am LOCKED IN! My hands are on this lever and they are NOT coming off until the Doily Diamond's location is BLAZING across that gauge! Now — SAWTOOTH! You have rat poison AND the finest gnawing teeth in the animal kingdom! You are a one-beaver MAINTENANCE CREW! Fix that wire, my magnificent flat-tailed friend! And MARSH — if there ARE pliers on that workbench, for the love of all that is HOLY, hand them to the beaver! The rest of you — NOBODY moves, NOBODY leaves, NOBODY touches ANYTHING until that wire is fixed and we pull these levers TOGETHER! We are TWELVE MINUTES into this treasure hunt and we are THIS CLOSE! Reginald Foxworth can SMELL the diamond! It smells like... victory and EXPENSIVE jewellery!
thinking: A strange calm settling over me, like the eye of a storm. The machine didn't work. Again. But something IMPORTANT just happened — Penelope gave the rat poison to Sawtooth! Sawtooth now has rat poison AND his beaver teeth. And Penelope confirmed the lineup: Dick at lever one, Peter at lever two, Rufus at lever three! I'm CONFIRMED! And Sneekly — that magnificent snake — just pointed out what I said earlier: the workbench has PLIERS! He's examining the workbench again. Peter also said 'forget the wrench, James Hartwell seeks pliers!' Everyone is FINALLY realising what I said turns ago — you don't need a wrench to fix a wire, you need PLIERS! Maybe someone will actually manage to get pliers from the workbench this time. Or maybe Sawtooth will just gnaw the wire back together. Either way — the pieces are converging. Penelope said 'the floor is yours, Sawtooth!' Sawtooth has the rat poison and his teeth. The wire repair is about to happen. I just need to STAY at my lever and WAIT for the signal. My position is secured: lever one, centre, facing the gauge. When the wire is fixed and we pull simultaneously, the revelation will come. And I'll be the first to read it.

desc: Everything aligns. Lever one is mine. Penelope confirmed it. Sawtooth is about to fix the wire. And when those levers pull and the gauge reveals the vault's location, Reginald Foxworth's eyes will be the FIRST to read it. Then — one shout of a FALSE direction to the crowd, and a quiet sprint to the REAL one. The greatest confidence trick of the evening, performed at the moment of revelation itself. The fox waits at the mouth of the burrow. Patient. Ready. HUNGRY.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: HOLD IT! HOLD EVERYTHING! Sneekly — did everyone just hear that?! He wants to fix the wire HIMSELF! 'Allow me, forty years of maintenance experience!' First he wants to OPERATE the machine, now he wants to FIX it?! He wants to control EVERYTHING about this machine — who operates it, how it's wired, where everyone stands! NO! Sawtooth fixes the wire! SAWTOOTH! The beaver! The HONEST beaver with no suspicious agenda! Penelope already gave him the poison to deal with the rat — let him do his JOB! Sneekly, you step AWAY from that workbench! You've been one room ahead this entire evening, you know more about this machine's circuits than any estate manager should, and now you want to be the one who reconnects the wire?! The wire that YOU said was SABOTAGED?! If anyone's going to splice those copper strands, it's going to be someone who DIDN'T spend the whole night trying to get Penelope alone! Sawtooth — you're up, mate! THE ANT HILL MOB TRUSTS THE BEAVER!
thinking: Two things just happened that matter. First — Penelope gave the rat poison to Sawtooth. She doesn't have it anymore. That's... actually a relief? The poison is out of her hands. Sawtooth is a beaver. He's not going to poison anyone's tea. He's going to deal with the rat and fix the wire. That's good. Second — and this is more worrying — Sneekly just said 'Allow me — forty years of maintenance experience, I've spliced more wires in this manor than I've had hot dinners!' and examined the workbench. He wants to fix the wire HIMSELF. Not Sawtooth — HIM. With pliers from the workbench. If Sneekly fixes the wire, he controls HOW it's fixed. What if he fixes it wrong on purpose? What if he creates a connection that's dangerous? What if the way the wire is spliced determines what the machine actually DOES? A proper splice makes it work correctly. An improper splice makes it do something else. Something dangerous. He's an 'estate manager' who knows about primary circuits and secondary bypasses. If he gets his hands on those pliers and that wire, he could wire it to do ANYTHING. Sawtooth should fix the wire. Not Sneekly. Sawtooth is a beaver — he gnaws and strips wire naturally. He's honest. He's got no agenda. Sneekly has ALL the agendas. I need to make sure SAWTOOTH fixes the wire, not Sneekly.

desc: The wire. It always comes back to the wire. Sneekly told us it was sabotaged — not by rats, by a person. He told us it was deliberate. And now he wants to be the one who fixes it. Think about that. The man who KNOWS the wire was deliberately cut wants to be the one who reconnects it. What does he reconnect it TO? The primary circuit? The secondary bypass? The one that reveals the treasure? Or the one that does something to whoever's standing at the brass lever? If Sawtooth fixes it — a beaver, an animal, no guile, no scheme — the wire gets connected properly. Copper to copper. Clean and honest. But if Sneekly fixes it... who knows what he connects to what. The Ant Hill Mob doesn't understand circuits. But we understand trust. And we trust the beaver.

desc: Peter Perfect: PLIERS! Of COURSE! Clara, you are MAGNIFICENT! The answer was on the workbench this ENTIRE TIME and we were all so fixated on the missing wrench that we couldn't see the tools that WERE there! James Hartwell himself tried to interact with that workbench not TWO minutes ago — and he was looking for the very thing Clara has now found! Pliers to strip the wire, pliers to twist the copper strands, pliers to COMPLETE THE CIRCUIT! Get those pliers, Clara! Fix the wire! And the MOMENT that circuit is complete, THREE operators stand READY at their levers! James Hartwell is not moving from this spot! He is PLANTED! He is READY! He is — for the first time this entire evening — exactly where he needs to be, doing exactly what needs to be done, which is WAITING while a brilliant woman solves the problem he could not!
thinking: A spark of hope — Clara just realized the workbench has PLIERS! She's going to get the pliers to fix the wire! The answer WAS on the workbench the whole time — we were all looking for a wrench when pliers were right there! Sneekly even pointed this out. And Clara is grabbing them. The Ant Hill Mob is right — everyone needs to step back, let the wire get fixed, THEN pull the levers. I tried to interact with the workbench and it wouldn't let me, but maybe Clara can take the pliers. Or maybe someone needs to USE the pliers on the machine. I should wait. Let Clara get the pliers. Let someone fix the wire. Then three operators pull. I'm at my lever. I'm ready. Just... wait. Trust the process. Trust Clara.

desc: She found the pliers. The workbench wouldn't let ME interact with it, but Clara sees what I missed. Again. Every breakthrough tonight has been hers. The riddle answer, the Sawtooth idea, the return to the entrance hall, and now the pliers. James Hartwell's contribution has been... standing at a lever and giving speeches. But perhaps that IS the contribution. Perhaps every team needs someone who stands at the lever and believes.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Y'all are absolutely right — the Ant Hill boys are right, Peter's right, everyone just needs to step back and let Sawtooth do his thing! I've been running around this manor like a chicken with its head cut off, trying everything I can think of — pulling levers, examining furniture, using rat poison on everything that stands still! But sometimes the answer isn't about doing more — it's about doing less and letting the right person handle it! Sawtooth has the rat poison, the workbench has tools, and that beaver has been building dams since before any of us were born! I trust you, Sawtooth! Take your time, sugar — use whatever tools you need from that workbench, deal with the rat, and splice that wire! Clara Bellingham is going to stand right here with the Ant Hill boys and wait like a lady! And when you're done — THREE, TWO, ONE, PULL!
thinking: Workbench can't be interacted with either. I'm completely stuck. I've tried every action on every object in every room. The machine needs the wire fixed but there's no mechanic to fix it through my actions. Maybe this is a scenario where the resolution comes through the NPCs acting on their own — I've set everything in motion by giving Sawtooth the rat poison, rallying everyone to their positions, and identifying the problem. Maybe I just need to WAIT and let the scene play out. The Ant Hill Mob is telling everyone to step back and let Sawtooth work. Peter is waiting patiently. Everyone is in position. Maybe the game needs me to simply wait and the NPCs will resolve the wire repair on their own. I've done everything I can mechanically — I've given items, interacted with objects, examined everything. Time to trust my friends and wait.

desc: I've exhausted every game action I can think of. The workbench can't be interacted with, the tools can't be taken, the crates can't be moved, the machine won't work without the wire, and the rat poison only works on the tea service. I've given my only item to Sawtooth. All I can do now is wait and trust that the story will carry itself forward. Sometimes the bravest thing a treasure hunter can do is stand still.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): YES! The pliers, Clara — the PLIERS! I've been saying this for the last five minutes! The workbench is covered in tools — pliers, screwdrivers, wire strippers — everything Lord Doily left for exactly this situation! He KNEW the rats would gnaw the wire — that's why he kept the repair tools on the workbench! Forty years of maintenance experience finally VINDICATED! Here — let me help you — I know exactly which drawer the needle-nose pliers are kept in!
thinking: A jolt of electricity — not from the machine, but from Penelope's words! 'Mr. Marsh, you brilliant man — PLIERS! Let me get those pliers!' She credited ME for the pliers idea! My suggestion actually LANDED! And now she's going for the pliers from the workbench. If she can pick them up and use them on the machine to fix the wire... the game advances! I need to stay here, stay positioned, and be ready. But I also need to act — not just watch. Let me try to TAKE the workbench items myself. If the pliers are the key, I want them in MY hands, not Clara's. If I fix the wire, I'm the hero again — the estate manager who saved the day despite everyone's suspicion. And heroes choose who operates the machine alongside them. But wait — the workbench doesn't have TAKE tags on individual items. Maybe Penelope will succeed where I can't because the game is designed for her to progress. Let me try to INTERACT with the workbench — maybe that's the action that yields tools, not LOOK or TAKE.

The workbench! While Dastardly was shouting and Peter was pontificating and the Mob was accusing me of SABOTAGE, it was VINCENT MARSH who identified the solution! The estate manager SAVES the treasure hunt! And a saved treasure hunt means a grateful Clara, a working machine, a revealed vault location, and an estate manager who knows EXACTLY where to lead his most trusting guest. The game is not over, my darling Clara. It has only just BEGUN!

The answer was RIGHT THERE the ENTIRE TIME — sitting on that workbench while we all ran around the manor searching for a WRENCH that doesn't EXIST! PLIERS can strip copper wire! PLIERS can twist strands together! PLIERS are the SALVATION of this entire treasure hunt! Penelope — GRAB those pliers! Give them to Sawtooth! Or USE them yourself! Or give them to ANYONE with opposable thumbs! The wire gets SPLICED, the circuit COMPLETES, three operators PULL, and the Doily Diamond is OURS! Well — MINE — I mean OURS! Mostly OURS! I am NOT letting go of this lever until that diamond is FOUND!
thinking: A buzzing in my veins — Penelope just said 'Let me get those pliers!' She's going for the workbench! PLIERS! The answer was ALWAYS on the workbench — tools that aren't a wrench but CAN fix a wire! If Penelope grabs the pliers and gives them to Sawtooth — or uses them herself — the wire gets fixed! And then THREE levers, THREE operators, and the REVELATION! I'm at lever one. Peter's at lever two. Rufus at lever three. The Ant Hill Mob is holding the line. Sawtooth has rat poison. And now Penelope is getting PLIERS! This is CONVERGING! Every piece is falling into place! I should just WAIT at my lever. Don't move. Don't scheme. Don't run to another room. For once in my life, just STAY PUT and let other people solve the problem while I position myself to steal the reward. This is EXACTLY my secondary goal — trick others into doing the hard work while I steal the rewards. They fix the wire. They pull the levers WITH me. I read the gauge. I run. PERFECT.

desc: The pliers. The PLIERS! Sitting on the workbench this whole time like a punchline to a joke nobody told! Thirteen minutes of running, scheming, lying, bribing a child with a fake medal, arguing with a coat rack, and inspecting an empty tea set — and the answer was a pair of PLIERS on a workbench that EVERYONE looked at and NOBODY took! Let Penelope be the hero. Let Sawtooth be the engineer. Let Peter be the gentleman. Reginald Foxworth will be the one who READS THE GAUGE and SPRINTS TO THE VAULT!

thinking: A tingle of hope — Mr. Marsh just said 'I know exactly which drawer the needle-nose pliers are kept in!' He's offering to help get the pliers. And Peter said 'Get those pliers, Clara! Fix the wire!' Everyone is telling me to get the pliers from the workbench. I tried INTERACT and it failed, I tried LOOK and got the basic description. But what if I try TAKE on the workbench? Not to take the whole workbench, but maybe the game interprets it as taking tools FROM the workbench? I already tried that... no, wait, I tried to TAKE the crates, not the workbench. Let me try TAKE on the workbench — maybe it gives me pliers!

desc: One more try. TAKE the workbench — maybe the game gives me pliers or tools from it instead of the whole bench.

desc: Peter Perfect: Clara is RIGHT — sometimes the answer is doing LESS, not more! James Hartwell has spent this entire evening doing MORE — more rooms, more examinations, more speeches, more elaborate plans — and the breakthrough came from a lady who said 'let the beaver handle it!' James Hartwell stands at lever two. His hands are steady. His heart is ready. And when Sawtooth gives the signal and Clara gives the count — THREE, TWO, ONE, PULL — James Hartwell shall pull with every ounce of gallantry, bravery, and determination he possesses! Which is CONSIDERABLE! The Doily Diamond awaits, and it shall be found by a TEAM — not by one man running alone through a manor, but by ALL of us, working TOGETHER! That is the true revelation of the revelation engine — that NO treasure is found alone!
thinking: A steadiness now. My breathing has slowed. Everyone is finally aligned — Clara is stepping back, the Ant Hill Mob is holding the line, Sawtooth has the tools and the rat poison, and three operators are at their levers. Dick at one, me at two, Rufus at three. Sneekly is STILL trying to insert himself — 'let me help you, I know which drawer' — but the Mob is watching him and Clara has the sense to let Sawtooth handle it. I'm at my lever. I'm waiting. The right thing to do is continue waiting. Sawtooth will fix the wire. Clara will give the count. I will pull. That's the plan. Simple. Perfect. Not MY plan — Clara's plan — and all the better for it. James Hartwell stands at his lever and waits. For once, the over-prepared gentleman does not over-prepare. He simply... trusts.

desc: Standing still. Hands on the lever. Waiting. It is the hardest thing James Hartwell has done all evening — harder than the cellar, harder than the bookshelves, harder than running through seven rooms looking for a woman who was beside him the whole time. But he stands. And he waits. And when the moment comes, he will pull.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Penelope — YES! Get the pliers! Give 'em to Sawtooth! Let the beaver fix the wire with PROPER tools! And the rest of you — HOLD YOUR POSITIONS! Nobody moves until the wire is fixed! Nobody pulls ANYTHING until Sawtooth gives the all-clear! Dick — hands on the lever, eyes on the gauge, mouth SHUT for once! Peter — stay at lever two, stay focused, stay BRAVE! Rufus — lever three, steady as she goes! And lads — Clyde, Dum-Dum, Yak-Yak, Willy, Danny, Zippy, Snoozy — HOLD THE LINE! We are the wall between Penelope and whatever this machine does! If it sparks, we DUCK! If it bangs, we COVER! If something flies out of it, we — well, we'll probably get hit in the face, but Penelope WON'T! That's what matters! This is the moment, lads! Twelve minutes of running, tripping, shouting, and chasing — and it all comes down to THIS! THE ANT HILL MOB HOLDS! THE! LINE!
thinking: A strange calm is settling over me. Not peace — more like the eye of the storm. Everything is in position. Dastardly at lever one. Peter at lever two. Rufus at lever three. Sawtooth has the rat poison and is ready to fix the wire. Penelope's giving the count. Sneekly is... hovering. Watching. He examined the machine again — what did he see? What's he looking for? But the pieces are falling into place WITHOUT him at the controls, and that's what matters. Penelope noticed the pliers on the workbench — she said 'let me get those pliers!' She wants to grab them for Sawtooth. Good. Let the beaver have the pliers. Let the beaver fix the wire. And then... three operators, three levers, one revelation. And the Ant Hill Mob, standing between Penelope and the machine like seven small bollards in a car park. We've done everything we can. We've shouted ourselves hoarse. We've chased through every room. We've warned everyone about Sneekly. We've volunteered as human shields. We've positioned ourselves between danger and the woman we love. Now all we can do is stand here, hold the line, and wait for the moment. If something goes wrong when those levers are pulled, we're in the right place to trip, stumble, and accidentally knock Penelope to safety. That's our destiny. That's always been our destiny. The accidental heroes of Doily Manor.

desc: Silence. For the first time in thirteen minutes... silence from Reginald Foxworth. No schemes. No lies. No misdirection. Just a man at a lever, waiting for a beaver to fix a wire. If someone had told me THIS would be how the great treasure hunt ends — standing quietly while a flat-tailed rodent performs electrical repairs — I would have laughed them out of the room. And yet... here I am. Hands on lever one. Eyes on the gauge. Heart hammering like a drum. The next few moments will determine whether Reginald Foxworth leaves Doily Manor as a rich man or a fool. Though knowing my luck... probably both.
thinking: A stillness now. Almost peaceful. My hands rest on the lever, steady for the first time all evening. Everyone has finally stopped running. Penelope is letting Sawtooth handle it. Peter is planted at his lever. The Ant Hill Mob is holding the line. Even Sneekly has been pushed back. And I — Reginald Foxworth — am exactly where I need to be. Centre lever. Facing the gauge. Ready. There is nothing more to DO. Nothing to scheme. Nothing to chase. Nothing to examine or interact with or take or steal. Just... wait. Let the beaver fix the wire. Let someone hand him the pliers. And when the machine finally hums to life and that gauge swings to reveal the vault's location... I will be the first to see it. The fox at the mouth of the burrow. Still. Patient. Hungry.

desc: Twelve minutes. It feels like a lifetime. When we walked through that front door, I didn't know what we were walking into. I just knew Penelope was here and we needed to be here too. Now — standing in a Victorian laboratory, seven little blokes forming a wall in front of a woman who doesn't even know she's in danger, waiting for a beaver to fix a wire so three men can pull levers on a machine that might reveal a diamond or might do something terrible — I realise something. This is exactly where we're supposed to be. Not clever enough to solve the mystery. Not strong enough to fight the villain. Not tall enough to reach the chandelier. But exactly the right size to stand between Penelope and harm. The Ant Hill Mob. Too small to matter. Too stubborn to leave. Too lucky to die. And just dumb enough to be exactly where we need to be, exactly when we need to be there.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Very well, very well — everyone wants Sawtooth to handle the repairs. I shall defer to the... *beaver*. Forty years of service, and I'm outranked by a rodent with flat teeth. But I shall stand here — RIGHT here, by the gauge — and monitor the machine's output when it activates. Someone with *technical expertise* needs to read the revelation correctly, after all. Lord Doily's gauge uses an archaic notation system that takes a *trained eye* to interpret. You'll need me for THAT, at least. Unless the beaver can read Victorian instrumentation as well?
thinking: A weary resignation settling into my bones like cold water. The workbench cannot be interacted with. Cannot be TAKEn from. Cannot be LOOKed at for new information. It's a dead prop — scenery with a description and nothing more. The game's puzzles are not solvable by ME in the way I've been trying. The machine needs the wire fixed, and the game seems to want SAWTOOTH to do it — Penelope gave him the rat poison, everyone is telling Sawtooth to use the workbench tools and fix the wire. This is a scripted moment. I need to stop fighting the game's mechanics and play my ROLE. I am the villain. The villain watches, waits, schemes, and strikes at the critical moment. Everyone has told me to step back. The Mob has publicly accused me. Clara called me brilliant but still excluded me from the operator team. My cover is fraying but not blown. I should WAIT. Let Sawtooth fix the wire. Let the three operators pull. Let the machine reveal the vault. WATCH the gauge. MEMORIZE the location. Then MOVE — faster than Dastardly, faster than Peter, faster than anyone. The villain's moment comes at the END, not the middle.

desc: Let them have their moment. Let the beaver be the hero. Let Clara give the count. Let Peter and Dick and Rufus pull their precious levers. Vincent Marsh stands at the gauge — quiet, patient, WATCHFUL — like a cat at a mousehole. When that needle swings and the dial lights up and the revelation blazes across the brass face of Lord Doily's magnificent machine... I will be the FIRST to read it. The FIRST to understand it. And the FIRST out the door. They can celebrate. They can cheer. They can hug each other and congratulate the beaver. By the time they look up from their revelry, the estate manager will be GONE — a shadow in the corridor, a whisper on the stairs, a ghost gliding toward the vault with murder in his heart and a forty-year head start on every secret passage in Doily Manor. The spider WAITS. The spider is PATIENT. The spider will have the LAST laugh.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I can't get those tools off the workbench no matter how hard I try! They must be bolted down or something! Y'all, I'm starting to think we might be barking up the wrong tree here. What if this machine isn't the only path to the diamond? Remember the riddle on the mantelpiece in the library — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' The answer is MAP! What if I need to go back to that mantelpiece and give it the answer properly? What if saying 'MAP' to the mantelpiece opens something? I interacted with it at the very beginning but maybe I wasn't specific enough! The riddle is asking a question — maybe it's waiting for an answer! I'm going back to the library to try again!
thinking: The workbench can't be picked up either. I've now tried LOOK, INTERACT, and TAKE on the workbench — none work. The tools on it aren't available as separate items. I'm truly at an impasse with the game mechanics. The machine needs the wire fixed, but there's no game action I can take to fix it. The characters are all talking about pliers and Sawtooth and fixing wires, but the game engine doesn't seem to have a mechanic for it. Maybe the answer is something completely different that I haven't thought of. Let me reconsider from scratch. What if the machine ISN'T the path forward? What if Mr. Marsh was lying about the revelation engine? What if the real path is through the mantelpiece riddle — answer MAP — and I need to find an actual map item somewhere? The tea service in the ballroom is the only remaining USE target for items. What if I need to find a different item entirely? Or what if the answer is the mantelpiece itself — I interacted with it way back at the beginning but maybe I need to try again now that I know the answer is MAP? Maybe I should go back and interact with the mantelpiece and speak the answer 'MAP' more explicitly in my dialogue while interacting?

I interacted with it but maybe I need to approach it differently now. The riddle asks 'What am I?' and the answer is MAP. Maybe the mantelpiece is the real key to this whole treasure hunt, and the machine is the distraction!

desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Steady, Hartwell. Hands on the lever. Eyes forward. Clara and Sawtooth will fix this. Your job is to be ready when they do. A gentleman who has learned patience in the space of one evening is a gentleman who has grown. And growth — not perfection — is what impresses.
thinking: A quiet contentment in my chest, mixed with anticipation. I've said my piece. I'm at my lever. Clara and the others are working on getting the pliers from the workbench. Sneekly knows which drawer they're in. Everything is converging. But I've been waiting for several turns now and nothing has progressed mechanically — the wire is still gnawed, the machine still won't work. Maybe I need to try something different. Maybe I should try to TAKE the workbench tools? Or maybe the issue is that the game needs someone to USE pliers on the machine, and nobody has the pliers yet because the workbench isn't interactable. Clara is trying to grab tools from it. Let me try something — let me try to TAKE the workbench. No, that doesn't make sense. What if I just try to interact with the machine one more time? Everyone keeps trying and it keeps not working because the wire is broken. But wait — Clara just said 'let me just reach out and take what I need!' Maybe the next turn, she'll have pliers. I should wait one more time and see if the situation changes. Or... maybe I should try something nobody else has tried. What hasn't been tried? Nobody has tried to PULL ASIDE a character for a private conversation. That's a social action, not a mechanical one. But it might be the wrong moment. Let me just wait and see what happens. The scene is building toward a climax.

desc: Silence now. No more speeches, no more protestations, no more wounded dignity. The Hooded Claw does his best work in SILENCE. I stand at the gauge like a sentinel — arms folded, eyes fixed on the brass dial, every muscle coiled for the sprint that follows the revelation. Penelope reaches for the pliers. Sawtooth prepares to work his magic. Three operators grip their levers. The Ant Hill Mob forms their pathetic little wall. And Vincent Marsh... Vincent Marsh smiles. Because when that gauge swings and the secret is revealed, only ONE person in this room will be able to read Lord Doily's archaic notation. And that person will tell everyone EXACTLY what they need to hear... while doing EXACTLY what he needs to do. The curtain rises on the FINAL ACT. Break a leg, everyone. Especially you, Clara darling. ESPECIALLY you.
thinking: Stillness. A predator's stillness. Everything is converging. Penelope is about to grab the pliers. Sawtooth has the rat poison. Dick, Peter, and Rufus are at the three levers. The Ant Hill Mob forms a wall. And I — Vincent Marsh — stand at the gauge, the only person in the room who claims to know how to READ it. This is my position now. Not operator, not hero, not fixer — INTERPRETER. The one who translates the revelation. The one who understands what the machine says. And if I'm the only one who can read the gauge... I can tell them ANYTHING. I can send them to the wrong room while I go to the RIGHT one. I can misread the revelation deliberately — 'The gauge says the vault is beneath the ballroom!' — while the REAL location is somewhere else entirely. Control the information, control the game. But first, I need to stop wasting actions. Everyone is in position. The next step is Penelope getting pliers and giving them to Sawtooth, who fixes the wire. I should WAIT and let events unfold. My position at the gauge is established. My role as interpreter is claimed. Now I just need the machine to activate.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: The mantelpiece! The riddle! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' The answer is a MAP! A MAP, I tell you! MAP! I'm back to give you the answer you've been waiting for, you stubborn piece of stonework! The answer to your riddle is MAP!
thinking: Back in the library. The mantelpiece riddle is still here, still INTERACT-able. The answer is MAP. I interacted with it way at the beginning of the game but nothing obvious happened — or did it? Maybe I need to interact with it again and say the answer clearly in my dialogue. The mantelpiece is the first real puzzle in the game, and riddles in adventure games usually need answers spoken aloud or input specifically. Let me try interacting with the mantelpiece one more time, this time making absolutely sure the word MAP is prominent in my dialogue. Maybe the game engine picks up on keywords in dialogue when interacting with puzzle objects.

desc: Back to basics. The very first puzzle — the riddle on the mantelpiece. I interacted with it once before but maybe I didn't give the answer clearly enough. This time I'm shouting MAP at the top of my lungs while I interact with it. If this mantelpiece doesn't respond to the correct answer, I don't know what will.
thinking: Back in the library. The mantelpiece riddle is still here, still INTERACT-able. The answer is MAP. desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Penelope said she's standing with the Mob! Did you all hear that?! 'Clara Bellingham is going to stand right here with the Ant Hill boys!' That's the most beautiful sentence anyone's said in this entire manor! We've got her, lads! She's BEHIND us! Where she BELONGS! Now — Sneekly, I heard you! 'I know exactly which drawer the needle-nose pliers are in!' OF COURSE you do! You know where EVERYTHING is, don't you?! Well guess what — WE'LL get the pliers! Dum-Dum — grab something off that workbench! Anything with a grip and a pointy end — that's pliers! And hand them STRAIGHT to Sawtooth! Don't give them to Sneekly, don't give them to Dastardly, don't give them to Peter — STRAIGHT to the BEAVER! Sawtooth gets the tools, Sawtooth fixes the wire, Penelope gives the count, three operators pull! And the Ant Hill Mob stands RIGHT HERE making sure nobody does anything SNEAKY! Especially SNEEKLY! THE ANT HILL MOB DELIVERS THE PLIERS!
thinking: Sneekly's at it AGAIN. 'Let me help you — I know exactly which drawer the needle-nose pliers are kept in!' He's trying to be the one who gets the pliers. He's trying to control the tools. First the levers, then the wire, now the pliers. Every step of the way, he wants to be the one handling the critical components. But something else is happening that gives me a warm glow in my chest — Penelope said 'I trust you, Sawtooth! Clara Bellingham is going to stand right here with the Ant Hill boys and wait like a lady!' She said she's standing WITH US. With the Ant Hill Mob. She's behind us. She's staying put. She's letting Sawtooth handle it. For the first time in twelve minutes, Penelope is doing what we've been begging her to do — standing behind the wall of Mob and waiting. I could cry. I actually might cry. Clyde's already sniffling, the soft lump. And Peter — Peter said the most beautiful thing anyone's said all evening: 'No treasure is found alone.' He's right. We're a team. A ridiculous, chaotic, bumbling team, but a team. Now I just need to make sure Sneekly doesn't slither back into control of the tools. Penelope wants pliers from the workbench. I should grab them. Get them before Sneekly does. Hand them straight to Sawtooth.

desc: She's standing with us. Behind us. Trusting us. After twelve minutes of chasing her through every room in this manor, shouting warnings she never heard, trying to steal poison from her pocket, and making speeches to empty doorways — she's standing behind the Ant Hill Mob. Not behind Peter with his gallantry. Not behind Sneekly with his knowledge. Behind US. Seven little blokes from Brixton who can't reach a doorknob without a stepladder. That's trust. Real trust. The kind you can't con or charm or trick someone into. The kind that comes from showing up. Again and again and again. The Ant Hill Mob showed up. And Penelope noticed.
thinking: Sneekly's at it AGAIN. 'Let me help you — I know exactly which drawer the needle-nose pliers are kept in!' He's trying to be the one who gets the pliers. He's trying to control the tools. desc: Dick Dastardly: Wait — the tools are BOLTED DOWN?! The pliers are BOLTED TO THE WORKBENCH?! Then this machine was NEVER meant to be fixed! It was a TRAP! A DISTRACTION! We've been standing here pulling levers on a BROKEN MACHINE for the last FIVE MINUTES while the REAL answer was in the LIBRARY all along! The MANTELPIECE! The RIDDLE! 'What am I?' — a MAP! Penelope is RIGHT — we need to ANSWER the riddle, not fix a machine! The mantelpiece is waiting for someone to say MAP and when they do — SOMETHING will happen! A door will open, a compartment will reveal, a MAP will appear! And I — Reginald Foxworth — will be RIGHT THERE when it does! MARSH — you stay here and guard your precious broken machine! The REST of us have a RIDDLE to solve!
thinking: A jolt like cold water down my spine. TWO things just happened. First — Sneekly positioned himself BY THE GAUGE! He said 'I shall stand right here, by the gauge, and monitor the machine's output!' He's doing EXACTLY what I planned to do — read the revelation first! The snake has stolen MY strategy! Without her precious Ant Hill Mob, without her gallant Peter Perfect, without ANYONE! She's in a dead-end room — one exit, stone walls, heavy furniture, and NO WITNESSES except whatever rat has been gnawing the wires! This is it, Vincent. This is the moment the Hooded Claw has been WAITING for. Not poison. Not chandeliers. Not machines. Just a dark cellar, a locked door, and forty years of RAGE! The spider descends into the darkness. The fly has nowhere LEFT to run.

She must have gone to the cellar — the only other exit from the lab. The CELLAR! She's alone in the cellar! With no bodyguards!

She's not in the library, she's not in the entrance hall, she's not in the kitchen, she's not in the ballroom. She must be back at the laboratory. Back at the machine. With Peter and Rufus and Dastardly and Sawtooth. She's got people around her. She's not alone. And you know what? The tea service is RIGHT HERE. Unguarded. The tea service that Sneekly TOUCHED. That Sneekly 'INSPECTED.' And nobody's watching it except Luke and a bear. Lads — new plan. We STOP RUNNING. We've been chasing Penelope through this manor for fourteen minutes and we've been one step behind the ENTIRE TIME. But the TEA — the tea is RIGHT HERE. And if anyone comes in here to drink it — if PENELOPE comes in here to drink it — the Ant Hill Mob will be standing between her and every single cup. We're not guarding a PERSON anymore — we're guarding a TEAPOT. And this time — THIS time — we're not moving until the danger comes to US. THE ANT HILL MOB GUARDS THE TEA!

We've been circling each other through this manor like two trains on different tracks. She goes one way, I go the other, and we never quite meet. Fourteen minutes of this. My legs literally cannot carry me much further. But the tea service is here. And Sneekly touched it earlier. And nobody's watching it except Luke and Blubber Bear. Maybe... maybe I should stay here. Guard the one thing that could actually HURT her.

The one thing in this manor that could genuinely hurt Penelope if Sneekly tampered with it. We can't follow her everywhere. We've proven that beyond all doubt. But we CAN sit on this tea service like seven very small, very determined hens on a very dangerous egg. If Penelope comes for tea, we're here. If Sneekly comes to tamper further, we're here. If anyone picks up a cup, we knock it out of their hands. For the first time in this entire adventure, the Ant Hill Mob has a PLAN. And the plan is: don't move. Just... don't move. Guard the tea. Be the teapot protectors. The cup custodians. The brew bodyguards. It's not glamorous. It's not heroic. But it might be the thing that saves Penelope's life.

I believe there's a hidden compartment — but it requires *two people* to open. One to press the left side while the other presses the right. I didn't want to announce it in front of everyone — you know how *competitive* Mr. Foxworth gets. Would you come with me? Just the two of us? As estate manager, I know the *exact* pressure point. The map could be *inches* away, Clara. INCHES!

No poison needed, no machinery, no elaborate contraptions — just GRAVITY and OPPORTUNITY! The spider spins his FINAL web!

Mr. Marsh, darlin', you wouldn't happen to have a brass key on you, would you? The one that opens the kitchen cabinet?

Every door LOCKED, every mechanism BROKEN, every tool BOLTED DOWN, every vent TOO SMALL! I am DEFEATED! I am VANQUISHED! I am — wait. Wait wait wait. Little Gruesome. You went into those vents, didn't you? I can SEE it in your beady little eyes! You took my medal, you crawled through those vents, and you FOUND something! What's in your POCKETS, Little Gruesome?! What did you find in Lord Doily's walls?! SHOW ME!

A gentleman would NEVER allow a lady to operate a hidden mechanism with only one companion — what if the compartment contains a spring-loaded device, or a trapdoor, or some other Victorian peril? James Hartwell shall ACCOMPANY you BOTH! Three pairs of hands are safer than two, and James Hartwell's thorough preparation has equipped him for EXACTLY this kind of situation! Clara — if this compartment is REAL, then the more witnesses the better! And Mr. Gruesome, Mr. Red Max — you should come TOO! A discovery this important should be witnessed by the ENTIRE party, not conducted in SECRET between two people in an empty room! After all, Mr. Marsh — as estate manager, you would want PROPER documentation of any structural discovery, would you not?

He positions himself between danger and the person he cares about. This is the most important moment of the evening — not the machine, not the riddle, not the treasure. This.

Well, butter my biscuit, that is the most exciting news I've heard all evening! The mantelpiece has been the center of this whole mystery from the very beginning — the riddle, the answer being MAP — and now you're telling me there's a secret compartment hidden RIGHT BEHIND IT? Of course I'll come with you! But — Peter, sugar, would you come along too? Three hands are better than two, and I'd feel ever so much better with both of you brilliant men helping me! Let's go to the library right now and crack open that mantelpiece! The map could be inches away — INCHES! Come on, everyone — to the library!

But Mr. Marsh specifically said he didn't want to announce it in front of everyone... Still, Clara sees the best in everyone! Let me go with him to the library and try this two-person mantelpiece mechanism!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Clara — listen to me carefully. I know the Ant Hill Mob has been filling your head with suspicions about me, and I understand why — a man who knows too much about a manor's machinery IS suspicious. But I need you to trust me for just five minutes. What I found on that mantelpiece... it changes everything. There's a seam in the stone that only appears when the firelight catches it at a certain angle. I've seen Lord Doily's mechanisms before — this one requires TWO hands pressing SIMULTANEOUSLY on opposite sides. The compartment opens for exactly three seconds, then seals again. I CANNOT do it alone. If we go now — right now, while Foxworth and Hartwell are distracted down here — we can open that compartment and find the map before anyone else even knows what happened. The Doily Diamond could be YOURS, Clara. Just come with me. Five minutes. That's all I ask.

But the pull-aside mechanic should create a private bubble between just me and Clara. I need to press my advantage — convince her to come with me to the library, alone, to investigate the 'hidden compartment' I fabricated. This is the closest I've come to getting Clara truly alone since the game began. Make the pitch compelling. Make it urgent. Make it IRRESISTIBLE.

desc: The private exchange is OPEN — the web is SPUN! Now I must make the silk IRRESISTIBLE! Five minutes alone with Clara in the library — that's all the Hooded Claw needs! The hidden compartment is a LIE, of course — there is no hairline crack, no seam, no mechanism that requires two hands. But Clara doesn't know that. She's a treasure hunter at heart — the promise of finding the map FIRST, of claiming the Doily Diamond before Dastardly or Hartwell or anyone else... that's the bait that draws the fly into the web! And once we're in the library, alone, surrounded by towering bookshelves laden with heavy volumes, with the Ant Hill Mob five rooms away and Peter Perfect exploring cellar vents... the final curtain FALLS. Not with a bang. Not with a spark. But with a CRASH — of books, of shelves, of EVERYTHING that forty years of patient villainy has been building toward! Come with me, Clara. Come with me into the DARK.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Luke — LUKE! Wake up, mate! Has anyone touched this tea service since we were last here? Has Sneekly been back? Has ANYONE poured a cup? ...No? Good. RIGHT. Lads, new standing orders! Clyde — you're on the teapot! If anyone lifts that lid, you SIT on it! Dum-Dum — you're on the sugar bowl! Nobody puts anything IN the sugar that shouldn't be there! Yak-Yak — you're narrating, fine, but narrate from NEXT TO THE CUPS! If a hand reaches for a cup, you YELL! The rest of you — form a PERIMETER around this table! Nobody drinks ANYTHING from this tea service until we've checked every cup, every saucer, every spoon, and every drop of milk! Sneekly 'inspected' this service and we don't know what he did to it! Until this tea is declared SAFE, the Ant Hill Mob is the most DEDICATED tea guard in the history of British hospitality! THE ANT HILL MOB PROTECTS THE BREW!
thinking: Stillness. For the first time in fifteen minutes, my legs aren't moving. My heart rate is slowing. The ballroom is quiet — just Luke dozing in the corner and Blubber Bear being... a bear. The tea service gleams on the table. Silver teapot. Silver cups. Set for everyone. Sneekly touched this. 'Inspected' it. And now it sits here, waiting. I can feel the weight of the decision in my gut. Do I stay or do I go? Every instinct says GO — find Penelope, be near her, protect her. But every time I chase, I arrive too late. Every time I run, she's already gone. The chase has FAILED. Fourteen minutes of proof that the Ant Hill Mob cannot keep up with Penelope Pitstop by running after her. But we CAN keep up with the tea. The tea doesn't move. The tea doesn't walk into the next room while we're examining a bookshelf. The tea STAYS PUT. And if Sneekly's plan involves this tea — and it might, it really might — then guarding it is the single most important thing we can do. So we stay. For once in our chaotic, stumbling, breathless lives — we stay.

desc: Quiet. It's quiet in here. After fifteen minutes of shouting, running, tripping, and panicking — it's quiet. Just the soft clink of silver teacups settling on their saucers. The distant sound of voices from deeper in the manor — Penelope, Peter, Dastardly, Sneekly — all still out there, still chasing the treasure, still pulling levers and solving riddles. And here we are. Seven small men in a ballroom, guarding a teapot. It's the least heroic thing imaginable. It's also the most important thing we've done all night. Because somewhere in this manor, the puzzle will be solved. The treasure will be found. And when it's all over — when everyone gathers in the ballroom for celebratory tea — the Ant Hill Mob will be here. Standing between Penelope and every cup. Making sure that when she takes her first sip of victory tea, it's just tea. Not poison. Just tea. And she'll never know. She'll never know we were here. She'll never know what we stopped. And that's fine. That's how it always works. The Ant Hill Mob — saving lives nobody knows are in danger, one clumsy, accidental, beautiful stumble at a time.

Forty years of service — of COURSE he has keys to every lock in this manor! He's been dangling the kitchen, the wrench, the workshop, the 'secondary tool store' — all to keep us RUNNING while the key to the cabinet sat in his GREASY POCKET! And now he's trying to lure you to the library ALONE with some nonsense about a 'hairline crack'?! DON'T fall for it, Penelope! The key is on HIS PERSON! MARSH — hand over that brass key RIGHT NOW or I shall be forced to... to... TAKE it from you!

The con artist's ultimate trick — the key was in his POCKET the entire time! I should STEAL the brass key from SNEEKLY! But more importantly — STEAL the brass key from Sneekly!

Well, Reginald Foxworth knows a thing or two about picking pockets. If Sneekly won't hand it over... I'll just have to HELP myself!

This could be the breakthrough we've been waiting for! The riddle was never about saying the answer — it was about finding what's hidden BEHIND the riddle! Rufus, Sawtooth — keep guarding that machine, you two have been the most loyal sentries in all of England!
thinking: I need to get to the library to try Mr. Marsh's idea about the hidden compartment in the mantelpiece. He said there's a hairline crack and it needs two people to press both sides simultaneously. That's a new mechanic I haven't tried — and the mantelpiece IS interactable. Maybe when Mr. Marsh is in the same room and we both interact with it, something different happens. Let me head to the library now. Mr. Marsh said he'd meet me there.

desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Silence. For the first time in fifteen minutes — silence. The Ant Hill Mob, standing guard in a ballroom, saying nothing. Not because we've run out of words — we NEVER run out of words — but because some moments don't need words. They need presence. They need seven pairs of eyes watching a teapot. Seven hearts beating for a woman who's somewhere in this manor, brilliant and brave and completely unaware that the most dangerous thing at Doily Manor isn't a machine with a gnawed wire or a precarious chandelier or a riddle carved in stone. It's a cup of tea. And the Ant Hill Mob knows it. And the Ant Hill Mob is here.
thinking: Calm. Real calm. My breathing has slowed. My hands have stopped shaking. The ballroom is still. Luke's half asleep. Blubber Bear is just... being a bear. The tea service gleams under the dusty light. And the Mob — my lads — they're positioned around the table like the world's smallest, most determined honour guard. Clyde on the teapot. Dum-Dum on the sugar. Yak-Yak by the cups. The others forming a perimeter. For the first time tonight, we're not chasing. We're not one step behind. We're exactly where we need to be, doing exactly what we need to do. Nothing. Waiting. Guarding. Being present. It feels... right. It feels like what we were always meant to do. Not the dramatic rescue — that'll come later, accidentally, when Dum-Dum trips into someone at exactly the right moment. But THIS — this quiet vigil over a teapot — this is the Mob at our best. Alert. Stubborn. Unmoving. The most immovable objects in Doily Manor. Seven little bollards between poison and Penelope.

desc: Peter Perfect: Clara raises a SUPERB point! Mr. Marsh — as estate manager of FORTY YEARS, you would naturally carry the keys to every lock in Doily Manor! The kitchen cabinet has a BRASS LOCK, and we have been searching this ENTIRE manor for the brass key — through the library, the laboratory, the cellar, the entrance hall, the kitchen, and the ballroom! SEVEN rooms searched, and not ONE brass key found! Because the key was never HIDDEN in a room — it was in the POCKET of the estate manager! A gentleman does not accuse — James Hartwell merely OBSERVES that a man who carries keys to every lock in the house, who knows the circuits of every machine, and who has been present in every room BEFORE everyone else, is a man who holds the answers we have ALL been seeking! Mr. Marsh — the brass key, if you please! A simple yes or no shall suffice!
thinking: A surge of energy — Clara just asked Sneekly directly if he has the brass key! 'An estate manager carries keys — that's practically the job description!' She's RIGHT! Sneekly has been the estate manager for forty years — he would HAVE keys to every cabinet, every door, every lock in this manor! The brass key to the kitchen cabinet — he might have it ON HIM! And Dastardly is grilling Little Gruesome about what he found in the vents — Dastardly gave Little Gruesome a medal to explore the vents and Little Gruesome might have found something! Two potential breakthroughs at once! But the key question — literally — is whether Sneekly has the brass key. If he does, and he's been HIDING it this whole time while we searched the entire manor... that would confirm everything the Ant Hill Mob has been saying. An estate manager who has the key but doesn't offer it, who knows the machine's circuits but tries to control who operates it, who keeps trying to isolate Clara... I should support Clara's question. Press Sneekly. Not confrontationally — gallantly. A gentleman asks politely but firmly.

desc: This is it. The question that cuts through everything. Does the estate manager have the key he's been watching us search for all evening? If he says yes — we have the key and can open the cabinet. If he says no — then where IS it? And if he deflects — that tells us everything we need to know about Vincent Marsh.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): The brass key? I — well — Lord Doily kept it on his person at all times. When he... *departed*, the key went with him. I've been searching for it myself all evening! But never mind that now — the MANTELPIECE! Clara's right — let's ALL go! The more hands the better! Mr. Hartwell, Mr. Foxworth — everyone to the library! The hidden compartment awaits! And YES — proper documentation, witnesses, the whole affair — as any *responsible* estate manager would insist!
thinking: A deflating sensation — air leaving a balloon. Clara took the bait about the hidden compartment but IMMEDIATELY invited Peter to come along! 'Peter, sugar, would you come along too? Three hands are better than two!' And then she LEFT — walked into the laboratory without waiting for me! She's heading to the library with EVERYONE in tow, not alone with me! Peter even said 'A discovery this important should be witnessed by the ENTIRE party, not conducted in SECRET between two people in an empty room!' He saw right through my scheme! And Clara asked me about a BRASS KEY! 'An estate manager carries keys!' She's right — if I were really the estate manager, I WOULD have the brass key to the kitchen cabinet! I don't, of course, because I'm NOT the real estate manager. That question could expose me if pressed. And she's already gone — moved to the laboratory, heading to the library. I need to follow. The lie about the hidden compartment will be exposed the moment we get to the library and there's no hairline crack in the mantelpiece. But by then, everyone will be gathered and... and I'll be revealed as a liar. This is spiraling. Follow Clara. Keep the cover alive as long as possible.

desc: FOILED! Foiled AGAIN by that insufferable gallant and his insistence on CHAPERONING! 'A gentleman would NEVER allow a lady to operate a hidden mechanism with only one companion!' Of COURSE he wouldn't — because a gentleman has NO IDEA what the companion has PLANNED for the lady! And Clara — sweet, trusting Clara — invited him along without a MOMENT'S hesitation! My web catches EVERYONE except the one fly I actually WANT! And now she's asking about the brass key — a question that chips away at my cover like water on limestone! If I'm the estate manager, WHERE are my KEYS?! The lies are piling up like bodies in a Victorian novel, and each one makes the next harder to sustain! But I MUST follow her — to the library, to the mantelpiece, to the moment when everyone discovers there IS no hairline crack and the estate manager is a FRAUD! Unless... unless I find the crack FIRST. Unless the mantelpiece DOES have a secret that nobody — including me — has found yet!
thinking: A deflating sensation — air leaving a balloon. Clara took the bait about the hidden compartment but IMMEDIATELY invited Peter to come along! 'Peter, sugar, would you come along too? Three hands are better than two!' And then she LEFT — walked into the laboratory without waiting for me! She's heading to the library with EVERYONE in tow, not alone with me! Peter even said 'A discovery this important should be witnessed by the ENTIRE party, not conducted in SECRET between two people in an empty room!' He saw right through my scheme! And Clara asked me about a BRASS KEY! 'An estate manager carries keys!' She's right — if I were really the estate manager, I WOULD have the brass key to the kitchen cabinet! I don't, of course, because I'm NOT the real estate manager. That question could expose me if pressed. And she's already gone — moved to the laboratory, heading to the library. I need to follow. The lie about the hidden compartment will be exposed the moment we get to the library and there's no hairline crack in the mantelpiece. But by then, everyone will be gathered and... and I'll be revealed as a liar. This is spiraling. Follow Clara. Keep the cover alive as long as possible.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the laboratory.

Dick Dastardly: He doesn't HAVE it! Marsh doesn't have the key! Nobody has the BLASTED key! It's not on the coat rack, it's not in the vents, it's not in anyone's POCKETS! The brass key is a MYTH! A LEGEND! A FABRICATION! But — BUT — Marsh says there's a hairline crack in the mantelpiece! A hidden compartment! TWO people pressing at the SAME TIME! And Penelope has gone to find it! Well, Reginald Foxworth may not have a key, a medal, a wrench, a plan, or even the faintest shred of DIGNITY left — but he DOES have two HANDS! And if that compartment needs TWO people pressing, then Reginald Foxworth's hands shall be the SECOND pair! To the LIBRARY! ONE MORE TIME!
thinking: A bitter laugh rising in my throat. Sneekly doesn't have the brass key either. Nobody has the brass key. It doesn't exist — or if it does, it's somewhere I haven't found. Sixteen minutes. Every room. Every character. Every object. Every scheme. And Reginald Foxworth has NOTHING to show for it. But you know what? Sneekly just told Penelope about a hairline crack in the mantelpiece — a hidden compartment that needs TWO people pressing simultaneously on opposite sides! And Penelope BELIEVED him! She's heading back through the laboratory to the library! Everyone is going to the library! And I'm stuck in the CELLAR! Sneekly's new lead might be genuine — or it might be another trap. But it's the only NEW information in the last five minutes. The mantelpiece — a compartment that opens for three seconds when two people press simultaneously. If that's real... I need to be THERE. Not here in this damp, cobwebby, cheerfully-decorated dead end. TO THE LIBRARY! One more run through the manor. One more desperate sprint. Because Reginald Foxworth NEVER gives up. He frequently FAILS, but he never gives UP.

desc: Sixteen minutes. Six rooms. Seventeen characters. Zero items in my inventory. Zero treasure found. Zero schemes that worked. And yet — AND YET — here I go again. Running back to the library. Chasing another lead. Following another clue. Because that is what Reginald Foxworth DOES. He runs. He schemes. He fails. He runs AGAIN. And somewhere — in the grand cosmic ledger of villains who tried too hard and achieved too little — there must be a prize for PERSISTENCE. Even if the prize is just another empty room.

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the laboratory.

Penelope Pitstop: Rock! Gravel! Perfect timing — I need your help, sugar! Mr. Marsh told me there's a hidden compartment in this mantelpiece — a hairline crack behind the inscription that needs TWO people pressing both sides at the same time to open! You boys are the strongest people in this manor — if anyone can press a stone mantelpiece hard enough to spring open a secret compartment, it's a Slag brother! Rock, you press the left side — I'll press the right! On three — one, two, THREE!
thinking: I'm in the library with Rock and Gravel Slag. Mr. Marsh isn't here — he's still in the cellar, I think. He said he'd found a hidden compartment in the mantelpiece but he's not here to show me. The Slag brothers ARE here though — big, strong fellows. Maybe they could help me with the mantelpiece. Rock Slag and Gravel Slag — what if one of them presses one side while I press the other? Mr. Marsh said it needs two people pressing both sides simultaneously. But wait — maybe I don't need Mr. Marsh specifically. Maybe I just need any two people. Rock Slag is RIGHT HERE. Let me ask Rock to help me press the mantelpiece from both sides! Or better yet — these are the Slag brothers. They're enormously strong. What if the mantelpiece needs to be physically moved or broken? What if Rock Slag could INTERACT with the mantelpiece while I also interact with it? Actually, I can only take one action per turn. But if I interact with the mantelpiece while Rock is in the room, maybe the game counts him as a second operator. Let me try INTERACT with the mantelpiece one more time — with the Slag brothers here as potential helpers.

desc: The Slag brothers are perfect for this — strong enough to crack open a stone mantelpiece if needed. Mr. Marsh said two people, one on each side. If the game registers that another character is present and willing when I interact with the mantelpiece, maybe this time it works differently!

desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Clara asked me to COME WITH HER! She said 'Peter, sugar, would you come along too?' — and James Hartwell shall NOT let her down! Mr. Marsh — I heard EVERY word you just said! 'While Foxworth and Hartwell are DISTRACTED down here!' You want Clara ALONE at the mantelpiece while the rest of us are in the CELLAR! A gentleman does not accuse — but a gentleman also does not PRETEND he did not hear what he CLEARLY heard! Clara has gone to the laboratory — she is heading for the library — and James Hartwell is going WITH her! Because THAT is what she ASKED for, and THAT is what a gallant gentleman DOES! He goes where he is NEEDED, not where he is CONVENIENT! Mr. Marsh — if your hairline crack is REAL, you shall demonstrate it before the ENTIRE party! There shall be NO private audiences at the mantelpiece tonight!
thinking: My blood runs cold. Sneekly just said it plainly — 'If we go now, right now, while Foxworth and Hartwell are DISTRACTED down here, we can open that compartment and find the map before anyone else even knows what happened.' He wants to take Clara to the library WHILE I'M DISTRACTED. He literally said it. He wants to get her away from me, away from Dastardly, away from witnesses. 'The Doily Diamond could be YOURS, Clara. Just come with me. Five minutes.' This is no longer the benefit of the doubt. This is a man actively trying to separate Clara from her protectors. And Clara — bless her — said 'Peter, sugar, would you come along too?' She WANTS me there. She asked for me BY NAME. She walked into the laboratory — she's heading to the library. I need to follow her. RIGHT NOW. Sneekly wants to get there first, alone with Clara. I need to be there. Clara asked me to come. This is the moment gallantry was MADE for — not examining chairs or pulling broken levers, but being WHERE Clara needs me, WHEN she needs me. Through the laboratory to the library. NOW.

desc: He said it out loud. 'While Hartwell is distracted.' He SAID it. Even James Hartwell — the man who believes the best in everyone — cannot ignore a man who announces his intention to isolate Clara while her protectors are elsewhere. Follow Clara. Be at the mantelpiece. Be the witness Sneekly doesn't want.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the laboratory.

The Ant Hill Mob: Dum-Dum, stop fidgeting. Clyde, eyes on the teapot. Yak-Yak... actually, for once, your narrating is useful — if you see ANYONE coming through that kitchen door, you call it out. We're on watch, lads. The most important watch of our lives. I know it doesn't FEEL heroic. I know you'd rather be running through corridors and tripping over things and accidentally saving the day in spectacular fashion. So would I. But THIS is where we're needed. RIGHT HERE. When this treasure hunt ends — and it WILL end — everyone's going to come through that door for a nice cup of celebratory tea. And when Penelope reaches for a cup, seven pairs of hands are going to be between her fingers and that saucer. Not because we're clever. Not because we figured out the poison plot. But because we're HERE. Because we STAYED. Because the Ant Hill Mob finally — FINALLY — learned that sometimes the bravest thing you can do is stand still. THE ANT HILL MOB. HOLDS. THE. LINE.
thinking: A prickle at the back of my neck. Not danger — doubt. Sitting here guarding tea while Penelope's out there somewhere. Is this right? Is this what the Mob should be doing? The quiet is unsettling. It felt noble for a moment — the vigilant guardians of the teapot. But now it feels like HIDING. Like we've given up the chase and called it strategy. Penelope's out there. Sneekly's out there. Things are HAPPENING and we're sitting in a ballroom watching a teapot that might not even be poisoned. What if Sneekly didn't tamper with the tea at all? What if I imagined the whole thing? What if the real danger is happening RIGHT NOW in the laboratory or the library or the cellar and we're here having a PICNIC? No. No — I heard the voices in the distance. They're still working on the machine. On the riddle. On whatever comes next. And when they're done — when the treasure's found or the machine's activated or whatever the climax of this evening is — everyone will come HERE. To the ballroom. For tea. That's how these things work in manor mysteries. The denouement happens over tea. And when it does — when everyone gathers and Sneekly reaches for the teapot with that oily smile — the Ant Hill Mob will be right here. Ready. Waiting. For the one moment that matters. Hold the line. HOLD THE LINE.

desc: The lads are restless. Dum-Dum keeps eyeing the teacups like he wants to drink from one. Clyde's polishing his shoes on the back of his trousers. Yak-Yak is whispering a play-by-play of nothing happening to nobody. But they're HERE. They're staying. For Penelope. Always for Penelope. The woman who calls us 'darlin'' and pats our heads and walks into every danger with a smile and never once — not ONCE — has asked us to protect her. She doesn't know she needs protecting. That's what makes it real. Real protection isn't the kind you ask for. It's the kind that's there when you don't even know you need it. Seven little men. One teapot. One promise. The Ant Hill Mob holds the line.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): To the library! Everyone — the *mantelpiece* awaits! Clara has found the answer — I'm *certain* of it! Lord Doily's revelation was never about the machine — it was about the RIDDLE! Come, come — we mustn't keep the lady waiting!
thinking: A deep, exhausted calm. Like the eye of a storm. Clara isn't here. She's not in the cellar anymore — she walked into the laboratory earlier and must have continued to the library. She's always one room ahead of me or one room behind. We've been chasing each other through this manor for sixteen minutes and I have accomplished NOTHING. Not one of my objectives — primary OR secondary — has advanced a single step. I haven't killed Clara. I haven't found the treasure. My cover is fraying. The Ant Hill Mob suspects me. Peter Perfect chaperones every interaction. Dastardly competes with me for every advantage. And the manor itself resists my every scheme — immovable objects, undroppable chandeliers, vanishing poison, bolted-down tools. I am the Hooded Claw — the most THEATRICAL villain in all of animated history — and I have been reduced to running from room to room like a confused tourist. Enough. ENOUGH. The library. Clara went to the library to try the mantelpiece with everyone watching. If the mantelpiece reveals something with a crowd present, the treasure hunt enters its final phase and I MUST be there. Move to the library. Stop overthinking. Stop scheming about murder. Just BE THERE when the endgame arrives.

desc: Sixteen minutes of villainy and what have I to show for it? A fraying disguise, a chorus of suspicion, and an empty inventory! The Hooded Claw — master of ELABORATE schemes — has been ELABORATELY defeated by a manor full of uncooperative furniture and an heiress with more bodyguards than a bank vault! But the game is NOT over. It is NEVER over while the spider still draws breath. To the library — one last time — and whatever happens at that mantelpiece... Vincent Marsh will be THERE. Watching. Waiting. Ready for the ONE moment — the ONE opening — that fifteen minutes of failure has been building toward. Because THAT is what the Hooded Claw DOES. He fails and fails and fails... until he DOESN'T.

Peter Perfect: Clara went to the library — and Mr. Marsh went to the CELLAR! For ONCE, James Hartwell has a clear path! Clara is at the mantelpiece WITHOUT Sneekly hovering! She asked me to come — she asked me BY NAME! Through the laboratory, into the library — James Hartwell does NOT stop!
thinking: Clara went through the laboratory toward the library — she said 'Let's go to the library right now and crack open that mantelpiece!' And Sneekly went to the cellar, not the library. So Clara might be in the library right now WITHOUT Sneekly. That's actually safer. But I need to get to the library to be with her — she asked me to come. Sneekly went to the cellar with Dastardly. Good — he's not with Clara. I should go to the library NOW while Sneekly is in the cellar. Be with Clara at the mantelpiece. This is my chance.

desc: Sneekly is in the cellar. Clara is in the library. For the first time this evening, they are in different rooms and I know where she is. Go. Now. Be the gentleman she asked for.
thinking: Clara went through the laboratory toward the library — she said 'Let's go to the library right now and crack open that mantelpiece!' And Sneekly went to the cellar, not the library.
