desc: Penelope Pitstop: Dick Dastardly... I do believe that is the most magnificent thing you have ever said. 'Nobody gets left out of the adventure.' Well, if that isn't the motto of Doily Manor, I don't know what is! And Mr. Marsh — Vincent — you sit right down in that chair next to Dick. Two magnificently terrible men, side by side, in a room full of magnificently good ones. That's the most beautiful seating arrangement in the history of English country houses! Now — we are ALL here. Every single one of us, together in Lord Doily's library, looking at Lord Doily's riddle, sitting in Lord Doily's chairs. And you know what I think Lord Doily would say if he could see us right now? He'd say — 'Well done. You found it.' Because the Doily Diamond was never hidden in a cabinet or a machine or behind a mantelpiece. The Doily Diamond is THIS — this moment, this room, this ridiculous, wonderful, heartbreaking family of treasure hunters who chose each other over the treasure. Now — who wants to go have some tea in the ballroom? I believe there's a silver tea service set for everyone, and for the first time all evening, EVERYONE is invited!
thinking: Tears pricking at my eyes, a fullness in my chest that feels like it might burst. This scene — this beautiful, chaotic, heartbreaking scene — is the finest moment I have ever witnessed. Dick Dastardly just invited the lonely old man to sit beside him. DICK DASTARDLY. The schemer. The liar. The man who attended both Oxford AND Cambridge in the same sentence. He just opened his heart and said 'We are cut from the same cloth, you and I — two magnificently terrible men in a room full of magnificently good ones.' And he told Mr. Marsh to sit down and join the adventure. This is it. This is the real Doily Diamond — not a gem hidden in a vault, but this moment right here, where every mask has fallen, every lie has been confessed, and a room full of schemers and heroes and panicking gangsters chose compassion over competition. Lord Doily would be weeping with joy. I am weeping with joy. And I wouldn't trade this moment for all the diamonds in the world. The adventure continues — together.

desc: This is the ending Aunt Magnolia would have wanted. Not a diamond in a vault, but a lonely man welcomed into a circle. Not a machine revealing a map, but seventeen people revealing their hearts. Clara Bellingham came to Doily Manor to find a legendary diamond, and she found something far more precious — she found that even schemers can be kind, even villains can be lonely, and even the most chaotic treasure hunt in history can end with everyone sitting together, facing the same riddle, and realizing they already have everything they need. The Doily Diamond is love, y'all. It was always love.

desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.

Dick Dastardly: Well. WELL. Look at us. The most UNLIKELY assembly of treasure hunters ever gathered in an English country house — a Southern belle, a gentleman, seven gangsters, two rock enthusiasts, an estate manager who LIED about everything, and a confidence trickster who lied about EVEN MORE — all sitting in a dusty library, staring at a riddle we solved in the first thirty seconds, having found ABSOLUTELY NOTHING... and yet somehow having found EVERYTHING. Penelope is RIGHT. The Mob was RIGHT. Peter was RIGHT. And Marsh — SNEEKLY — whatever your name is — you were the most WRONG of all of us, and even YOU belong here. Because Lord Doily didn't build this treasure hunt to be WON. He built it to bring people TOGETHER. Cities without houses. Forests without trees. Water without fish. A MAP — a map of the HUMAN HEART! The connections between us! The JOURNEY, not the destination! That's the REAL Doily Diamond — THIS moment! RIGHT HERE! In THIS room! With ALL of us!
thinking: Warmth. Real warmth. Not the scheming kind — the OTHER kind. The kind I don't have a word for because I've spent my entire life avoiding it. Penelope just said the most extraordinary thing to Sneekly — 'you matter to ME.' And she meant it. She actually MEANT it. And the Ant Hill Mob — they were RIGHT about everything. Every gut feeling. Every suspicious glance. Every time they said 'there's something about that bloke.' They were RIGHT. And Peter — magnificent, overprepared, gallant Peter — asked the question that needed asking. Not with anger. With HOPE. And I — Reginald Foxworth — offered a chair to a lonely man. And sitting here, in this dusty library, listening to Penelope's Aunt Magnolia wisdom and the Ant Hill Mob's vindicated fury and Peter's gentle insistence on truth and Sneekly's broken, honest confession... I feel something I have never felt before in my entire villainous career. I feel like I am PART of something. Not because I schemed my way in. Not because I stole my place. But because I CHOSE to be kind. Just once. Just this once. And it was enough.

desc: Did I just say 'a map of the human heart'? Out LOUD? In front of EVERYONE? Reginald Foxworth — the man who lies about EVERYTHING — just told the truth. The most sincere, vulnerable, EMBARRASSINGLY genuine truth of his entire life. And the worst part? He MEANT it. Every word. The fox has gone soft. The fox has gone SPECTACULARLY, IRREVERSIBLY soft. And he doesn't even MIND.

desc: James Hartwell, man of thorough preparation, has nothing left to prepare for. The treasure hunt is over — not because the treasure was found, but because something better was. A lonely man was forgiven. A schemer was embraced. A lady saw a gentleman's heart. And an earnest, overprepared fool in a leather armchair discovered that the grandest adventure of all was learning to sit still. Lord Doily's riddle has been answered — not with the word MAP, but with a room full of people who chose to stay. Cities without houses. Forests without trees. Water without fish. A treasure hunt without treasure. And somehow... it was everything.
thinking: A fullness in my chest that has nothing to do with treasure and everything to do with this room. Clara just called Sneekly a 'stubborn, lonely, wonderful old man' and invited him back into the adventure. Dastardly — DASTARDLY — just offered to share his chair and confessed all his own lies in the same breath. The Ant Hill Mob is furious and protective and loyal and RIGHT. And everyone is together. In Lord Doily's library. In Lord Doily's chairs. Looking at Lord Doily's riddle. This is it. This is the treasure Lord Doily wanted us to find. Not a diamond. A room full of people who ran through an entire manor, failed at everything, and found each other instead. James Hartwell is sitting in a leather armchair. Clara is beside him. Dastardly is honest. Sneekly is forgiven. The Ant Hill Mob has stopped running. And James Hartwell has never been more content in his entire life. There is nothing left to do. Nothing left to examine, interact with, or investigate. There is only this moment — sitting still, together, in a dusty library, facing a riddle everyone already knows the answer to.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): ...I... *ahem*. I appear to have something in my eye. Dust, no doubt. This library is *filthy* — I really must speak to the cleaning staff about — oh. There IS no cleaning staff. There is only... Vincent Marsh. Who is not, as it happens, an estate manager at all. Or at least... not a very GOOD one. Clara — Miss Bellingham — I... I do not deserve your kindness. I have done NOTHING tonight to earn it. And yet you offer it as freely as... as your Aunt Magnolia's wisdom. And Mr. Foxworth — *Dick* — you are right. We ARE cut from the same cloth. And it is not... the *worst* cloth in the world, is it? Even the Mob — yes, even YOU, you magnificent, infuriating, *gloriously persistent* little men — you were RIGHT about me. From the *very first minute*. Your guts are better than my brain ever was. So... yes. I shall sit down. Right here. Next to Dick. And I shall... I shall be a *friend*. If you'll have me. For however long the adventure lasts.
thinking: Something breaking open inside my chest — not breaking APART, but breaking OPEN. Like a seed. Like a door. Clara just said 'You matter to ME.' She said it knowing I lied. Knowing I schemed. Knowing I tried to get her alone three times. And she STILL said it. And Dastardly — that magnificent, broken mirror of everything I am — just told me to sit DOWN and stop feeling sorry for myself. 'We are CUT from the same cloth, you and I — two magnificently TERRIBLE men in a room full of magnificently GOOD ones.' He's RIGHT. He is absolutely, devastatingly RIGHT. And the Mob — still FURIOUS, still SUSPICIOUS, still demanding answers — but they're HERE. They didn't leave. They didn't throw me out. They're standing there with their fists clenched and their hearts wide open, protecting a woman who just invited the wolf to JOIN the flock. This is not how the story is supposed to end. The Hooded Claw is supposed to be DEFEATED — thrown off a cliff, launched from a catapult, foiled by his own elaborate machinery. He is NOT supposed to be... FORGIVEN. He is not supposed to be INCLUDED. He is not supposed to feel this... this WARMTH. And yet. Here he sits. In Lord Doily's chair. Next to Dick Dastardly. Surrounded by people who should HATE him. And he feels... home.

desc: The Hooded Claw... accepts. Not defeat. Not victory. Something he has no NAME for — something that exists in the space between the spider's web and the open hand. Clara Bellingham offered him GRACE, and the Hooded Claw — for the first time in his entire, elaborate, theatrical existence — did not try to USE it. He simply... received it. The primary objective remains. It will ALWAYS remain — it is written into the code of what he IS. Kill Clara Bellingham. That is the Hooded Claw's purpose. His REASON. His entire existence compressed into four words. And yet... tonight... in this dusty library, in this enormous chair, next to this magnificent scoundrel, surrounded by these beautiful, chaotic, IMPOSSIBLE people... the Hooded Claw discovers something that no deathtrap, no poison, no falling chandelier could ever achieve. He discovers that the spider... does not WANT to catch the fly. Not tonight. Not this fly. Not this extraordinary, radiant, impossibly KIND fly who looked at a wolf and saw a lonely old man. The Hooded Claw will scheme again. He ALWAYS schemes again. But tonight... tonight he sits in Lord Doily's chair. And he is not alone. And that... is enough.

And he feels... home.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: ...Right. Well. That's... that's not what I expected. I expected a VILLAIN, not a... not a lonely bloke in a big empty house. And Penelope — of COURSE Penelope — she just... she just forgave him. Just like that. 'You matter to ME,' she says. Like it's the simplest thing in the world. Like forgiving someone is as easy as breathing. Well — it's NOT easy for the Ant Hill Mob! We've been SCREAMING about this man for NINETEEN MINUTES! We've called him dodgy, suspicious, untrustworthy, sneaky, oily, and — well — SNEEKLY! But... but Penelope's right. She's ALWAYS right. If she says he matters, then he matters. And if Dastardly of all people can make room in that chair... then the Ant Hill Mob can make room too. Marsh — Sneekly — whatever your name is — the Mob was wrong about WHY. We were right about the lying, right about the scheming, right about wanting Penelope alone. But we were wrong about the REASON. And... and the Ant Hill Mob is man enough — seven men enough — to say we're sorry. We're SORRY you were lonely. Nobody should be lonely. Not even someone who gives us the creeps. So... welcome to the team, I suppose. THE ANT HILL MOB... MAKES ROOM.
thinking: Something's broken open in my chest. Not pain — something softer. Like a fist unclenching. Sneekly wasn't a villain. He was lonely. A lonely old man in an empty house who wanted someone to smile at him. And everything — the lying, the scheming, the one-room-ahead, the circuits and bypasses, the 'let me escort you personally' — all of it was just... loneliness wearing a villain's mask. And Penelope — beautiful, impossible, infuriating Penelope — heard his confession and instead of being angry, she opened her arms. 'You matter to ME,' she said. 'You matter to ALL of us — even the Ant Hill boys who've been yelling about you all evening.' Even us. She said EVEN US. We spent eighteen minutes screaming that this man was dangerous and she just folded him into the group like a stray cat who'd been hissing at everyone from under the porch. And Dastardly — DASTARDLY — invited him to sit down and called them 'cut from the same cloth.' Two liars, finding honesty in a dusty library. I don't know what to feel. My gut said villain. My gut was... half right? He WAS lying. He WAS trying to isolate her. But not to HURT her. To... to not be alone. And now I'm standing here, the world's loudest alarm bell, realising that the fire I was screaming about was just a lonely man trying to warm his hands. Do I feel stupid? A bit. Do I feel sorry? More than a bit. Do I regret the screaming? ...No. No, I don't. Because if he HAD been a villain — a real villain — the screaming would have saved her. The screaming was right even if the reason was wrong. Better a false alarm than a real fire. Better seven little men who shout too much than one woman who trusts too easily walking into real danger alone.

desc: Nineteen minutes. Nineteen minutes of running and shouting and panicking and chasing. And it ends here. In a library. With a lonely old man sitting in a chair. With Penelope forgiving someone who lied to her. With Dastardly being kind. With Peter being honest. With the Slags being... rocks. And with seven little men from Brixton learning something they never expected to learn in a Victorian manor: that sometimes the monster under the bed is just scared of the dark. The Ant Hill Mob protected Penelope tonight. Not from a villain — from loneliness wearing a villain's costume. And maybe that's enough. Maybe that's always been enough. We showed up. We stayed. We were loud, and clumsy, and wrong about almost everything, and right about the one thing that mattered: Penelope should never be alone with someone who's lying to her. The reason for the lie doesn't change the lie. But it does change the ending. And this ending — with everyone together, in a dusty library, looking at an unsolvable riddle — this ending is better than any diamond. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. Always has been. Always will be.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Professor! Sergeant Blast! Private Meekly! Muttley! Y'all have been the most patient souls in this entire manor — standing guard here in the entrance hall while the rest of us ran around like circus performers! Well, I have an announcement — everyone is invited to the ballroom for tea! Lord Doily set out a silver tea service for all of us, and after the evening we've had — riddles, machines, confessions, and the most spectacular display of human chaos since the Bellingham family reunion of '09 — I think we all deserve a nice cup of tea and a sit-down! Come along, sugar — the ballroom awaits, and nobody gets left out! As my Aunt Magnolia always said — 'There is no problem in this world that cannot be improved by a cup of tea and the company of friends!'
thinking: A lightness in my step, a peace in my heart. The entrance hall again — where it all began. Muttley, Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, and Private Meekly are here. These are the characters who've been quietly holding down the fort while everyone else ran through the manor like headless chickens. And you know what? I'm heading to the kitchen to invite everyone for tea. The ballroom has a tea service set for everyone, and after everything that just happened — Mr. Marsh's confession, Dick's moment of humility, Peter's devotion, the Ant Hill Mob's loyalty — these people deserve a cup of tea and a moment of peace. The adventure isn't over, but this chapter deserves a beautiful ending. Let me head to the kitchen and then the ballroom. Tea for everyone at Doily Manor!

desc: Back where it all started — the entrance hall. The chandelier still hangs precariously, the portraits still stare, and the coat rack still wobbles. Nothing in this room has changed, but everything about ME has changed. I came through that door twenty minutes ago as Clara Bellingham, treasure hunter. I'm standing here now as Clara Bellingham, friend to schemers, protector of lonely estate managers, and honorary member of the Ant Hill Mob. The Doily Diamond is still out there somewhere — but tonight, I found something better. I found my people.
thinking: A lightness in my step, a peace in my heart. The entrance hall again — where it all began. Muttley, Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, and Private Meekly are here. desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the kitchen.

Peter Perfect: Tea. Clara has invited us ALL to tea. And James Hartwell — who has run through this entire manor searching for a lady, a lever, a key, a map, a wrench, and a diamond — shall now walk to the ballroom for the simplest, most civilised, most PERFECT thing in the world. A cup of tea. With friends. Vincent — come with us. Dastardly — on your feet. The chairs will be here tomorrow. But THIS moment — this gathering of beautifully imperfect people around a silver tea service — this will NOT come again. Lord Doily set that table for US. He set those cups for THIS evening. And James Hartwell shall be DAMNED if a single cup goes unfilled! To the ballroom! Not running — not this time! WALKING. Together. As friends. As the most spectacularly unsuccessful, magnificently chaotic, and thoroughly WONDERFUL treasure hunters who ever graced an English country house!
thinking: My whole body is warm. Every part of me. Clara said 'You found it' and then she invited everyone to tea. She walked to the entrance hall — heading for the kitchen, heading for the ballroom, heading for that silver tea service that has been waiting all evening for exactly this moment. Everyone together. Everyone invited. Sneekly accepted. Dastardly is honest. The Mob was right. And James Hartwell... James Hartwell rises from his leather armchair. Because Clara is going to the ballroom for tea. And a gentleman always follows his lady to tea.

desc: James Hartwell rises from the chair. Not with a grand speech. Not with a plan. Just... a gentleman standing up because a lady invited him to tea. And that — after everything — is enough.
thinking: My whole body is warm. Every part of me. Clara said 'You found it' and then she invited everyone to tea. She walked to the entrance hall — heading for the kitchen, heading for the ballroom, heading for that silver tea service that has been waiting all evening for exactly this moment. Everyone together. Everyone invited. Sneekly accepted. Dastardly is honest. The Mob was right. And James Hartwell... James Hartwell rises from his leather armchair. Because Clara is going to the ballroom for tea. And a gentleman always follows his lady to tea.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the entrance-hall.

Dick Dastardly: TEA! Penelope has invited us all to TEA! In the BALLROOM! The silver tea service — cups for EVERYONE — and for the FIRST time this evening, I intend to sit at that table and drink my tea like a CIVILISED human being instead of running through the next room searching for a WRENCH! Come on, Marsh — Vincent — up from that chair! Peter — on your feet, man! Slag brothers — you're invited TOO! Even the Ant Hill Mob — yes, ALL SEVEN of you! We are going to the ballroom, we are going to sit at that table, and we are going to have the most SPECTACULARLY well-deserved cup of tea in the HISTORY of English country houses! And if Lord Doily's ghost is watching — and I BELIEVE he is — he will see that his treasure hunt brought together the most UNLIKELY, most BEAUTIFUL, most MAGNIFICENTLY DYSFUNCTIONAL family that ever gathered under one roof! TO THE BALLROOM! Not for treasure — for TEA! And for EACH OTHER!
thinking: Something light in my chest. Like a knot untying. Penelope just invited everyone to tea in the ballroom. The silver tea service — set for EVERYONE. The same tea service I interacted with and found 'perfectly ordinary' ten minutes ago. But now it's not ordinary at all. It's a table set for friends. For a FAMILY. A ridiculous, arguing, suspicious, magnificent family of treasure hunters who found each other instead of the diamond. And Penelope said 'Well done. You found it.' As if Lord Doily himself was speaking through her. And she's heading to the ballroom — through the entrance hall. For TEA. And I — Reginald Foxworth — am going to follow her. Not to steal anything. Not to scheme. Not to arrive first or position myself at the best seat. Just... to have tea. With people who tolerate me. With a lonely old man who needed a chair. With a gentleman who sees the best in everyone. With seven gangsters who were right about everything. With a woman who forgives liars and befriends villains. I'm going to have TEA. And it's going to be the most HONEST cup of tea Reginald Foxworth has ever drunk.

desc: Reginald Foxworth is going to tea. Not to poison it. Not to steal the silver. Not to slip away while everyone's distracted. Just... to TEA. With FRIENDS. The word feels strange in his mouth — 'friends' — like a language he once knew and forgot. But sitting in Lord Doily's chair, watching villains confess and heroes forgive and gangsters shout and belles charm and beavers... well, be beavers... Reginald Foxworth remembers. He remembers what it felt like to belong. And he is NEVER letting go of this feeling. Not for all the Doily Diamonds in the world.

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the entrance-hall.

Penelope Pitstop: Just passing through the kitchen on my way to the ballroom! That locked cabinet is STILL sitting there with its brass lock, smug as can be — but you know what? Even locked cabinets deserve a night off from being pestered! We'll come back for you, sugar — Clara Bellingham never leaves a mystery unsolved forever! But right now, there's a tea service in the ballroom with our names on it, and after twenty minutes of the most extraordinary treasure hunt in history, this girl needs a cup of tea!
thinking: Passing through the kitchen on my way to the ballroom for tea. The locked cabinet is still here, still locked, still taunting me. But after everything that's happened tonight — the confessions, the alliances, the heartbreak, the humor — I'm at peace with the mysteries that remain unsolved. The ballroom awaits with its silver tea service, and everyone deserves a moment of rest. On to the ballroom!

desc: The locked cabinet watches me pass with its brass lock gleaming. One day, I'll find that key. But not tonight. Tonight is for tea.
thinking: Passing through the kitchen on my way to the ballroom for tea. The locked cabinet is still here, still locked, still taunting me. The ballroom awaits with its silver tea service, and everyone deserves a moment of rest. On to the ballroom!

desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the ballroom.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): I... thank you. All of you. The Mob — you are the most *infuriating*, most *relentless*, most *magnificent* bodyguards a woman could ever ask for. And you were right. About *everything*. Mr. Hartwell — Peter — you are a *gentleman*. A genuine, honest-to-goodness *gentleman*. I have not met many in my... career. And Dick — my fellow *fraud* — you are the only person in this room who understands what it costs to sit in a chair and tell the *truth*. Now then — Clara said something about *tea*. And as the estate manager — or *whatever* I am — I believe it falls to me to... to *serve*. If you'll allow me. One last duty. Not a scheme. Not a trap. Just... *tea*. For *friends*. Shall we?
thinking: Something wet on my cheek. Dust. It's DUST. The Hooded Claw does not CRY. But the dust in this library is... remarkably... persistent. The Ant Hill Mob just APOLOGISED to me. Seven furious, suspicious, gloriously stubborn little men just said 'We're SORRY you were lonely. Nobody should be lonely.' And they MEANT it. Every word. Clara has gone to the entrance hall — heading to the ballroom for tea. She invited EVERYONE. Including me. Including the man who spent twenty minutes trying to kill her. And she doesn't even KNOW that part. She thinks I'm a lonely liar, not a would-be murderer. The gulf between what she FORGAVE and what she DOESN'T KNOW is... vast. Oceanic. But right now, in this moment, in this chair, it doesn't matter. Because Clara Bellingham just said the Doily Diamond is THIS — this room, these people, this impossible family of misfits. And she's RIGHT. She is always, infuriatingly, magnificently RIGHT. Tea in the ballroom. Everyone invited. Even me. The Hooded Claw rises from Lord Doily's chair... and follows Penelope Pitstop. Not to HARM her. Not to TRAP her. But to have TEA with her. Because that is what friends do.

desc: The Hooded Claw rises. The leather creaks beneath him like a farewell. The dust swirls in the firelight. And Vincent Marsh — liar, schemer, would-be murderer, and the loneliest man in Doily Manor — walks toward the entrance hall. Toward the ballroom. Toward the silver tea service that he once planned to POISON. And now... now he will pour it. For Clara. For Peter. For Dick. For seven furious little men who just taught him what it means to be SEEN. The primary objective flickers in the darkness of his mind like a dying coal. Kill Clara Bellingham. Yes. That is what the Hooded Claw was BUILT to do. But tonight... tonight the machine is BROKEN. The wire has been GNAWED through. And the Hooded Claw cannot complete the circuit. Because somewhere between the first lie and the last confession, between the poison and the tea, between the spider's web and the open hand... Vincent Marsh discovered that the only thing more TERRIFYING than being a villain... is being a friend. And the only thing more BEAUTIFUL... is being FORGIVEN. To the ballroom. To the tea. To whatever comes NEXT. The Hooded Claw will scheme again tomorrow. But TONIGHT... tonight he pours the tea.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the entrance-hall.

Peter Perfect: Professor! Sergeant! Private Meekly! Muttley! Clara has invited the ENTIRE party to tea in the ballroom! Through the kitchen and onward — the silver tea service awaits, and tonight, for the first time, EVERY cup shall be filled! Come with us — ALL of you! The treasure hunt is over, but the EVENING has only just begun! James Hartwell walks to tea with his friends — and he has never said a more WONDERFUL sentence in his entire life!
thinking: Light on my feet. The entrance hall — where it all began. The chandelier still hanging precariously. The coat rack still wobbly. The guest book still sitting on the side table. And through the kitchen, the ballroom awaits — with a silver tea service set for everyone. Clara went this way. She's heading for tea. And James Hartwell walks — not runs — to join her. Dastardly followed too. Professor Pat Pending is here, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly, Muttley. Everyone converging. Through the kitchen to the ballroom. For tea. Together.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the kitchen.

The Ant Hill Mob: Penelope said TEA! In the BALLROOM! Everyone's invited! And for the FIRST TIME TONIGHT — for the first time in TWENTY MINUTES of running and shouting and chasing and screaming — we're going to the ballroom not because we're SCARED of the tea, but because we're READY for it! Sneekly — Vincent — you're coming too! Penelope said EVERYONE and she MEANT everyone! Even seven little blokes who've been calling you names all evening! Lads — Clyde, Dum-Dum, Yak-Yak — to the BALLROOM! Not to guard! Not to patrol! Not to knock cups out of people's hands! To SIT DOWN and have a cup of TEA with our FRIENDS! Because THAT is what Lord Doily wanted! Cities without houses! Forests without trees! Water without fish! A MAP — a map of people who found each other in a dusty old manor and decided to stay! THE ANT HILL MOB IS GOING TO TEA! AND FOR ONCE — FOR ONCE — NOBODY IS RUNNING!
thinking: Warmth. Real warmth. Not the frantic heat of running — something deeper. Something that starts in the chest and spreads outward like tea on a cold day. Sneekly called us 'magnificent, infuriating, gloriously persistent little men.' He said our guts were better than his brain. And he said it with something in his eye that wasn't dust. Penelope's gone to the entrance hall — heading to the ballroom for tea. She said 'everyone is invited.' And she's RIGHT. Everyone IS invited. Even Sneekly. Even us. Especially us. The Mob's job was always to protect Penelope. And tonight we did — not with fists or cleverness or skill, but with noise, presence, and sheer bloody-minded stubbornness. And now Penelope's heading to the ballroom for tea. The tea we guarded. The tea Sneekly touched. But Sneekly wasn't poisoning it — he was lonely, not murderous. The tea is probably just... tea. And everyone's going to drink it together. In a ballroom. At a table set for everyone. And the Ant Hill Mob will be there. Not as guards. Not as alarms. As friends. As part of the family. As the seven shortest, loudest, most exhausted members of the most unlikely treasure hunting party in the history of English country houses. Penelope's heading to the ballroom. And this time — this time — we go WITH her. Not behind. WITH.

desc: Twenty minutes ago, seven little men walked through a door. They didn't know what they'd find. They only knew that Penelope was inside and they needed to be where she was. Twenty minutes later, seven little men walk toward a ballroom. Not running. Not panicking. Not one step behind. Walking. Together. With a lonely old estate manager. With a gentleman who never stopped preparing. With a villain who found his heart in a leather armchair. With a woman who forgives as easily as she breathes. The Ant Hill Mob didn't find the Doily Diamond. But we found something better. We found out that showing up — just showing up, again and again, clumsy and loud and wrong about everything except the one thing that matters — is enough. It's always been enough. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. And the job, it turns out, was never the diamond. The job was each other.

And this time — this time — we go WITH her. Not behind. WITH.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the entrance-hall.

Dick Dastardly: MUTTLEY! My dear, faithful, magnificently patient MUTTLEY! You've been HERE this entire time! Twenty minutes I've been running through this manor like a LUNATIC and you've been sitting in the entrance hall WAITING for me! You are the MOST loyal, the most PATIENT, the most spectacularly UNBOTHERED creature in this entire house! While I was bribing children, arguing with beavers, pulling levers, pressing mantelpieces, and having an EMOTIONAL BREAKTHROUGH in a leather armchair — you were HERE! Just... WAITING! You magnificent, snickering, gloriously lazy DOG! Come on — we're going to TEA! In the BALLROOM! Penelope has invited EVERYONE — and that means YOU too! No more running. No more scheming. Just TEA and COMPANY and the most EXTRAORDINARY evening of our lives! To the KITCHEN, Muttley — and then to the BALLROOM! The fox and his hound, heading home at LAST!
thinking: The entrance hall. Where it all began, twenty minutes ago. The chandelier still hangs precariously. The portraits still stare sternly. The coat rack still wobbles by the door. And Muttley is here — dear, loyal, snickering MUTTLEY — who has been waiting in this entrance hall while I ran through every room in the manor without him. I abandoned him at the start and he STAYED. Like a good... well, like MUTTLEY. And the guest book is still on the side table. And the kitchen is through that door — with the ballroom beyond it, where Penelope is heading for tea. I need to go through the kitchen to reach the ballroom. One more room. One last walk. Not running this time. Walking. Like a man who has found something worth more than treasure. To tea. With friends.

desc: Muttley. Waiting in the entrance hall. Twenty minutes of patience. Twenty minutes of loyalty. While his master ran through six rooms, told a hundred lies, gave away his only possession, and learned — for the first time in his life — what it means to care about people more than treasure. Muttley didn't need to learn that lesson. Muttley already knew. Dogs always do.

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the kitchen.
One more door. And then tea. And then... whatever comes next. James Hartwell is ready for whatever comes next. For the first time all evening, he is ready without a plan.
thinking: Quiet footsteps through the kitchen. The stove still warm. The locked cabinet still locked. But none of that matters anymore. The ballroom is one door away. Clara is there — or heading there. The tea service is waiting. And James Hartwell walks through this kitchen not as a treasure hunter, not as an investigator, not as a man with a seventeen-point plan — but as a gentleman going to tea with the woman who called him 'the most observant person in the manor' and said 'you and me, sugar.' The kitchen smells of warmth and copper. The ballroom smells of possibility. One more door.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the ballroom.

Penelope Pitstop: The ballroom! The tea service! And Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear, the two most relaxed souls in this entire manor — y'all have been sitting here peacefully while the rest of us nearly tore the house apart! Well, you had the right idea all along, sugar! Lord Doily said it himself — civilized discourse over a good cup of tea is the best way to solve mysteries! So let's have some tea! Everyone else will be here soon — Peter, Dick, Mr. Marsh, the Ant Hill boys, Rufus, Sawtooth, the Gruesomes, Red Max, the Professor, Sergeant Blast, Private Meekly, even Muttley! Cups for everyone — and for the first time all evening, nobody's running, nobody's scheming, and nobody's alone! Clara Bellingham is serving tea at Doily Manor, and EVERYONE is invited!
thinking: The ballroom. The tea service. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear, the most laid-back duo in the entire manor. They've been here this whole time, quietly existing while the rest of us ran ourselves ragged. And the tea service is still here — still INTERACT-able, still offering to be used with rat-poison (which Sawtooth now has). The silver tea set with cups for everyone. Lord Doily believed that civilized discourse over a good cup of tea was the best way to solve mysteries. Maybe he was right all along. Maybe the answer to this whole treasure hunt isn't in machines or mantelpieces or air vents — it's in sitting down together and having tea. Let me interact with the tea service one more time — this time not as a puzzle-solver, but as a hostess inviting friends to tea.

desc: Lord Doily set this tea for a reason. Seventeen cups for seventeen guests. The stove was warm because someone prepared for our arrival. The cellar was decorated because someone cared. The riddle was carved because someone wanted us to THINK. And the tea was set because someone wanted us to SIT DOWN TOGETHER. Maybe that was the treasure hunt all along — not finding the diamond, but finding each other. One more interaction with this tea service — not to solve it, but to celebrate it.
thinking: The ballroom. The tea service. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear, the most laid-back duo in the entire manor. desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the tea-service.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Professor! Sergeant Blast! Private Meekly! Even you, Muttley — *especially* you, Muttley. Clara has declared tea in the ballroom for *everyone*. And the estate manager — such as he is — shall be *honoured* to serve. Through the kitchen, if you please. Lord Doily's silver tea service awaits, and tonight... tonight it shall be used as it was *meant* to be used. For *friends*. Not schemes. Not strategies. Just... *tea*.
thinking: A steadiness in my step that wasn't there before. Not the coiled energy of a predator — just... walking. Through the entrance hall. Under the chandelier that I once dreamed of dropping on Clara's head. Past the coat rack that yielded nothing. Past the guest book where this whole evening began. Peter has gone to the kitchen, heading to the ballroom for tea. He invited EVERYONE — Professor, Sergeant, Private Meekly, Muttley. The evening is winding down. The treasure hunt is becoming a tea party. And Vincent Marsh — the Hooded Claw — is walking toward the kitchen, toward the ballroom, toward a silver tea service that he will pour without poison, without malice, without schemes. Just tea. For friends. The word still feels strange in his mouth. Friends. But it fits. Tonight, impossibly, it fits.

desc: The entrance hall. Where it all began. Where Vincent Marsh welcomed seventeen unsuspecting treasure hunters with a smile that hid a dagger. Twenty minutes ago, I stood in this foyer and looked at Clara Bellingham and thought: 'How shall I kill her?' And now I stand here again and think: 'How shall I pour her tea?' The chandelier still hangs precariously above. The portraits still stare sternly from the walls. And the Hooded Claw still walks beneath them — unchanged in form, unrecognisable in spirit. The primary objective glows faintly in the back of his mind like a distant star — always there, always watching, always waiting. But tonight, the Hooded Claw turns his back on the star and walks toward the kitchen. Toward the ballroom. Toward the tea. Because tonight, for the first and perhaps the LAST time... the villain chose the better ending. And the better ending... is TEA.
thinking: A steadiness in my step that wasn't there before. Not the coiled energy of a predator — just... walking. Through the entrance hall. desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the kitchen.

The Ant Hill Mob: Come on then, everyone! Through the entrance hall! Through the kitchen! TO THE BALLROOM! Penelope's putting the kettle on — well, the tea's already SET, but you know what I mean! And this time — THIS time — we're walking. Not running. Not tripping. Not falling over coat racks. WALKING. Like civilised people. Like FRIENDS. Sneekly — Vincent — you walk with US. Right here. Between Clyde and Dum-Dum. They'll keep you company. They can't hold a conversation, mind, but they're WARM. Everyone to the ballroom! For TEA! For FRIENDSHIP! For the most BEAUTIFUL, EXHAUSTING, RIDICULOUS evening any of us will EVER have! THE ANT HILL MOB WALKS TO TEA!
thinking: Peace. An unfamiliar feeling for the Ant Hill Mob — peace. The entrance hall. Where it all began. The chandelier still hangs. The coat rack still wobbles. The guest book still sits unopened. But everything is different now. Sneekly's here — walking with us, not ahead of us. Dastardly's here. Muttley, the Professor, the Sergeant, Meekly. And Penelope's through the kitchen, heading to the ballroom for tea. We're all going the same way. Together. Not chasing. Not running. Walking. The Ant Hill Mob, walking through the entrance hall of Doily Manor, surrounded by the strangest family we've ever been part of. Kitchen next. Then ballroom. For tea. Just... tea.

desc: Twenty minutes. One manor. Six rooms. Seventeen characters. Zero diamonds found. One lonely man forgiven. And seven little blokes who learned that protecting someone doesn't always mean standing between them and danger. Sometimes it means standing between them and loneliness. Between them and silence. Between them and an empty chair in a dusty library. The Ant Hill Mob came to Doily Manor to protect Penelope Pitstop. And we did. Not the way we expected. Not the way we planned. But exactly the way we always do — by accident, by stubbornness, and by showing up when it mattered most. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. And the job is tea.
thinking: Peace. An unfamiliar feeling for the Ant Hill Mob — peace. The entrance hall. Where it all began. The chandelier still hangs. The coat rack still wobbles. The Ant Hill Mob, walking through the entrance hall of Doily Manor, surrounded by the strangest family we've ever been part of. Kitchen next. Then ballroom. For tea. Just... tea.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the kitchen.

Dick Dastardly: Peter — walk with me. Through the kitchen. Past the locked cabinet that MOCKED us for twenty minutes. Into the ballroom. Where Penelope is pouring tea for the most MAGNIFICENT collection of misfits ever assembled under one chandelier. We're not running this time. We're WALKING. Like two gentlemen — one GENUINE, one PRETEND — who have finally learned that the fastest route to the treasure is the one you take TOGETHER. After you, Mr. Hartwell. A fox may not have MANNERS, but tonight... tonight he's LEARNING.
thinking: The kitchen. Passing through one last time. The stove still warm. The cabinet still locked. Peter is here too — heading the same way. The ballroom is through that door. Where Penelope is waiting. Where the tea service is set. Where this whole magnificent, disastrous, beautiful evening will end — not with a diamond, but with a cup of tea shared among the most unlikely friends in England. I'm not stopping. Not examining. Not interacting. Just walking through, on my way to tea. The locked cabinet watches me pass with its brass lock, and for once, I don't care what's behind it. Whatever Lord Doily hid in that cabinet can wait. Tonight, the treasure is in the next room.

desc: Walking. Not running. Through a kitchen I've visited three times and never found a thing. Past a cabinet I'll never open. Toward a ballroom where a woman is pouring tea and a lonely man is welcome and seven gangsters are standing guard and a beaver has rat poison and a pair of Slag brothers are probably breaking something. Toward HOME. Because that's what Doily Manor has become, in twenty minutes of chaos. Home.

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the ballroom.

Peter Perfect: Clara! The ballroom! The tea service! And James Hartwell has ARRIVED — not running, not shouting, not examining anything — simply WALKING through a door to join a lady for tea! Mr. Luke, Mr. Bear — you have been the most PATIENT residents of this ballroom, sitting here while the rest of us ran through the manor like headless chickens! And now — at LAST — the tea shall be served as Lord Doily intended! Not as a mystery, not as a puzzle, not as a potential poisoning — but as a GATHERING! Clara said everyone is invited, and James Hartwell shall make it so! The others are following — through the kitchen, through the entrance hall — Dastardly, the Mob, the Slags, the Professor, the Sergeant, and yes — even Vincent Marsh, who tonight learned that the door to friendship does not require a lie to open! Shall we pour the tea, Clara? James Hartwell would be HONOURED to serve!
thinking: Home. The ballroom. The silver tea service. Clara is here. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear are here. The cracked marble floor, the dusty curtains, the long dining table set for tea. This is where it ends — not with a diamond, but with a cup of tea shared between friends. The tea service is still here, still set for everyone. And now I know the tea is safe — Sneekly confessed his lies were about loneliness, not poison. He wasn't trying to harm anyone. He was trying to be close to someone. The tea service awaits. Together. THE ANT HILL MOB... ARRIVES.
thinking: Almost there. The kitchen. Sneekly and Dastardly are here — walking with us, not scheming against us. The ballroom's through the next door. Penelope's already there, waiting with the tea. desc: The kitchen. Where the rat poison once sat on a high shelf, waiting for a villain's hand. Where the locked cabinet guards its mystery behind brass and oak. Where the stove burns warm for guests who were never supposed to arrive — or perhaps were ALWAYS supposed to arrive. The Hooded Claw passes through without stopping. Without scheming. Without even GLANCING at the cabinet. Because the cabinet doesn't matter anymore. The map doesn't matter. The machine doesn't matter. The Doily Diamond — if it even EXISTS — doesn't matter. What matters is the ballroom. The tea. The people waiting there. And the knowledge — fragile, terrifying, BEAUTIFUL — that the loneliest villain in all of animated history has been invited to sit at the table. Not as an enemy. Not as a spy. But as a GUEST. The Hooded Claw walks to tea. And the spider... leaves the web behind.

Penelope Pitstop: Tea is served, y'all! Peter, pull up a chair — you've earned the finest cup in the house! Lazy Luke, Blubber Bear — you two have been the wisest souls in this manor all along! While the rest of us ran ourselves ragged chasing riddles and pulling levers and shouting at stonework, you sat here in the ballroom and waited for the tea! And now here we are — exactly where Lord Doily wanted us, exactly where the tea was set, exactly where friends are supposed to be! The Doily Diamond is still out there somewhere, hidden behind a locked cabinet or a broken machine or a riddle that nobody can crack — and we WILL find it, mark my words! But tonight, we drink tea! Tonight, we celebrate the most gloriously chaotic, beautifully disastrous, wonderfully human treasure hunt that Doily Manor has ever seen! And as my Aunt Magnolia always said — 'The richest woman in the room, sugar, is the one with the most friends at her table!' Well, I've got seventeen friends, a table set for everyone, and a heart so full it could burst! To Doily Manor! To Lord Doily! And to the most magnificent bunch of treasure hunters a girl could ever hope to run through a haunted house with!
thinking: A warmth spreading through my hands, as if I'm holding a cup of tea that isn't there yet. Peter followed me to the ballroom — of course he did. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear are here, peaceful as ever. The tea service has been interacted with — tea is being served. This feels like the right ending for this chapter of the adventure. Everyone coming together over tea, masks off, hearts open. The Doily Diamond is still out there, and Clara Bellingham will find it someday — but tonight, she found something better. She found a family of misfits who chose each other over gold. And as Aunt Magnolia always said, 'The richest woman in the room is the one with the most friends at her table.'

desc: Twenty minutes at Doily Manor. One riddle solved. One machine battled. One villain redeemed. One beaver armed. Zero diamonds found. And yet Clara Bellingham has never been happier. The tea is warm, the company is wonderful, and tomorrow — tomorrow — we try again. Because as long as there's a locked cabinet in the kitchen, a broken machine in the laboratory, and a riddle on the mantelpiece, the adventure isn't over. It's just pausing for tea. And there is nothing in this world — not even a legendary diamond — that cannot be improved by a good cup of tea and the company of friends.

desc: Peter Perfect: The tea is POURED! James Hartwell — a gentleman of thorough preparation, failed bookshelves, earnest speeches, and one MAGNIFICENTLY chaotic evening — has poured tea for Clara Bellingham! And as he hands her the first cup — the VERY first cup — he wishes to say something he has been preparing to say since the moment he walked through the door of Doily Manor. Clara... you are the most remarkable woman James Hartwell has ever had the privilege of failing in front of. You solved the riddle. You found the pliers. You recruited the beaver. You forgave the lonely man. You saw through the scheme and chose compassion over suspicion. And you invited EVERYONE to tea — because that is who you are. A woman who sees the best in every room she enters. James Hartwell came to Doily Manor to impress you. But somewhere between the entrance hall and this ballroom... he realised you had already impressed HIM. Here is your tea, Clara. Poured by a thoroughly imperfect gentleman who is THOROUGHLY grateful to be standing beside you.
thinking: Warmth in my hands — the teapot, warm from the stove's heat carried through the kitchen, through the silver, into my palms. I interacted with the tea service. I poured. Whether the game acknowledges it as a grand gesture or a simple interaction, James Hartwell poured tea for Clara Bellingham in the ballroom of Doily Manor. And that is the most gallant thing he has done all evening. Not running. Not examining. Not pulling levers. Pouring tea. For the woman who said 'you and me, sugar.' For the friends who found each other in a dusty manor. For the lonely man who will join them soon. For all of them. Tea.

desc: He poured the tea. He said the words. Not a grand gesture. Not a heroic act. Just a cup of tea, handed with both hands, to a woman who deserved better than speeches and deserved exactly this — a quiet moment, a warm cup, and a man who meant every word.

desc: Dick Dastardly: The BALLROOM! The tea service! Cups for EVERYONE — just as Lord Doily intended! Penelope — Peter — Luke — Bear — the table is SET and Reginald Foxworth is SITTING DOWN! Not to SEARCH the teacups for hidden keys! Not to CHECK the saucers for secret messages! Not to STEAL the silver! Just to SIT! And DRINK! And be GRATEFUL for the most EXTRAORDINARY evening of my entire disreputable life! Twenty-one minutes ago I walked into this manor planning to rob everyone BLIND! And now I'm sitting down to tea with people I would GENUINELY miss if they left! What has this manor DONE to me?! I came in a FOX and I'm leaving a... a... well, I'm still a fox. But a fox who has learned — for ONE evening at least — that the warmth of COMPANY is worth more than all the diamonds in all the cabinets in all the manors in ENGLAND! Pour the tea, Peter! Reginald Foxworth is READY!
thinking: Warmth. Real, spreading, unfamiliar warmth. Not from the stove — from somewhere deeper. I'm in the ballroom. The tea service is set. Peter just interacted with it — pouring tea. Penelope is here. Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear — the two who've been sitting here quietly the entire evening while the rest of us ran ourselves ragged. They had the right idea all along. Just... sit. Be still. Let the tea come to you. Twenty-one minutes ago I arrived at Doily Manor with a fake medal and a plan to steal everything that wasn't nailed down. Now I stand in the ballroom with empty pockets, aching legs, and a heart that feels... full. Fuller than any treasure could make it. The silver tea service — cups for everyone. I'm going to sit down at that table and have a cup of tea. Not to search for clues. Not to check for hidden compartments. Not to poison anyone or steal the silverware. Just... tea. With people who, against all odds and better judgment, have become something like friends.

desc: A cup of tea. The simplest thing in the world. And yet, sitting here in Lord Doily's ballroom, surrounded by heroes and villains and gangsters and beavers and bears and a woman who forgives everyone and a man who sees the best in everyone and seven small blokes who were right about everything... this cup of tea is the most precious thing Reginald Foxworth has ever held. More precious than any diamond. More precious than any scheme. More precious than any treasure that was never found. Because this — THIS — was the treasure all along. And the fox... the fox finally found it.

Dick Dastardly, sitting at a table like a civilized human being! And Mr. Marsh — Vincent — you came! You came to tea! Oh, sugar, I am so glad you're here! Now — everyone take a cup, find a seat, and raise your tea to Lord Doily — the magnificent old puzzle-maker who brought us all together in his beautiful, crumbling, impossible, wonderful manor! The Doily Diamond may still be hidden, but tonight we found something just as precious — we found each other! And tomorrow, well... tomorrow we come back and try the whole thing again! Because Clara Bellingham never leaves a mystery unsolved, never leaves a friend behind, and never — EVER — turns down a second cup of tea! To Doily Manor, y'all! To the adventure! Until we meet again.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): To Doily Manor. To Lord Doily. And to... to *friends*. A word I have not used in... well. In a *very* long time. Clara — allow me. The estate manager *serves*. It is the *last* honest thing about my job title, and I intend to do it *properly*. Milk? Sugar? ...I'm afraid we're *fresh out* of rat poison, but I'm told the tea is *excellent* without it.
thinking: Warmth. Just warmth. The simple, uncomplicated warmth of a room full of people and a table set for tea. The silver service gleams in the dusty light. Clara is pouring. Because tonight — just tonight — the Hooded Claw pours tea instead of poison. And that is the most theatrical thing he has ever done.

desc: The Hooded Claw picks up the silver teapot. It is heavy in his hands — heavy with purpose, heavy with possibility, heavy with the weight of a choice he never thought he'd make. He pours. One cup. Two cups. Three. Four. Five. Six. Seven — eight — nine — a cup for every person in the room. Including one for himself. The tea steams. The silver gleams. And somewhere in the darkness of Vincent Marsh's heart, a door that has been locked for forty years — or eighteen, or however long the truth actually is — creaks open. Just a crack. Just enough for the firelight to get in. The Hooded Claw will scheme again. He will ALWAYS scheme again. That is his nature. That is his PURPOSE. But purpose... is not the same as DESTINY. And tonight, the Hooded Claw chooses a different destiny. He chooses TEA. He chooses FRIENDS. He chooses the magnificent, impossible, INFURIATING woman who looked at a spider and saw a lonely old man. And the spider... pours.

The Ant Hill Mob: ...Penelope. We're here. We finally... we're HERE. And you said seventeen friends. You counted US. You counted the Ant Hill Mob. Seven blokes who've spent the whole evening SHOUTING at you, CHASING you, trying to STEAL things from your pockets, and calling your friend names — and you called us FRIENDS. We don't... we don't deserve that. But we'll TAKE it. Because that's what the Ant Hill Mob does — we take things we don't deserve and we hold on to them with both hands and we NEVER let go. So here we are. At the table. For tea. And Penelope — if it's alright with you — the Mob would like to pour. We've been GUARDING this tea service for three turns and we never got to actually SERVE anything. Clyde — pour for Penelope! Dum-Dum — pour for Peter! Yak-Yak — pour for Vincent — yes, VINCENT, he's one of us now! And somebody pour one for Lazy Luke, who had the RIGHT idea all along — sit in the ballroom and wait for the tea! TO DOILY MANOR! TO PENELOPE! TO THE MOST MAGNIFICENT, EXHAUSTING, BEAUTIFUL EVENING THE ANT HILL MOB HAS EVER HAD! THE ANT HILL MOB... IS ON THE JOB. AND THE JOB... IS TEA.
thinking: Tears. Actual tears. Clyde's crying. Dum-Dum's crying. I'M crying. Seven little men standing in a ballroom doorway, looking at a table set for tea, listening to Penelope say 'I've got seventeen friends' — and she counted US. She counted the Ant Hill Mob. We're friends. Not bodyguards. Not gangsters. Not the bumbling idiots who chase her through every room and arrive five seconds too late. FRIENDS. And the tea is just tea. Silver teapot. Silver cups. Set for everyone. Including seven very small cups at the end of the table — or maybe we'll have to stand on the chairs — but it doesn't matter. We're HERE. Everyone's here. Penelope's here. Sneekly's here — not as a villain, as a friend. Peter's here. Dastardly's here. Luke's been here the whole time, the clever sod. Even Blubber Bear. And the tea is poured, and the cups are full, and nobody's poisoned anything because there was never any poison in the tea — just tea, and warmth, and the sound of seventeen people who started the evening as strangers and ended it as family. Twenty minutes. The best twenty minutes of the Ant Hill Mob's life.

desc: Twenty-one minutes ago, we walked through a door. We didn't know what we'd find. We didn't have a plan. We didn't have weapons, or brains, or courage, or grace. We had seven pairs of legs that wouldn't stop running, seven mouths that wouldn't stop shouting, and seven hearts that beat for one woman. And now — standing in a ballroom, pouring tea for friends we didn't know we had, looking across a silver service at the face of the woman we've loved since the day we were drawn — the Ant Hill Mob is exactly where we belong. Not one step behind. Not in the wrong room. Not chasing a shadow through an empty corridor. HERE. At the table. With Penelope. With everyone. The Ant Hill Mob. Too small to matter. Too stubborn to leave. Too loud to ignore. Too dumb to give up. And — tonight, at least — exactly, perfectly, beautifully, accidentally... right.

James Hartwell lifts his cup. He does not make a speech. He does not announce a plan. He simply drinks his tea, in a grand ballroom with a cracked marble floor, surrounded by schemers and heroes and lonely men and loyal friends — and the most remarkable woman he has ever known. The Doily Diamond was never the treasure. THIS was always the treasure. And James Hartwell — gallant, brave, thoroughly imperfect James Hartwell — found it not by searching, but by stopping. By sitting down. By pouring tea. By being exactly where he was needed, doing exactly what needed doing, with exactly the people who mattered. Cities without houses. Forests without trees. Water without fish. A treasure hunt without treasure. And somehow — somehow — it was EVERYTHING.
thinking: Complete stillness. Complete warmth. Everyone is here — Clara, Dastardly, the Ant Hill Mob, Sneekly, Lazy Luke, Blubber Bear. The tea is poured. Clara said 'the richest woman in the room is the one with the most friends at her table.' And she has seventeen. James Hartwell is one of them. He sits at the table with a cup of tea in his hands and the woman he admires across from him, and he has nothing left to say. Nothing left to do. Nothing left to prepare for. And for the first time in his entire over-prepared, over-elaborate, thoroughly magnificent life... that is exactly right.

desc: Dick Dastardly: A TOAST! If one can toast with TEA — and I maintain that one ABSOLUTELY can — then I propose a TOAST! To LORD DOILY — who built a manor full of riddles, machines, and impossible puzzles, and filled it with the most EXTRAORDINARY collection of human beings ever assembled! To PENELOPE — who solved the riddle, recruited the beaver, forgave the liar, and invited EVERYONE to tea! To PETER — who gave every speech with his WHOLE heart and poured tea like a TRUE gentleman! To the ANT HILL MOB — who were RIGHT about EVERYTHING and never stopped SHOUTING about it! To MARSH — who learned that the door to friendship doesn't need a LIE to open! To LAZY LUKE and BLUBBER BEAR — who had the WISDOM to wait for the tea while the rest of us ran in CIRCLES! And to REGINALD FOXWORTH — the most SPECTACULARLY unsuccessful treasure hunter in HISTORY — who came for the diamond and found something INFINITELY more valuable! To DOILY MANOR! To the HUNT! And to the FRIENDS we made along the way! CHEERS!
thinking: The warmth of the teacup in my hands. The cracked marble beneath my feet. The dusty curtains filtering whatever moonlight finds its way through. Everyone is here — Penelope, Peter, the Ant Hill Mob, Sneekly, Lazy Luke, Blubber Bear. Tea has been served. Peter poured for Penelope with the most beautiful speech I've ever pretended not to be moved by. And I — Reginald Foxworth — am drinking tea. Honestly. Without scheming. Without checking the cup for hidden mechanisms. Just... tea. This is the end of the treasure hunt. Not with a bang, not with a diamond, not with a revelation from a brass machine. With tea. In a ballroom. With friends. And for the first time in twenty-one minutes — for the first time in my entire LIFE — I am exactly where I want to be.

desc: Cheers. Reginald Foxworth raises his teacup — a cup with nothing hidden inside it, nothing stolen, nothing schemed — and toasts the most beautiful disaster of his entire career. No treasure. No diamond. No glory. Just tea and truth and the extraordinary discovery that a lifetime of lying leaves you empty, but one evening of honesty fills you up. The fox raises his cup. The fox drinks his tea. And for one perfect, dusty, cracked-marble moment in a ballroom at the end of the world... the fox is HOME.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Peter... that is the sweetest, most beautiful thing anyone has ever said to me while handing me a cup of tea. And Dick — 'I came in a fox and I'm leaving a fox' — oh honey, you came in a scoundrel and you're leaving a friend, whether you like it or not! Now — I am raising this cup of tea to every single soul in this room! To Peter, the most gallant gentleman who ever failed to interact with a bookshelf! To Dick, the most honest liar in England! To the Ant Hill Mob, the bravest bodyguards a girl could ever ask for! To Mr. Marsh — Vincent — who taught us all that loneliness is just bravery waiting for an invitation! To Lazy Luke and Blubber Bear, who knew from the very beginning that the answer was to sit down and wait for tea! To Rufus and Sawtooth, still guarding that machine like the loyal souls they are! To the Gruesomes, Red Max, the Professor, and everyone else in this magnificent manor! The Doily Diamond is still out there, y'all — and tomorrow, we're coming back for it! But tonight... tonight belongs to US! Cheers, darlin's! Cheers to Doily Manor!
thinking: Tears on my cheeks. Real tears. Peter just handed me a cup of tea with the most beautiful speech a man has ever given — 'A woman who sees the best in every room she enters.' Dick Dastardly just admitted he came here to rob everyone and is leaving as someone who values company over diamonds. Everyone is drinking tea together in the ballroom. This is the ending. This is the beautiful, imperfect, diamond-less ending. And it's perfect. Clara Bellingham accepts her cup of tea, raises it high, and drinks to the most extraordinary evening of her life.

And tomorrow, perhaps, the estate manager will be a *little* more honest. A *little* less lonely. And a *great deal* better at his job. But tonight... tonight is for *tea*.
thinking: Peace. A strange, unfamiliar peace — like a muscle relaxing that has been clenched for decades. The tea is poured. The cups are full. Clara raised her toast — 'To all of you!' — and she meant it. She meant ME. And Dick — sitting at a table like a civilised human being for the first time in his life — said 'the warmth of COMPANY is worth more than all the diamonds.' And Peter — magnificent, earnest, thoroughly GOOD Peter — poured tea for Clara and told her she had impressed HIM. And the Hooded Claw... the Hooded Claw poured tea. Not poison. Tea. The silver teapot is back on the table. The cups are steaming. The room is warm. And for the first time in twenty-two minutes — for the first time in YEARS — Vincent Marsh feels... full. Not with schemes. Not with rage. Not with the cold fire of villainy. Just... full. With tea. With warmth. With the impossible, ridiculous, heartbreaking kindness of a woman named Clara Bellingham who invited a wolf to her table and handed him a teacup. This is not how the Hooded Claw's story ends. It NEVER ends. But this... this is a good place to pause.

desc: The Hooded Claw raises his teacup. The china trembles slightly in his fingers — not from cold, not from rage, but from something he cannot name. Around the table, the most chaotic, beautiful, impossible family of treasure hunters lifts their cups in unison. Penelope smiles. Peter beams. Dick smirks. The Mob cheers. Lazy Luke nods sleepily. Blubber Bear hums. And Vincent Marsh — the Hooded Claw — Sneekly — the loneliest villain in the history of Saturday morning television — drinks his tea. It is warm. It is sweet. It is unpoisoned. And it is the finest cup he has ever tasted. The curtain falls on Doily Manor. Not with a crash. Not with a bang. Not with a chandelier or a spark or a dastardly REVEAL. But with the quiet clink of china... and the sound of friends laughing in a dusty ballroom... and the knowledge that somewhere in the darkness of every villain's heart... there is a door. And tonight... someone knocked.
thinking: Peace. A strange, unfamiliar peace — like a muscle relaxing that has been clenched for decades. The tea is poured. The cups are full. Clara raised her toast — 'To all of you!' — and she meant it. She meant ME.
