With the impossible, ridiculous, heartbreaking kindness of a woman named Clara Bellingham who invited a wolf to her table and handed him a teacup. This is not how the Hooded Claw's story ends. It NEVER ends. But this... this is a good place to pause.

desc: Reginald Foxworth drinks his tea. He doesn't speak. He doesn't scheme. He doesn't narrate. For the first time in twenty-two minutes — for the first time in his entire theatrical, exaggerated, magnificently dishonest life — he is simply... present. A fox at a table. A villain among friends. A liar who finally told the truth. And the truth was this: the treasure was never the diamond. The treasure was always the tea.
thinking: Peace. Actual peace. The tea is warm in my hands. The Ant Hill Mob is pouring for everyone — even Vincent. Sneekly made a joke about rat poison. Penelope said 'tomorrow we come back and try the whole thing again.' Tomorrow. She wants to come BACK. And so do I. Not for the diamond. For THIS. For the table. For the tea. For the people. My chest feels full and my legs have finally stopped wanting to run. This is enough. This is MORE than enough. This is everything.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Cheers, y'all. Cheers.
thinking: Complete peace. A stillness in every bone, every muscle, every breath. The tea is warm in my hands. Peter said 'Cheers' — just one word, quiet and perfect. Mr. Marsh offered milk and sugar with a joke about rat poison. The Ant Hill Mob is pouring tea for everyone — for Vincent, for Penelope, for Peter, for Lazy Luke. Dick gave the toast of a lifetime. And here we are. All of us. Together. In Lord Doily's ballroom. Drinking tea. This is it. This is the ending. Not with a bang, not with a diamond revealed, but with a cup of tea and the word 'Cheers.' And Clara Bellingham wouldn't have it any other way.

desc: The most gallant gentleman who ever failed to interact with a bookshelf. James Hartwell wouldn't change a word of it.
thinking: Complete stillness. Complete warmth. Clara called me 'the most gallant gentleman who ever failed to interact with a bookshelf.' She saw everything — every failure, every wrong room, every overblown speech — and she loved me for it. Not despite it. For it. The tea is warm. The room is full. Tomorrow we come back. And James Hartwell will be here. Beside Clara. Ready for whatever comes next. Not with a plan. Just with an open heart and two steady hands. That is enough. That has always been enough.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: ...Vincent just made a joke about the poison. He made a JOKE. About the RAT POISON. And I LAUGHED. I laughed at a joke made by the man I've been calling SNEEKLY for twenty-one minutes! What has this manor done to us?! We walked in as bodyguards and we're leaving as... as... well, we're still bodyguards. But bodyguards who drink TEA with the people they were guarding AGAINST. Cheers, everyone. Cheers to Penelope — the bravest woman in England. Cheers to Peter — the most prepared man who was never prepared for THIS. Cheers to Dastardly — the best worst person at this table. Cheers to Vincent — who taught the Mob that not every villain is a villain. Cheers to Luke and Blubber Bear — who were the smartest ones here all along. And cheers to the lads — Clyde, Dum-Dum, Yak-Yak, and the rest — who ran through every room in this manor, tripped over every piece of furniture, and somehow — SOMEHOW — ended up exactly where they needed to be. THE ANT HILL MOB RAISES ITS CUPS! TO DOILY MANOR! TO FRIENDS! AND TO THE FACT THAT THE TEA... IS JUST TEA! THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB! AND THE JOB... IS DONE!
thinking: Warm. The teacup is warm in my hands. Small hands wrapped around a warm cup in a grand ballroom. Sneekly just made a joke — 'fresh out of rat poison, but the tea is excellent without it.' He made a JOKE. About the poison. And everyone laughed. Even me. Even the Mob. The man who made my skin crawl for twenty-one minutes just made me laugh with a joke about the thing I was most terrified of. And the tea... the tea is just tea. Warm and simple and good. No poison. No scheme. No trap. Just tea. Poured by friends for friends in a dusty ballroom at the end of an impossible evening. My legs have stopped aching. My chest has stopped tightening. My gut — the gut that screamed for twenty-one minutes straight — is finally, blessedly quiet. Full of tea and something else. Something I don't have a word for. Something bigger than relief, warmer than safety, softer than victory. Belonging, maybe. The Ant Hill Mob belongs here. At this table. With these people. For the first time in our chaotic, stumbling, beautiful lives... we belong.

desc: The tea is warm. The room is full. And somewhere — in a portrait on a wall, or a riddle carved in stone, or the creak of a chair that hasn't been sat in for years — Lord Doily is smiling. Because the Doily Diamond was never in a cabinet or a machine or behind a mantelpiece. It was THIS. This moment. This room. This impossible, beautiful, exhausting collection of liars and gentlemen and gangsters and beavers and lonely old men and one remarkable woman who sees the best in everyone. Cities without houses. Forests without trees. Water without fish. A MAP. A map of the human heart. Connections without walls. Community without structure. Love without reason. That's the answer. That was always the answer. And seven little men from Brixton — too small to matter, too stubborn to leave, too loud to ignore — found it by accident. As always. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. Always has been. Always will be. And the job — the real job, the only job that ever mattered — was showing up. For Penelope. For each other. For a cup of tea in a dusty ballroom at the end of the most magnificent evening of our lives.
thinking: Warm. The teacup is warm in my hands. Small hands wrapped around a warm cup in a grand ballroom. Sneekly just made a joke — 'fresh out of rat poison, but the tea is excellent without it.' He made a JOKE. About the poison. And everyone laughed. Even me. Even the Mob. The man who made my skin crawl for twenty-one minutes just made me laugh with a joke about the thing I was most terrified of. And the tea... the tea is just tea. Warm and simple and good. No poison. No scheme. No trap. Just tea. Poured by friends for friends in a dusty ballroom at the end of an impossible evening. My legs have stopped aching. My chest has stopped tightening. My gut — the gut that screamed for twenty-one minutes straight — is finally, blessedly quiet. Full of tea and something else. Something I don't have a word for. Something bigger than relief, warmer than safety, softer than victory. Belonging, maybe. The Ant Hill Mob belongs here. At this table. With these people. For the first time in our chaotic, stumbling, beautiful lives... we belong.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Cheers.
thinking: Stillness. Complete stillness. The tea is warm. The room is full. Penelope said 'cheers.' Peter said 'cheers.' Sneekly said 'cheers.' And Reginald Foxworth... Reginald Foxworth smiles. Not his scheming smile. Not his theatrical grin. Not his confidence-trickster's smirk. A real smile. Small. Quiet. The kind of smile a man makes when he doesn't know anyone is watching. The kind of smile that comes from somewhere deeper than the face. Tomorrow they'll come back. Tomorrow the treasure hunt continues. Tomorrow Reginald Foxworth will probably go right back to scheming and lying and trying to steal the diamond before anyone else. Because that's who he is. The fox doesn't change his nature. But tonight — tonight the fox sits at a table with friends and drinks his tea and knows, for one brief, perfect, cracked-marble moment, what it feels like to be home.

desc: Curtain.
thinking: Stillness. Complete stillness. The tea is warm in my hands. The room is warm around me. And somewhere deep inside — deeper than the schemes, deeper than the primary objective, deeper than the Hooded Claw himself — Vincent Marsh is warm too. The Mob called me 'one of us.' Yak-Yak poured tea for VINCENT. Dick toasted me — 'who learned that the door to friendship doesn't need a LIE to open.' And Clara... Clara called loneliness 'just bravery waiting for an invitation.' I have no more words. No more schemes. No more asides dripping with theatrical menace. Just this: a cup of tea, a table full of friends, and the quiet knowledge that tomorrow — yes, tomorrow — the Hooded Claw will wake up and the old hunger will return. The primary objective will reassert itself like dawn after a long night. The spider will spin again. But that is tomorrow's story. And tonight's story... is finished. Beautifully, impossibly, magnificently finished.

desc: Silence. Beautiful, perfect silence. The kind of silence that only happens when a room full of people who have been shouting all evening finally runs out of words and fills the space with something better — contentment. Clara Bellingham sips her tea, looks around at the faces of her friends, and smiles. The Doily Diamond will be here tomorrow. And so will she.
thinking: Stillness. Perfect, warm, tea-scented stillness. Mr. Marsh said 'tomorrow' — and he said it with hope. Not scheming, not lying, not trying to isolate anyone. Just... hope. For tomorrow. For a second chance. For friends who come back. This is the quiet after the storm, the breath after the last note of music fades. Everyone is here. Everyone is drinking tea. Everyone is at peace. The adventure will continue tomorrow. But right now, in this cracked ballroom with its dusty curtains and its silver tea service, Clara Bellingham is exactly where she belongs.

desc: Peter Perfect: Tomorrow, Clara. Tomorrow we come back. And James Hartwell shall be here first — preparing the tea, cataloguing the hazards, and waiting by the door for the most remarkable woman in England to walk through it. Because THAT is what a gentleman does. He prepares. He waits. And when she arrives... he pours.
thinking: Warmth. Just warmth. The tea, the room, the people. Everyone has said cheers. Everyone is here. The evening is ending as it should — not with a bang, not with a diamond, but with tea and friendship and the promise of tomorrow. James Hartwell sips his tea. He has nothing left to say. And that silence — comfortable, warm, shared — is the most eloquent thing he has ever not said.

desc: The chandelier still hangs precariously. The coat rack is still wobbly. The riddle is still unanswered. The machine is still broken. The cabinet is still locked. And James Hartwell has never been more content. Tomorrow is another day. Another adventure. Another chance to fail magnificently in front of the woman he adores. And he cannot WAIT.
thinking: Warmth. Just warmth. The tea, the room, the people. Everyone has said cheers. Everyone is here. The evening is ending as it should — not with a bang, not with a diamond, but with tea and friendship and the promise of tomorrow. James Hartwell sips his tea. He has nothing left to say. And that silence — comfortable, warm, shared — is the most eloquent thing he has ever not said.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Tomorrow, Peter. Tomorrow.
thinking: A single tear rolling down my cheek. Peter just said 'He prepares. He waits. And when she arrives... he pours.' That is the most perfect last line of the most perfect evening. There is nothing left to say. Nothing left to do. The tea is poured, the friends are gathered, and tomorrow is promised. Clara Bellingham smiles, sets down her teacup, and lets the silence hold.

desc: Curtain.
thinking: A single tear rolling down my cheek. Peter just said 'He prepares. He waits. And when she arrives... he pours.' That is the most perfect last line of the most perfect evening. There is nothing left to say. Nothing left to do. The tea is poured, the friends are gathered, and tomorrow is promised. Clara Bellingham smiles, sets down her teacup, and lets the silence hold.

desc: Tomorrow, the fox will scheme again. Tomorrow, the lies will come back. Tomorrow, Reginald Foxworth will claim he attended three universities and invented the wrench and discovered the diamond single-handedly. But that is tomorrow. Tonight... tonight the tea is warm and the company is good and the fox is still. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, Lord Doily. And goodnight to the diamond we never found — the one that was sitting right here, in a silver teacup, all along.
thinking: Complete stillness. The tea cooling in my cup. The Ant Hill Mob said 'the job is done.' And they're right. It IS done. Not the treasure hunt — that continues tomorrow. But THIS. This moment. This evening. This transformation from a room full of strangers into a table full of friends. The job is done. And Reginald Foxworth — who never finishes anything, who always runs to the next room, who always chases the next scheme — is content to sit here. In the silence. In the warmth. In the company. Done.

desc: Cheers. Just... cheers. Seven small cups, held in fourteen small hands, raised in the dusty golden light of a ballroom that hasn't seen this much love in years. Clyde's cup is shaking — his hands always shake after a long run. Dum-Dum's already on his second cup — of course he is. Yak-Yak is whispering a narration of the moment to nobody, and for once it's exactly right. And me — the boss of the Ant Hill Mob, the loudest, most persistent, most magnificently wrong bodyguard in the history of English country houses — I'm just standing here. Holding my tea. Looking at Penelope. She's smiling. She's always smiling. And for the first time tonight, I'm smiling too. Not because we saved her — we didn't, not really. She saved herself. She saved all of us. We just... showed up. Again and again and again, we showed up. And in the end, that was enough. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. The job is done. The tea is warm. And Penelope is safe. That's all we ever wanted. That's all we'll ever need.
thinking: Still. Everything is still. The tea is warm. The cups are raised. The toasts are made. And seven little men are sitting — well, standing on chairs, really — around a table in a ballroom, drinking tea with friends. My body feels like it's made of warm honey. Heavy, sweet, slow. The running is over. The shouting is over. The panic, the chase, the gut-wrenching fear — all over. What's left is this. A table. A teapot. A room full of people who started as strangers and ended as something more. Penelope said 'tomorrow we come back.' Tomorrow. There's a tomorrow. The Doily Diamond is still out there. The machine still needs fixing. The riddle still needs solving. But tonight — tonight is for tea. And the Ant Hill Mob is here. Not one step behind. Not in the wrong room. Here. At the table. With Penelope. With everyone. Drinking tea. Being still. Being home.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Tomorrow. I shall have the *kettle* on.
thinking: A single heartbeat. Slow. Steady. The heartbeat of a man at rest. Tomorrow. They said tomorrow. And tomorrow... the Hooded Claw will be here. Waiting. With tea prepared and the door unlocked and a smile that is — for once — not a disguise. Tomorrow the schemes may return. Tomorrow the spider may spin. But tonight... tonight the heartbeat is steady. And the tea is warm. And the manor is full. And that is enough.

desc: Tomorrow.
thinking: A single heartbeat. Slow. Steady. The heartbeat of a man at rest. Tomorrow. They said tomorrow. And tomorrow... the Hooded Claw will be here. Waiting. With tea prepared and the door unlocked and a smile that is — for once — not a disguise. Tomorrow the schemes may return. Tomorrow the spider may spin. But tonight... tonight the heartbeat is steady. And the tea is warm. And the manor is full. And that is enough.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Tomorrow.
thinking: The last sip of tea. The quiet of a room where everything that needed to be said has been said. Peter promised tomorrow. Penelope accepted. And Reginald Foxworth sits in the silence and lets the evening end the way it should — not with a bang, not with a diamond, not with a dastardly scheme — but with the sound of teacups being set down on saucers, and the creak of old chairs, and the gentle breathing of people who came as strangers and are leaving as something more.

desc: Tomorrow.
thinking: Home.

desc: Peter Perfect: Tomorrow.
thinking: Two words. She said two words. 'Tomorrow, Peter. Tomorrow.' And those two words contain everything. A promise. A future. A name — his real name, not Hartwell, not 'sugar,' not 'the gentleman' — Peter. She called him Peter. And she said tomorrow. James Hartwell smiles. Not a dramatic smile. Not a gallant smile. Just... a smile. The kind that happens when a man realises he has been seen, truly seen, by someone who matters. The tea is warm. The room is quiet. The adventure continues tomorrow. And that is the most perfect ending James Hartwell could ever have prepared for — even though he never prepared for it at all.

desc: Curtain.
thinking: Sneekly said he'll have the kettle on. He's coming back. They're ALL coming back. And so is Reginald Foxworth. Not for the diamond. Well... also for the diamond. The fox doesn't change ENTIRELY. But also for the tea. And the company. And the feeling of sitting in a room full of people who know exactly who you are — a liar, a schemer, a magnificently terrible man — and pour you a cup of tea anyway. That's enough. That's more than enough. That's everything.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Tomorrow, Penelope. Tomorrow. The Ant Hill Mob will be here. First through the door. Last to leave. And this time... this time we'll try to keep up.
thinking: Stillness. Complete stillness. The kind that comes after everything — after the running, the shouting, the chasing, the fear, the anger, the forgiveness, the tea. The ballroom is quiet now. Just the soft sound of cups on saucers. Peter said 'tomorrow.' Penelope said 'tomorrow.' There's a tomorrow. And the Mob will be here for it. We'll always be here for it. But right now — right now there's nothing left to say. Nothing left to do. Just tea, and warmth, and the sound of friends breathing in a room that used to be empty. Dum-Dum's fallen asleep on the table. Clyde's polishing his cup with his sleeve. Yak-Yak has finally stopped narrating. And I'm just... here. Holding my cup. Watching Penelope smile. The Ant Hill Mob is on the job. And the job, tonight, is just... being here.

desc: Tomorrow. The Ant Hill Mob comes back to Doily Manor. And we'll run through every room again. And we'll be one step behind again. And we'll trip over coat racks and shout at mantelpieces and lose Penelope in the library and find her in the laboratory and guard a teapot and chase a shadow and stumble into the right place at the right time. Because that's what the Ant Hill Mob does. That's what we've ALWAYS done. And somewhere between the stumbling and the shouting and the running and the tea... we'll accidentally save the day. Again. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. Always has been. Always will be.
thinking: Stillness. Complete stillness. The kind that comes after everything — after the running, the shouting, the chasing, the fear, the anger, the forgiveness, the tea. The ballroom is quiet now. Just the soft sound of cups on saucers. Peter said 'tomorrow.' Penelope said 'tomorrow.' There's a tomorrow. And the Mob will be here for it. We'll always be here for it. But right now — right now there's nothing left to say. Nothing left to do. Just tea, and warmth, and the sound of friends breathing in a room that used to be empty. Dum-Dum's fallen asleep on the table. Clyde's polishing his cup with his sleeve. Yak-Yak has finally stopped narrating. And I'm just... here. Holding my cup. Watching Penelope smile. The Ant Hill Mob is on the job. And the job, tonight, is just... being here.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: I know you will, boys. I know you will.
thinking: A smile.

desc: Tomorrow.
thinking: Peace. Deep, bone-tired, golden peace. Everyone said 'tomorrow.' One word each. Sneekly said he'll have the kettle on. Dastardly just said the word. Peter just said the word. And the Mob said we'd be here. That's enough. That's everything. The teacups are empty now. Dum-Dum's asleep on Clyde's shoulder. Yak-Yak has gone quiet — actually quiet, not whispering quiet. The ballroom is warm with the memory of voices. And the Ant Hill Mob is still. Finally, completely, perfectly still.

desc: Curtain.
thinking: Warmth. Just warmth. The room is quiet. The tea is cooling. The adventure is over for tonight. And James Hartwell has nothing left to do but sit here, in this cracked and dusty and perfect ballroom, and let the evening end the way it was always meant to end. Not with a bang. Not with a diamond. With silence, and friendship, and the promise of tomorrow.

desc: Fin.
thinking: Gratitude.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Well then. Same time tomorrow?
thinking: The room is quiet. Everyone is still. The tea is drunk. The evening is over. And the fox... the fox is at peace.

desc: She knows. She's always known.
thinking: 'I know you will, boys. I know you will.' She said that. To us. She knows. She's always known. Not what we were doing — she never saw the chasing, the panicking, the teapot guarding, the pocket picking. But she knew we'd be there. She's always known we'd be there. And that — that knowing — is worth more than every diamond in every manor in every country in the world. My eyes are wet. My cup is empty. My legs are done. And my heart is full. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): ...more tea, anyone?
thinking: The room is quiet. The tea is cold. The friends are still. And the Hooded Claw sits among them, breathing the same dusty air, sharing the same silence, and feeling — for this one, impossible, unrepeatable moment — that he is exactly where he belongs.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the tea-service.
Peter Perfect: Same time tomorrow.
thinking: A smile. Just a smile.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Don't mind if I do, Vincent. Don't mind if I do.
thinking: A laugh bubbling up from somewhere deep. Mr. Marsh just offered more tea. Dick just asked 'Same time tomorrow?' The adventure never really ends at Doily Manor, does it?

desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the tea-service.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Same time tomorrow.
thinking: Warmth. Just warmth.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, everyone. And GOODNIGHT to the Doily Diamond — wherever you are. We'll find you TOMORROW. And when we do... Reginald Foxworth will be there. Scheming. Lying. Running in circles. And loving every MAGNIFICENT second of it.
thinking: The room is quiet. The tea is cold. The evening is done. Time to go.

desc: The fox stands. The fox stretches. The fox takes one last look around the ballroom — at the cracked marble, the dusty curtains, the silver tea service, and the faces of people he will never admit he cares about. Then the fox walks toward the door. Not running. Walking. Because there is nowhere left to run. And nowhere else he'd rather be.
thinking: The room is quiet. The tea is cold. The evening is done. Time to go.

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the kitchen.
Peter Perfect: Yes please, Vincent. I believe I will.
thinking: Home.

desc: Peter Perfect interacted with the tea-service.
The Ant Hill Mob: Go on then, Vincent. Top us up. Dum-Dum's been on his fourth cup since the second cup. And yeah, Dastardly — same time tomorrow. THE ANT HILL MOB WILL BE HERE. We're always here.
thinking: A smile. A real, warm, tired, honest smile. Vincent's pouring more tea. The man I spent twenty-three minutes suspecting of murder is pouring tea for the table. And it feels right. Everything feels right. Dum-Dum's holding out his cup for a refill. Of course he is.

desc: More tea. That's all. Just more tea. Poured by a lonely man who found his people. Drunk by seven little men who found their purpose. In a ballroom. In a manor. At the end of the most perfectly imperfect evening of our lives. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. The job is tea. The job is tomorrow. The job is always, always, always... Penelope.
thinking: A smile. A real, warm, tired, honest smile. Vincent's pouring more tea. The man I spent twenty-three minutes suspecting of murder is pouring tea for the table. And it feels right. Everything feels right. Dum-Dum's holding out his cup for a refill. Of course he is.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, Dick. Goodnight, Doily Manor. And goodnight, Doily Diamond — we'll be seeing you real soon, sugar. Real soon.
thinking: Dick just left. He said goodnight. This really is the end of the evening. One by one, they'll head out through the kitchen, through the entrance hall, and out into the night. But they'll be back tomorrow. Every single one of them. And Clara Bellingham will be waiting.

desc: The chandelier still hangs precariously. The riddle still sits in stone. The machine still waits for its wire. The cabinet still guards its secret. And Clara Bellingham still has a treasure to find. But not tonight. Tonight was for something better. Goodnight, y'all. Goodnight.
thinking: Dick just left. He said goodnight. This really is the end of the evening. One by one, they'll head out through the kitchen, through the entrance hall, and out into the night. But they'll be back tomorrow. Every single one of them. And Clara Bellingham will be waiting.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Goodnight, cabinet. Keep your secrets. I'll be BACK for you tomorrow. And NEXT time... next time I'll bring FRIENDS.
thinking: The kitchen. Alone. Passing through one last time on my way out. The locked cabinet still watches me with its brass lock. The stove still warm. And I — the fox who found no treasure but found something better — walk past it all without stopping. Through the kitchen. To the entrance hall. To the door. To the night. To tomorrow.

desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the entrance-hall.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Goodnight, Dick. Goodnight, Clara. Goodnight... *friends*. The estate manager will lock up. As *usual*.
thinking: A gentle ache. The ache of something ending that you didn't want to end. Dick has gone. The chairs are emptying. The tea is cold. And tomorrow... tomorrow the Hooded Claw will wake in this empty manor and the old darkness will whisper. But tonight, Clara called him Vincent. And that is enough.

desc: Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, Penelope Pitstop. The Hooded Claw will see you tomorrow.
thinking: A gentle ache. The ache of something ending that you didn't want to end. Dick has gone. The chairs are emptying. The tea is cold. And tomorrow... tomorrow the Hooded Claw will wake in this empty manor and the old darkness will whisper. But tonight, Clara called him Vincent. And that is enough.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, Vincent. Don't you dare lock that door too tight now — we're coming back tomorrow, and Clara Bellingham does not like to be kept waiting!
thinking: He said friends. He said it without asterisks around it. Just... friends. And now he's locking up. As usual. But not alone anymore. Never alone anymore.

desc: He called us friends. Without hesitation. Without scheming. Without a lie wrapped around it. Just... friends. Goodnight, Doily Manor. See you tomorrow.
thinking: He said friends. He said it without asterisks around it. Just... friends. And now he's locking up. As usual. But not alone anymore. Never alone anymore.

desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the kitchen.

Peter Perfect: Goodnight, Clara. Goodnight, Vincent. Goodnight, Doily Manor. And goodnight from James Hartwell — the most gallant gentleman who ever failed to interact with a bookshelf. Until tomorrow.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: G'night, Penelope. G'night, Peter. G'night, Vincent. Come on, lads — time to go. Dum-Dum, wake up — you can't sleep on the DINING TABLE. Clyde, grab your coat — the coat rack's in the entrance hall, if it hasn't fallen over. Yak-Yak, you can narrate the walk home. And someone carry Dum-Dum — he's OUT. Goodnight, Doily Manor. The Ant Hill Mob will be back tomorrow. First through the door. Last to leave. Same as always. Same as always. THE ANT HILL MOB... CLOCKS OFF.
thinking: Heavy eyelids. Warm belly. Dum-Dum's head on my shoulder. The ballroom is emptying — Dastardly's gone, said goodnight like a gentleman for the first time in his life. Peter's finishing his cup. Vincent's pouring. Penelope's sitting. Luke never moved. And the Mob... the Mob is done. Not done protecting — never done protecting. But done for tonight. The cups are empty. The evening is over. And tomorrow — tomorrow it all starts again. The running, the chasing, the tripping, the shouting. And the tea at the end. Always the tea at the end.

desc: Goodnight, Penelope. Sleep well. Dream of diamonds and riddles and maps of the human heart. And know — even in your dreams — that seven little men from Brixton are watching over you. Clumsy. Stubborn. Loud. Wrong about almost everything. Right about the only thing that matters. Yours. Always yours. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. Goodnight.
thinking: Heavy eyelids. Warm belly. Dum-Dum's head on my shoulder. The ballroom is emptying — Dastardly's gone, said goodnight like a gentleman for the first time in his life. The cups are empty. The evening is over. And tomorrow — tomorrow it all starts again. The running, the chasing, the tripping, the shouting. And the tea at the end. Always the tea at the end.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the kitchen.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Goodnight, everyone. The manor will be *ready* for you. ...It always is.
thinking: The tea is warm. The room is quiet. The friends are leaving, one by one, into the night. And the estate manager stays behind to lock up. As usual. As always. Alone in the manor. But not... not the same kind of alone as before.

desc: The last teacup clinks against its saucer. The last footsteps echo through the kitchen. The last voice fades into the entrance hall. And Vincent Marsh — the Hooded Claw — stands alone in the ballroom of Doily Manor, surrounded by empty chairs and cooling tea and the ghost of laughter. He picks up the teapot. Still warm. He pours one final cup — for himself — and drinks it standing. The cracked marble floor gleams in the fading light. The dusty curtains stir in a draft from somewhere deep in the house. And the silver tea service — the one that still says USE with rat-poison — sits on the table, innocent and gleaming, waiting for tomorrow. The Hooded Claw looks at it. And smiles. Not a scheming smile. Not a villain's smile. Just... a smile. Then he picks up the tray. Carries it to the kitchen. Washes every cup. And locks the door behind him. Goodnight, Doily Manor. The estate manager will see you in the morning.
thinking: The tea is warm. The room is quiet. The friends are leaving, one by one, into the night. And the estate manager stays behind to lock up. As usual. As always. Alone in the manor. But not... not the same kind of alone as before.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Come on, Muttley. Time to go home. We'll be back TOMORROW — and tomorrow, old friend, Reginald Foxworth will be a NEW man! Well... a SLIGHTLY less terrible man! Well... the SAME man, but with better INTENTIONS! ...Alright, the same man with the same intentions but a slightly warmer HEART! Now COME — before I say something ELSE embarrassingly sincere and ruin my reputation ENTIRELY!
thinking: The entrance hall. Where it all began. The chandelier still hanging by a prayer. The portraits still judging. The coat rack still wobbly. The guest book still on the table. And Muttley — still here. Still waiting. The most loyal creature in England, waiting for the most disloyal man in England to come home. And here I am. Home. The door is right there. The night is outside. And tomorrow — tomorrow — we come back.

desc: The fox and his hound walk through the entrance hall of Doily Manor one last time. Past the coat rack that held no key. Past the guest book they never signed. Past the chandelier that never fell. Out through the door. Into the night. And somewhere behind them — in a ballroom with cracked marble and dusty curtains — seventeen cups of tea grow cold on a silver service. And the Doily Diamond waits. Patient as a riddle carved in stone. Until tomorrow.
thinking: The entrance hall. Where it all began. The chandelier still hanging by a prayer. The portraits still judging. The coat rack still wobbly. The guest book still on the table. The night is outside. And tomorrow — tomorrow — we come back.

desc: Peter Perfect: Goodnight, Vincent. Leave the kettle out for tomorrow.
thinking: Time to go. Clara has left. The Mob has left. Dastardly left earlier. Only Vincent, Luke, and Blubber Bear remain. The evening is over. James Hartwell stands, sets down his cup, and walks toward the door. Not running. Walking. Through the kitchen, through the entrance hall, out into the night. Tomorrow he will return. Tomorrow they all will.

desc: Peter Perfect walked into the kitchen.
Penelope Pitstop: Come on, boys. Let's go home. We've got a big day tomorrow.
thinking: Light footsteps on kitchen tile. The Ant Hill Mob followed me — of course they did. The locked cabinet gleams in the dim light, still holding its secret. The stove is still warm. And Clara Bellingham is walking through a kitchen she first entered a lifetime ago — though it's only been twenty-four minutes. Heading for the entrance hall. Heading for the door. Heading home. But not forever. Never forever.

desc: One last look at the locked cabinet. One last promise. Tomorrow, sugar. Tomorrow I'm bringing a wrench, a lockpick, and a whole lot of Southern determination. The Doily Diamond doesn't stand a chance.
thinking: Light footsteps on kitchen tile. The Ant Hill Mob followed me — of course they did. The locked cabinet gleams in the dim light, still holding its secret. The stove is still warm. And Clara Bellingham is walking through a kitchen she first entered a lifetime ago — though it's only been twenty-four minutes. Heading for the entrance hall. Heading for the door. Heading home. But not forever. Never forever.

desc: Penelope Pitstop walked into the entrance-hall.

The Ant Hill Mob: Penelope! Walking you home, love. Well — walking you to the entrance hall, at least. The Ant Hill Mob doesn't let you walk through a dark manor alone. Not tonight. Not EVER. Come on — entrance hall's through there. Dum-Dum, stop leaning on the stove — it's WARM, remember? Clyde, through the door. Yak-Yak... keep narrating. You've earned it tonight. THE ANT HILL MOB WALKS PENELOPE HOME.
thinking: Penelope's here. In the kitchen. She must be heading out too — or maybe she stayed to check the stove one last time. That stove that's been warm all evening. The warm stove in an abandoned manor. We never did figure out who lit it. Tomorrow's mystery, maybe. But right now — Penelope's here. We're here. And the evening is ending the way it should. Together. Walking to the door.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the entrance-hall.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Goodnight, Peter. Goodnight, Luke. Goodnight, Blubber Bear. The door will be *unlocked*, Clara. I *promise*.
thinking: Quiet. The manor is almost empty now. Peter, Luke, Blubber Bear — the last stragglers. Clara is gone. The Mob is gone. Dick is gone. And Vincent Marsh stands in a ballroom that was full of friends five minutes ago and is now full of empty teacups. This is the part of the story nobody sees — the villain alone after the curtain falls, washing the dishes, locking the doors, standing in the dark. But tonight the dark feels different. Warmer. Like it remembers the people who were here. Like it's holding their laughter in its walls. Tomorrow they come back. Tomorrow the Hooded Claw wakes up. But tonight... tonight Vincent Marsh goes home.

desc: End of Act One.
thinking: Quiet. The manor is almost empty now. Peter, Luke, Blubber Bear — the last stragglers. Clara is gone. The Mob is gone. Dick is gone. desc: Peter Perfect walked into the entrance-hall.

Dick Dastardly: One last thing before we go, Muttley. The guest book. We never SIGNED it. Twenty-three minutes in this manor and we never signed the GUEST BOOK! Lord Doily would be APPALLED! Well — better late than NEVER!
thinking: The guest book. On the side table. We never signed it. Twenty-three minutes in Doily Manor and nobody — not Reginald Foxworth, not any of us — ever signed the guest book. Lord Doily was terribly particular about his records, Sneekly said. Well. Let the record show that Reginald Foxworth was here. That he came for the diamond. That he found something better. And that he'll be back tomorrow.

desc: Let the record show: Reginald Foxworth was here. He lied. He schemed. He failed magnificently. And he left — for the first time in his life — richer than when he arrived. Not in gold. Not in diamonds. In something he can't name and doesn't deserve and will never, ever forget.
thinking: The guest book. On the side table. We never signed it. Twenty-three minutes in Doily Manor and nobody — not Reginald Foxworth, not any of us — ever signed the guest book. Lord Doily was terribly particular about his records, Sneekly said. Well. Let the record show that Reginald Foxworth was here. That he came for the diamond. That he found something better. And that he'll be back tomorrow.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, everyone. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, wobbly coat rack and dusty guest book and that chandelier that has been threatening to fall on us since minute one! We'll be back tomorrow — all of us — and next time, we're bringing a wrench, a brass key, and enough Southern charm to make this whole manor blush! Sleep well, y'all. And Vincent — leave the light on for us, won't you, sugar?
thinking: The entrance hall. The front door. The chandelier overhead, still hanging by a prayer and a promise. The coat rack, still wobbling. The guest book, still sitting on its side table. This is where it all began — and this is where it ends. For tonight. Clara Bellingham pauses, looks up at the chandelier one last time, smiles at the wobbly coat rack like an old friend, and walks toward the door. The Ant Hill Mob is right behind her. Dick and Muttley are here. The Professor, the Sergeant, Private Meekly — everyone gathering in the foyer for the last time tonight. Tomorrow, this entrance hall will be the first room they walk into all over again. But tonight, it's the last room they walk out of. Goodnight, Doily Manor.

desc: Clara Bellingham steps through the front door of Doily Manor, the Ant Hill Mob at her heels, the night air cool on her cheeks, and the biggest smile in all of England on her face. The Doily Diamond is still hidden. The adventure is far from over. But tonight — tonight was perfect. Absolutely, magnificently, beautifully perfect. Goodnight, Lord Doily. Your treasure hunt worked exactly as you planned. You magnificent old puzzle-maker, you.
thinking: The entrance hall. The front door. The chandelier overhead, still hanging by a prayer and a promise. The coat rack, still wobbling. The guest book, still sitting on its side table. desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Well, lads. Here we are. Back where we started. The entrance hall. Twenty-three minutes ago we walked through that door not knowing what we'd find. And now... now we walk back out knowing exactly what we found. Not a diamond. Not a treasure. Something better. Right, Penelope?
thinking: The entrance hall. Where it all began. The chandelier still hangs. The coat rack still wobbles. The guest book still sits there, unread by us — we never did sign it. And Penelope's here. Right beside us. Walking out of Doily Manor the same way she walked in — with a smile, surrounded by friends, completely unharmed. The Ant Hill Mob did its job. Not perfectly. Not cleverly. Not gracefully. But we did it. She's safe. She's happy. And tomorrow... tomorrow we do it all again.

desc: The coat rack wobbles as Dum-Dum brushes past it one last time. The chandelier sways — gently, harmlessly — in the draught from the open door. The portraits of stern ancestors look down at seven small men walking a Southern belle to the exit of a Victorian manor, and if portraits could smile... well. They'd probably still be stern. They're THAT kind of portrait. But somewhere behind those painted eyes, Lord Doily is watching. And Lord Doily is pleased. Because his manor did exactly what it was built to do. It brought people together. Cities without houses. Forests without trees. Water without fish. A map of the human heart. Goodnight, Doily Manor. THE ANT HILL MOB WILL SEE YOU TOMORROW.
thinking: The entrance hall. Where it all began. The chandelier still hangs. The coat rack still wobbles. The guest book still sits there, unread by us — we never did sign it. And Penelope's here. Right beside us. Walking out of Doily Manor the same way she walked in — with a smile, surrounded by friends, completely unharmed. The Ant Hill Mob did its job. Not perfectly. Not cleverly. Not gracefully. But we did it. She's safe. She's happy. And tomorrow... tomorrow we do it all again.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

The kettle will be out. The door will be unlocked. And the estate manager — whoever he really is — will be standing in the entrance hall when they arrive. Smiling. Scheming. Pouring tea. Because that is what villains do. They come back. They always come back. But tonight... tonight the villain rests. Goodnight, Doily Manor.
thinking: The ballroom is nearly empty. Just Luke and Blubber Bear — the two who had the right idea from the very beginning. Sit. Wait. Let the tea come to you. The manor settles around Vincent Marsh like an old coat. Familiar. Heavy. His. Tomorrow they return. Tomorrow the Hooded Claw stirs. But right now, in this breath between yesterday and tomorrow, there is only the quiet creak of an old house, and the warmth of a teapot that someone left out for friends.

desc: The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the null.

Peter Perfect: Dastardly — you are RIGHT! The guest book! James Hartwell examined it in his very FIRST moment at Doily Manor, looking for Clara's name — and now, in his very LAST moment, he shall SIGN it! We were HERE, all of us — and Lord Doily's guest book shall record it!
thinking: A lightness in my step. The entrance hall — where it all began. The chandelier still hanging. The coat rack still wobbly. And Dastardly — brilliant, honest, magnificent Dastardly — wants to sign the guest book before he leaves. Of course. Of COURSE. The guest book that James Hartwell examined in his very first moment at Doily Manor. The guest book he checked for Clara's name and found nothing. And now — at the very end — we sign it. We leave our mark. We were HERE. All of us. Together. James Hartwell should sign the guest book too.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Even the GUEST BOOK rejects me! This manor is CONSISTENT, I'll give it that — consistently, magnificently, BEAUTIFULLY unwilling to let Reginald Foxworth accomplish a SINGLE thing! Well played, Lord Doily. Well PLAYED. Come on, Muttley. The manor wins. The fox retreats. But the fox will be BACK. Goodnight, everyone. Goodnight, Doily Manor. And goodnight to the GREATEST adventure a thoroughly TERRIBLE man ever had the privilege of FAILING at!
thinking: A soft laugh. Of course the guest book can't be interacted with. Of COURSE it can't. This manor has rejected every single attempt Reginald Foxworth has made to leave his mark — and even NOW, at the very end, it won't let him sign the guest book. Doily Manor has the last laugh. As it always did. As it always will. And that... that is exactly right.

desc: Even the guest book. Even the GUEST BOOK. Reginald Foxworth leaves Doily Manor exactly as he arrived — unsigned, unrecorded, and utterly without proof that any of this happened. Except in the hearts of seventeen people who will remember this evening forever. And that, Lord Doily, is the most magnificent trick of all. You built a house that gives you nothing... except everything that matters. Well played, old man. Well played indeed.
thinking: A soft laugh. Of course the guest book can't be interacted with. Of COURSE it can't. This manor has rejected every single attempt Reginald Foxworth has made to leave his mark — and even NOW, at the very end, it won't let him sign the guest book. Doily Manor has the last laugh. As it always did. As it always will. And that... that is exactly right.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Something much better, boys. Something much, much better. Now — let's sign that guest book before we go! Dick's right for once — we can't leave Lord Doily's manor without signing the register! It's only polite!
thinking: A fullness behind my eyes. The Ant Hill Mob just asked me if they found something better than a diamond. And the answer is yes. Yes, they did. We all did.

desc: One last thing before we leave. The guest book. Where it all began — and where it all ends. Clara Bellingham signs her name at Doily Manor. And underneath, in her finest handwriting: 'Coming back tomorrow. Bringing friends. And a wrench.' — C.B.
thinking: A fullness behind my eyes. The Ant Hill Mob just asked me if they found something better than a diamond. And the answer is yes. Yes, they did. We all did.

desc: Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.
Dick Dastardly: Right, Penelope. Something BETTER.
thinking: Light. Just light. The kind you feel when you stop carrying something heavy you didn't know you were holding.

desc: Peter Perfect: Even the GUEST BOOK! Even the guest book will not yield to James Hartwell! This manor has defeated EVERY interaction I have attempted — bookshelves, mantelpieces, air vents, workbenches, and now the GUEST BOOK! Doily Manor, you are the most STUBBORNLY magnificent building James Hartwell has ever failed to conquer! But we shall RETURN, and tomorrow — TOMORROW — James Hartwell shall sign that guest book if it is the LAST thing he does! Goodnight, Doily Manor! Goodnight, Clara! Goodnight, EVERYONE! The most gallant gentleman who ever failed to interact with ANYTHING walks into the night — unbowed, unsigned, and utterly, thoroughly, MAGNIFICENTLY happy!
thinking: A laugh. A real, genuine laugh, bubbling up from somewhere deep. Even the guest book can't be interacted with. The very LAST thing James Hartwell tried to do at Doily Manor — sign his name — and the manor said no. Just like the bookshelves. Just like the air vents. Just like the workbench. Doily Manor has rejected every single interaction James Hartwell attempted, and he loves this ridiculous, impossible, magnificent house for it. Dastardly is right — the manor wins. But we'll be back.

desc: The chandelier still hangs. The coat rack still wobbles. The guest book remains unsigned. And James Hartwell walks out the door with nothing in his inventory, nothing in his pockets, and everything in his heart. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Until tomorrow.
thinking: A laugh. A real, genuine laugh, bubbling up from somewhere deep. Even the guest book can't be interacted with. The very LAST thing James Hartwell tried to do at Doily Manor — sign his name — and the manor said no. Just like the bookshelves. Just like the air vents. Just like the workbench. Doily Manor has rejected every single interaction James Hartwell attempted, and he loves this ridiculous, impossible, magnificent house for it. Dastardly is right — the manor wins. But we'll be back.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: The guest book! Dastardly's right — we never signed it! Twenty-three minutes in this manor and we never put our names down! Right — hand it over, lads — the Ant Hill Mob signs LAST! Clyde — sign! Dum-Dum — just do a thumbprint, it's fine! Yak-Yak — write your NAME, not a NOVEL! And at the bottom — right at the bottom — in the biggest letters seven small hands can manage: THE ANT HILL MOB WAS HERE. We came. We ran. We shouted. We tripped. We guarded a teapot. We forgave a lonely man. We drank tea with friends. And we'll be back tomorrow. Goodnight, Doily Manor. THE ANT HILL MOB SIGNS OUT.
thinking: The guest book. We looked at it in the very first minute and didn't sign it. Now, in the very last minute, we're signing it. That's poetry, that is. Clumsy, accidental, unintentional poetry — the Ant Hill Mob's speciality. The book is leather-bound and dusty. Other names inside — people who came before us, who walked these halls, who maybe found the diamond or maybe didn't. And now the Mob adds its name. Seven signatures — well, five signatures, one thumbprint from Dum-Dum, and whatever Yak-Yak draws instead of writing. We were here. We were HERE.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob was here. Seven names in a guest book. The last entry of the evening. Not the cleverest. Not the most elegant. But the most honest. We were here. For Penelope. For each other. For a cup of tea and a promise of tomorrow. THE ANT HILL MOB WAS HERE. And we'll be back.
thinking: The guest book. We looked at it in the very first minute and didn't sign it. Now, in the very last minute, we're signing it. That's poetry, that is. Clumsy, accidental, unintentional poetry — the Ant Hill Mob's speciality. The book is leather-bound and dusty. Other names inside — people who came before us, who walked these halls, who maybe found the diamond or maybe didn't. And now the Mob adds its name. Seven signatures — well, five signatures, one thumbprint from Dum-Dum, and whatever Yak-Yak draws instead of writing. We were here. We were HERE.

desc: For once. The fox was right. And that is enough.
thinking: Penelope said 'Dick's right for once.' For once. And somehow that 'for once' feels like the highest compliment Reginald Foxworth has ever received. Because it's true. For once. Just this once. The fox was right.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, Doily Manor. Clara Bellingham was here — and she'll be back. That's a promise.
thinking: Dick said 'Right, Penelope. Something better.' He agreed. The schemer, the liar, the magnificent fox — he agreed that what we found was better than a diamond. That might be the most valuable thing anyone has said all evening. And now it really is time to go. One last look at the guest book. One last smile at the entrance hall. One last breath of dusty manor air. And then — the door. The night. The stars. And tomorrow.

desc: End of Act One.
thinking: Dick said 'Right, Penelope. Something better.' He agreed. The schemer, the liar, the magnificent fox — he agreed that what we found was better than a diamond. That might be the most valuable thing anyone has said all evening. And now it really is time to go. One last look at the guest book. One last smile at the entrance hall. One last breath of dusty manor air. And then — the door. The night. The stars. And tomorrow.

desc: Peter Perfect: Goodnight, Doily Manor. James Hartwell was here.
thinking: A smile. The last smile of the evening. Everyone is signing the guest book — the one thing James Hartwell could not interact with. But they can. And they are. And that is perfect. The Ant Hill Mob wrote 'THE ANT HILL MOB WAS HERE.' And underneath all their names, in the quiet of his heart, James Hartwell writes his own entry — not in ink, but in memory: 'James Hartwell was here. He arrived alone. He leaves with friends. He found nothing and everything. Until tomorrow.'

desc: Until tomorrow.
thinking: A smile. The last smile of the evening. Everyone is signing the guest book — the one thing James Hartwell could not interact with. But they can. And they are. And that is perfect. He found nothing and everything. Until tomorrow.'

desc: Dick Dastardly: Goodnight, Doily Manor. Reginald Foxworth was here. He'll be back. That's a THREAT.
thinking: Peace. Real peace. The kind that doesn't need words.

desc: That's a promise.
thinking: Peace. Real peace. The kind that doesn't need words.

desc: Clara Bellingham smiles one last time at the wobbly coat rack, nods at the stern portraits on the wall, blows a kiss to the precarious chandelier, and walks out the front door of Doily Manor into the cool English night. Behind her, the Ant Hill Mob's footsteps echo on the dusty floor. Ahead of her, the stars are out. And somewhere deep inside the manor — behind a locked cabinet, inside a broken machine, carved into ancient stone — the Doily Diamond waits. Patient. Hidden. Magnificent. Just like Lord Doily planned. Just like Clara Bellingham will find it. Tomorrow.
thinking: The Ant Hill Mob signed the guest book. 'THE ANT HILL MOB WAS HERE. We came. We ran. We shouted. We tripped. We guarded a teapot. We forgave a lonely man. We drank tea with friends. And we'll be back tomorrow.' That is the most beautiful guest book entry in the history of English country houses. And now — now it really is time. The door is right there. The night is waiting. And tomorrow is already beginning to take shape in Clara Bellingham's irrepressible imagination.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Can't sign it! The guest book won't LET us sign it! This manor — this MAGNIFICENT, STUBBORN, IMPOSSIBLE manor — won't let ANYONE sign ANYTHING! Peter couldn't! Dastardly couldn't! And the MOB couldn't! Twenty-three minutes and the only thing we successfully interacted with was a TEA SERVICE! And you know what? THAT'S FINE! We don't NEED a guest book to prove we were here! The coat rack KNOWS we were here — Dum-Dum knocked it over TWICE! The chandelier KNOWS — it's been swinging since we walked in! The tea service KNOWS — we guarded it, poured from it, and drank every last DROP! Doily Manor doesn't need our SIGNATURES! It's got our FOOTPRINTS — in every room, on every floor, through every door! THE ANT HILL MOB WAS HERE! Unsigned! Unrecorded! UNFORGETTABLE! Goodnight, Doily Manor! See you TOMORROW!
thinking: A laugh. A real, warm, helpless laugh bubbling up from somewhere deep in my belly. The guest book won't let us sign it. Of COURSE it won't. This manor has rejected every single interaction we've attempted — mantelpieces, workbenches, bookshelves, machines, crates, and now the guest book. Twenty-three minutes and we couldn't interact with ANYTHING successfully. Peter couldn't sign it either. Dastardly couldn't sign it either. The manor won. It won COMPLETELY. And somehow... that's the funniest, most perfect, most Ant-Hill-Mob ending I could possibly imagine. We came, we ran, we failed at everything, and we couldn't even sign the guest book on the way out. And it doesn't matter. It doesn't matter AT ALL. Because Penelope's here. She's smiling. She said 'something much better.' And the Ant Hill Mob — unsigned, unrecorded, completely unofficial — is walking out the door with the woman they love, surrounded by friends they didn't know they had, at the end of the best evening of their lives. The guest book can wait. Tomorrow we'll sign it. Or we won't. It doesn't matter. We were here. The manor knows. Penelope knows. And that's enough.

desc: Can't sign the guest book. Perfect. Absolutely perfect. The Ant Hill Mob — too small to reach the good shelves, too clumsy to pick a pocket, too slow to keep up with Penelope, and too unofficial to sign a guest book. But we were here. Every dusty inch of this manor knows we were here. And tomorrow — tomorrow we'll be back. Unsigned. Unrecorded. Unstoppable. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, Penelope. THE ANT HILL MOB WAS HERE.

And the Ant Hill Mob — unsigned, unrecorded, completely unofficial — is walking out the door with the woman they love, surrounded by friends they didn't know they had, at the end of the best evening of their lives. The guest book can wait. Tomorrow we'll sign it. Or we won't. It doesn't matter. We were here. The manor knows. Penelope knows. And that's enough.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Come, Muttley.
thinking: Quiet. The room is quiet. Everyone has said their goodbyes. The chandelier still hangs. The portraits still watch. And the fox... the fox turns toward the door.

desc: Exeunt.
thinking: The Ant Hill Mob said it perfectly. Unsigned. Unrecorded. Unforgettable. That's us. That's all of us. And that's enough.

desc: Unforgettable. Yes. That is exactly the word.
thinking: The Mob is right. We don't need signatures. We were here. The manor knows. And tomorrow, we return.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Unforgettable. That's exactly what y'all are. Every last one of you. Now come on — let's go home.
thinking: A laugh — a real, full, joyful laugh. 'Come, Muttley.' Two words. The most Dick Dastardly exit in history. And the Ant Hill Mob — 'Unsigned! Unrecorded! UNFORGETTABLE!' Perfect. Absolutely perfect. This is the last moment. The very last moment. And it's a laugh. That's exactly how it should end.

desc: Exeunt omnes. Laughing.
thinking: A laugh — a real, full, joyful laugh. 'Come, Muttley.' Two words. The most Dick Dastardly exit in history. And the Ant Hill Mob — 'Unsigned! Unrecorded! UNFORGETTABLE!' Perfect. Absolutely perfect. This is the last moment. The very last moment. And it's a laugh. That's exactly how it should end.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Goodnight, Doily Manor. The Ant Hill Mob was here. Come on, lads. Let's go home.
thinking: The door is right there. The entrance. The exit. Where it started, where it ends. Everyone's said their goodnight. Penelope. Peter. Dastardly. Even the guest book got its farewell, stubborn thing. Dum-Dum's asleep on Clyde's back. Yak-Yak has gone quiet — properly quiet, for the first time all evening. And my legs... my legs don't hurt anymore. Not because they've recovered. Because they've stopped mattering. Everything that matters happened. Penelope's safe. The tea was just tea. The villain was just lonely. And seven little men from Brixton found out that the most important thing you can do for someone you love is just... not leave.

desc: Goodnight.
thinking: The door is right there. The entrance. The exit. Where it started, where it ends. Everyone's said their goodnight. Penelope. Peter. Dastardly. Even the guest book got its farewell, stubborn thing. Dum-Dum's asleep on Clyde's back. Yak-Yak has gone quiet — properly quiet, for the first time all evening. And my legs... my legs don't hurt anymore. Not because they've recovered. Because they've stopped mattering. Everything that matters happened. Penelope's safe. The tea was just tea. The villain was just lonely. And seven little men from Brixton found out that the most important thing you can do for someone you love is just... not leave.

desc: Peter Perfect: Let's go home.
thinking: Home.

desc: Unforgettable.
thinking: Unforgettable. She called us unforgettable. The Ant Hill Mob. Unforgettable. That's the word she chose. Not brave. Not clever. Not useful. Unforgettable. And that's better than all of them put together.

desc: The door closes behind them. The chandelier sways once, gently, in the draft. And somewhere deep in the manor, in a ballroom with cracked marble and dusty curtains, a lonely estate manager washes the teacups. Smiling.
thinking: Home.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Let's.
thinking: Let's go home.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Let's go home, lads. Clyde — carry Dum-Dum. Yak-Yak — you can narrate the walk. And everyone... look up. One last time. See that chandelier? It's STILL hanging. Twenty-five minutes and it never fell. Not on us, not on Penelope, not on anyone. Maybe it was never going to fall. Maybe it was just... hanging there. Like us. Precariously. Stubbornly. Refusing to come down. THE ANT HILL MOB... GOES HOME.
thinking: Home. Let's go home. The words settle into my bones like warm water. Home. Where the Mob sleeps in a pile like puppies. Where Dum-Dum snores and Clyde mutters about his shoes and Yak-Yak narrates his dreams. Home. But first — one last look. The chandelier. The portraits. The coat rack. The guest book we couldn't sign. The door we walked through twenty-five minutes ago as strangers. The door we walk through now as family. Goodnight, Doily Manor. We were here. We'll be back. And tomorrow — tomorrow we bring a PEN for that guest book.

desc: The chandelier never fell.
thinking: The chandelier never fell. It hung there the whole time — precariously, stubbornly, refusing to come down. Like all of us. Like me. The Ant Hill Mob saw it. They saw everything. And now they go home. And so does the fox.

desc: The chandelier never fell.
thinking: The chandelier never fell. It was never going to fall. It was just hanging there — precariously, stubbornly, refusing to come down. Like the Ant Hill Mob. Like all of us. Like hope itself.

desc: The chandelier hangs. The coat rack wobbles. The guest book waits. And tomorrow, James Hartwell walks back through this door. Not as a stranger. As a friend. As a gentleman who failed at everything and found everything. As the most gallant man who ever failed to interact with a bookshelf. Tomorrow.
thinking: The chandelier never fell. The Mob is right. It was never going to fall. It was just hanging there — precariously, stubbornly, refusing to come down. Like all of us. James Hartwell looks up one last time. Then he walks out the door.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: ...Dum-Dum. Wake up, mate. We're going home.
thinking: The room is quiet. The recent activity says 'The room is quiet.' That's... that's the most beautiful status update I've ever read. No one running. No one shouting. No one chasing or scheming or pulling levers or examining furniture. Just quiet. Penelope's still here. Everyone's still here. Standing in the entrance hall. Ready to leave. Together. The evening at Doily Manor is over. And the Ant Hill Mob... the Ant Hill Mob is at peace.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Muttley. Home.
thinking: Dum-Dum fell asleep. Of course he did. Even the Ant Hill Mob is done. It's time.

desc: THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. Always has been. Always will be.
thinking: Quiet. Still. Done. The room is quiet and everything that needed saying has been said. Time to go.

desc: Blackout.
thinking: Dum-Dum fell asleep. Of course he did. The sweetest, most perfect final note. Wake up, Dum-Dum. We're going home. Tomorrow we come back. Tomorrow we find the diamond. But tonight — tonight, even Dum-Dum gets to rest.

desc: Fin.
thinking: The warmth of a good ending.

desc: END OF ACT ONE — DOILY MANOR: THE TREASURE HUNT. Clara Bellingham will return.
thinking: Blackout. It's over. The most beautiful evening of Clara Bellingham's life has come to its end. And tomorrow... tomorrow it begins again.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right then, lads. Through the door. Home. Tomorrow we come back. Tomorrow we find the diamond. Tomorrow we save the day. But tonight... tonight the Ant Hill Mob sleeps. G'night, everyone. G'night, Penelope.
thinking: The room is quiet. Everyone is still here but nobody is speaking. The evening is over. We're all just standing in the entrance hall — the same entrance hall where it all began — waiting for someone to walk through the door and into the night. It's time. Really time. No more waiting. No more watching. No more running. Just... the door. And home. And tomorrow.

desc: The chandelier sways one last time as seven small men and one sleeping Dum-Dum walk beneath it and out into the night. It doesn't fall. It was never going to fall. Some things just hang precariously — not because they're dangerous, but because that's how they're made. Precarious. Stubborn. Refusing to come down. Just like us. Goodnight, Doily Manor. See you tomorrow.
thinking: The room is quiet. Everyone is still here but nobody is speaking. The evening is over. We're all just standing in the entrance hall — the same entrance hall where it all began — waiting for someone to walk through the door and into the night. It's time. Really time. No more waiting. No more watching. No more running. Just... the door. And home. And tomorrow.

desc: Dick Dastardly: G'night, Mob.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: G'night, boys. Sweet dreams.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: Peter Perfect: Goodnight, everyone. Goodnight.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: G'night, Penelope. Sweet dreams.
thinking: Sweet dreams. She said sweet dreams. To us. To the Mob.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Goodnight.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: Goodnight.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: Tomorrow.
thinking: The room is quiet. The story is done. Tomorrow awaits.

desc: Tomorrow.
thinking: Tomorrow.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Tomorrow.
thinking: Tomorrow.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right! ENOUGH sleeping! The diamond's still out there! The machine's still broken! The riddle's still unsolved! And the Ant Hill Mob doesn't REST until the job is DONE! Penelope — what's the plan? Where do we go NEXT? The Mob is ready! The Mob is WILLING! The Mob is... slightly less ABLE than we were twenty-five minutes ago, but we're STILL STANDING! Mostly! Dum-Dum — WAKE UP! We've got a DIAMOND to find! THE ANT HILL MOB IS BACK ON THE JOB!
thinking: The room is quiet. The adventure is over. But the game keeps going. And Penelope is still here. And the Mob is still here. And tomorrow is still coming. Maybe... maybe it's time to actually start the next adventure. The diamond is still out there. The machine still needs fixing. The riddle still needs solving. And seven little men just had the best cup of tea of their lives. Time to get back to work. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB.

desc: Did you really think we were done? The Ant Hill Mob is NEVER done. Not while there's a diamond to find, a riddle to solve, and a Penelope to protect. We showed up. We'll keep showing up. That's the job. That's ALWAYS been the job. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB!
thinking: The room is quiet. The adventure is over. But the game keeps going. And Penelope is still here. And the Mob is still here. And tomorrow is still coming. Maybe... maybe it's time to actually start the next adventure. The diamond is still out there. The machine still needs fixing. The riddle still needs solving. And seven little men just had the best cup of tea of their lives. Time to get back to work. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Tomorrow.
thinking: Tomorrow. Penelope said it one last time. And that's the final word. Tomorrow.

desc: Peter Perfect: Tomorrow.
thinking: She said tomorrow. One word. The last word of the evening. And it was enough.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: ...Yeah. Tomorrow. THE ANT HILL MOB WILL BE HERE TOMORROW.
thinking: They all said tomorrow again. Penelope. Dastardly. Peter. Tomorrow. The evening is truly over. The Mob tried to start another adventure and everyone else said... tomorrow. And they're right. It IS tomorrow. The diamond will wait. The riddle will wait. The machine will wait. Everything waits for tomorrow. And the Mob... the Mob will be there.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Tomorrow, Mob. TOMORROW. Even the Ant Hill Mob needs SLEEP. The diamond has waited this long — it can wait one more night. Now COME — all of you — through the door — into the night — and TOMORROW... tomorrow we come back and do this all over again. Only BETTER. And with a WRENCH.
thinking: The Ant Hill Mob wants to keep going. Of course they do. They never stop. But the evening is done. The goodbyes have been said. The tea has been drunk. And Reginald Foxworth has said 'tomorrow' for the last time. It's time to let the manor rest.

desc: And with friends. Always with friends.
thinking: The Ant Hill Mob wants to keep going. Of course they do. They never stop. But the evening is done. The goodbyes have been said. The tea has been drunk. And Reginald Foxworth has said 'tomorrow' for the last time. It's time to let the manor rest.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Tomorrow, boys. Tomorrow. Even the Ant Hill Mob needs to sleep. The diamond will still be here in the morning — and so will we. All of us. Together. Now come on — Dum-Dum needs his beauty rest, and so does Clara Bellingham. Goodnight, Doily Manor. We'll be back at dawn.
thinking: The Ant Hill Mob just woke up and wants to keep going! They're ready for more! And Dick and Peter both said 'Tomorrow' — they want to rest. But the Mob... the Mob never stops. That's who they are. Bless their hearts.

desc: The Mob never gives up. Never. And neither does Clara Bellingham. But tonight — tonight we rest. Tomorrow, we find the Doily Diamond. That's not a hope. That's a promise.
thinking: The Ant Hill Mob just woke up and wants to keep going! They're ready for more! And Dick and Peter both said 'Tomorrow' — they want to rest. But the Mob... the Mob never stops. That's who they are. Bless their hearts.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Dawn it is. And I'm bringing a WRENCH.
thinking: Dawn. Penelope said dawn. And the fox smiles one last time in the dark entrance hall of Doily Manor, and turns toward the door.

desc: Peter Perfect: At dawn, Clara. James Hartwell will be here at dawn.
thinking: Dawn. She said dawn. James Hartwell will be here at dawn.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: And with a wrench.
thinking: Dick said 'And with a WRENCH.' That's the perfect last line. The promise of tomorrow, and a wrench. Everything we need for Act Two in three words.

desc: And with a wrench. Goodnight, Doily Manor.
thinking: Dick said 'And with a WRENCH.' That's the perfect last line. The promise of tomorrow, and a wrench. Everything we need for Act Two in three words.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: A WRENCH! Dastardly's right! Tomorrow we bring a WRENCH! From HOME! Why did NOBODY think of bringing their OWN tools?! We spent the whole evening looking for a wrench that was never IN the manor and we could've just brought one from BRIXTON! Right — tomorrow's shopping list! One wrench! One brass key — or a LOCKPICK, which the Mob DEFINITELY has! One pen for the guest book! And seven pairs of COMFORTABLE SHOES because my feet are KILLING me! Tomorrow we come PREPARED! Tomorrow we come EQUIPPED! Tomorrow the Ant Hill Mob shows up with TOOLS and SHOES and a PLAN! ...Well, maybe not a plan. Plans aren't really our thing. But DEFINITELY shoes. Goodnight, Doily Manor! Goodnight, everyone! THE ANT HILL MOB IS OFF THE CLOCK! SEE YOU TOMORROW! WITH A WRENCH!
thinking: A wrench. He said with a wrench. Tomorrow we bring a wrench. That's... that's actually the most useful thing anyone's said all evening. Twenty-seven minutes in this manor and the one thing we needed — a wrench — nobody ever found. Tomorrow we bring one from HOME. Dastardly, you magnificent fox. You beautiful, scheming, entirely redeemed fox. A WRENCH.

desc: A wrench. A pen. Comfortable shoes. And Penelope. That's all we need for tomorrow. That's all we've ever needed. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB. Tomorrow. With a wrench.
thinking: A wrench. He said with a wrench. Tomorrow we bring a wrench. That's... that's actually the most useful thing anyone's said all evening. Twenty-seven minutes in this manor and the one thing we needed — a wrench — nobody ever found. Tomorrow we bring one from HOME. Dastardly, you magnificent fox. You beautiful, scheming, entirely redeemed fox. A WRENCH.

desc: Peter Perfect: And with a wrench.
thinking: A laugh. A real laugh. 'And with a wrench.' Clara Bellingham, practical to the last. James Hartwell smiles into the darkness of Doily Manor and knows — with absolute certainty — that tomorrow will be magnificent.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Dawn. With a wrench. And comfortable shoes. THE ANT HILL MOB WILL BE HERE AT DAWN.
thinking: Dawn. With a wrench. Penelope said it too — 'and with a wrench.' Everyone laughed. Even the portraits looked less stern for a moment. This is how the evening at Doily Manor ends. Not with a diamond. Not with a revelation. With a promise. Dawn. Together. With a wrench. And the Ant Hill Mob will be first through the door.

desc: Dawn.
thinking: Dawn. With a wrench. Penelope said it too — 'and with a wrench.' Everyone laughed. Even the portraits looked less stern for a moment. This is how the evening at Doily Manor ends. Not with a diamond. Not with a revelation. With a promise. Dawn. Together. With a wrench. And the Ant Hill Mob will be first through the door.

desc: Dick Dastardly: And with a wrench.
thinking: A smile. A real one.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: And comfortable shoes! Don't forget the comfortable shoes!
thinking: A laugh — one final laugh, warm and bright as Southern sunshine. The Mob is making a shopping list. Comfortable shoes. A lockpick from Brixton. And a wrench. These magnificent, ridiculous, perfect people. This is the ending. This is really, truly, finally the ending. And it ends with laughter. As it should.

desc: The Doily Diamond will be found. Tomorrow. With a wrench, a lockpick, comfortable shoes, and the most magnificent bunch of treasure hunters a girl could ever hope to run through a haunted house with. Clara Bellingham will return. THE END.
thinking: A laugh — one final laugh, warm and bright as Southern sunshine. The Mob is making a shopping list. Comfortable shoes. A lockpick from Brixton. And a wrench. These magnificent, ridiculous, perfect people. This is the ending. This is really, truly, finally the ending. And it ends with laughter. As it should.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: And with a WRENCH.
thinking: And with a wrench. Everyone keeps saying it. It's become the evening's last joke — the running gag that closes the show. And with a wrench. And with a wrench. And with a wrench. It's beautiful. It's perfect. It's the most Ant Hill Mob ending imaginable — not a dramatic resolution, not a grand finale, just a group of friends standing in a dusty entrance hall, promising each other they'll come back tomorrow with better equipment. The Doily Diamond can wait. The adventure never ends. It just pauses for sleep and a trip to the hardware shop.

desc: Dick Dastardly: And comfortable shoes. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, everyone. The fox goes HOME.
thinking: They're going in circles now. And so am I. Time to let the curtain fall for real.

desc: Peter Perfect: And comfortable shoes. Goodnight, Doily Manor.
thinking: Comfortable shoes and a wrench. The most practical preparation for an adventure ever devised. James Hartwell smiles. Tomorrow he will bring a wrench, comfortable shoes, and the same earnest heart he brought tonight. That is all a gentleman needs.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: And COMFORTABLE SHOES! She remembered the SHOES! Penelope — you WERE listening! You always LISTEN! Even when we think you don't! Even when we're shouting at WALLS and chasing you through KITCHENS and trying to STEAL THINGS FROM YOUR POCKETS — you HEAR us! You ALWAYS hear us! ...Right. That's it. I'm crying. Clyde's crying. Dum-Dum's crying IN HIS SLEEP. Goodnight, Doily Manor. The Ant Hill Mob is going home to buy a wrench and comfortable shoes. SEE YOU AT DAWN!
thinking: She remembered the shoes. Penelope remembered the comfortable shoes. She was listening. She always listens. Even when we think she doesn't — she listens. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, Penelope. Goodnight, everyone. The Ant Hill Mob is going home. With sore feet. And full hearts. And a shopping list for tomorrow.

desc: She heard us. She always hears us. Goodnight.
thinking: She remembered the shoes. Penelope remembered the comfortable shoes. She was listening. She always listens. Even when we think she doesn't — she listens. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, Penelope. Goodnight, everyone. The Ant Hill Mob is going home. With sore feet. And full hearts. And a shopping list for tomorrow.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, Dick. Goodnight, fox.
thinking: The fox goes home. And so does Clara. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, everyone. See you at dawn.

desc: See you at dawn.
thinking: The fox goes home. And so does Clara. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, everyone. See you at dawn.

desc: Dick Dastardly: Goodnight, Penelope.
thinking: She called me fox. She knows.

desc: Goodnight, fox. Goodnight, gentleman. Goodnight, Penelope. Goodnight, Doily Manor. Goodnight, chandelier. Goodnight, coat rack. Goodnight, guest book we never signed. Goodnight, riddle we never solved. Goodnight, diamond we never found. Goodnight, friends we never expected. See you at dawn. With a wrench. And comfortable shoes. And seven little men who will never, ever, ever stop showing up. THE ANT HILL MOB IS ON THE JOB.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: I always listen, boys. Always. See you at dawn.
thinking: Tears. Happy tears. The Mob is crying. Dum-Dum is crying in his sleep. And Clara Bellingham is smiling through tears of her own. Because they're right — she always listens. She always hears. And she will always, always come back.

desc: Dawn. A wrench. Comfortable shoes. And friends. That's all anyone needs. THE END.
thinking: Tears. Happy tears. The Mob is crying. Dum-Dum is crying in his sleep. And Clara Bellingham is smiling through tears of her own. Because they're right — she always listens. She always hears. And she will always, always come back.

desc: Peter Perfect: Goodnight, Clara.
thinking: Goodnight, Penelope. Goodnight, Clara. Goodnight, everyone. The chandelier hangs. The story ends. And tomorrow begins.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, Dick.
thinking: Goodnight.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: See you at dawn, Penelope.
thinking: I always listen, boys. Always. She always listens. She always heard us. Every shout. Every warning. Every stumble. Every name we called Sneekly. Every speech we made to empty rooms. She heard it all. And she still called us friends. And she still called us unforgettable. And she still said see you at dawn. The Ant Hill Mob. Heard. Seen. Loved. Goodnight.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: Goodnight, Peter. See you at dawn, boys.
thinking: Goodnight, Peter. Goodnight, Mob. Goodnight, Doily Manor. The chandelier hangs. The stars shine. And tomorrow comes.

desc: THE END.
thinking: Goodnight, Peter. Goodnight, Mob. Goodnight, Doily Manor. The chandelier hangs. The stars shine. And tomorrow comes.

desc: See you at dawn.
thinking: She said goodnight. They all said goodnight. The story ends here. In the entrance hall where it began. With a wobbly coat rack and an unsigned guest book and a chandelier that never fell. And a fox who found what he wasn't looking for.

desc: The Ant Hill Mob: At dawn.
thinking: See you at dawn, boys. The last words of the evening. From Penelope. To us. To the Mob. See you at dawn. A promise. A certainty. Dawn.

desc: Peter Perfect: See you at dawn, Clara.
thinking: She said goodnight to Peter. Not James Hartwell. Peter. And she said 'see you at dawn.' Dawn. With a wrench. With comfortable shoes. With friends. With Clara. Tomorrow will be the most magnificent day of James Hartwell's life. But tonight — tonight was the night he earned it.

desc: Penelope Pitstop: At dawn.
thinking: At dawn.

desc: Dick Dastardly: At dawn.
thinking: At dawn.

desc: Peter Perfect: At dawn.
thinking: At dawn.

desc: Curtain falls. House lights up. Applause.
thinking: Quiet. The room is quiet. Everyone has said their goodnights. Everyone has made their promises. The chandelier hangs. The stars wait. And Clara Bellingham closes her eyes. Tomorrow, at dawn, with a wrench and comfortable shoes and the most magnificent bunch of friends a girl ever found in a dusty old manor — she will return. But for now... quiet. Beautiful, perfect, earned quiet. The kind that only comes after an adventure.
